tickets.title: Spike: confirm Langfuse Cloud accepts SDK 5.x with masking
tickets.summary: Prove that Langfuse Python SDK 5.x exports traces to Langfuse Cloud with masked and capture-off spans, and record the exact parameter names the wrapper must use.
tickets.description:
Why: ADR-018 chooses Langfuse Cloud Hobby with Python SDK 5.x (5.1.0 current) behind one wrapper, using `@observe` with `capture_input` / `capture_output` off on sensitive spans and `mask_otel_spans` for export masking. The MVP pins langfuse 4.6.1 and calls v2 methods that do not exist (G-15). plan.md E0: "confirm Langfuse Cloud accepts SDK 5.x as the first ticket". The wrapper ticket E0-T8 must not start until this passes.

Build:
- Bump `langfuse` in `backend/pyproject.toml` to the 5.x line (5.1.0 or newer 5.x) and re-lock (`poetry lock`), keeping every other locked version unchanged where possible. Do not touch `backend/src/observability/tracing.py` or its mocked tests (E0-T8 replaces them).
- Add `backend/scripts/spike_langfuse_v5.py`. It reads `LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY`, `LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY`, `LANGFUSE_HOST` from the environment (Settings does not exist in its final form yet), creates one trace with (a) a normal span whose input contains the marker `SPIKE-SSN-123-45-6789` and which is exported through SDK-level masking (`mask_otel_spans`, confirm the exact name and signature against the SDK 5.1.0 docs via Context7 or langfuse.com/docs) that replaces the marker with `[REDACTED]`, and (b) a sensitive span created with `capture_input=False, capture_output=False` and non-empty input/output. It flushes, then polls the Langfuse public API (`GET {host}/api/public/traces/{id}`, basic auth with the key pair) for up to 60 s.
- The script exits 0 only if: the trace is retrievable; no observation input/output contains `SPIKE-SSN`; the sensitive span has no input and no output. Otherwise it prints the reason and exits 1. A transport or auth error exits non-zero.
- Write `docs/spikes/langfuse-sdk5.md`: verdict (pass/fail), SDK version, the exact masking and capture-off parameter names that worked, host/region used, and any limitation found (for example if the legacy `mask=` does not cover OTel spans, which ADR-018 says it does not).

Out of scope: the production wrapper, orchestrator changes, Settings keys (E0-T3 and E0-T8). Needs a Langfuse Cloud Hobby project with a key pair supplied by Keshav (see questions).
acceptance_criteria: `cd backend && poetry lock --check` exits 0 and `poetry run python -c "import langfuse, importlib.metadata as m; print(m.version('langfuse'))"` prints a version starting with `5.`.

Given a valid Langfuse Cloud key pair in the environment, when `poetry run python scripts/spike_langfuse_v5.py` runs, then it exits 0 and prints the trace id it fetched from `/api/public/traces/{id}`.
Given the same run with `LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY` set to a wrong value, when the script runs, then it exits non-zero (the check can fail).

The script exits 1 if any fetched observation input or output contains the string `SPIKE-SSN`, and exits 1 if the sensitive span has a non-empty input or output (demonstrated by running once with masking disabled via a `--no-mask` flag and seeing exit 1).
`docs/spikes/langfuse-sdk5.md` exists and contains a `Verdict:` line with `pass` or `fail`, the installed SDK version, and the exact masking and capture-off parameter names.

tickets.title: Build the backend image from poetry.lock with dev and runtime stages
tickets.summary: The backend image installs only what `backend/poetry.lock` pins, has a real `dev` stage, and the build fails when the lock is stale.
tickets.description:
Why: G-28: `backend/Dockerfile:6-8` runs `pip install -e "."` from `>=` floors and ignores `poetry.lock`, so rebuilds change major versions. G-49: `docker-compose.override.yml` targets a `dev` stage that does not exist. ADR-021: lockfile installs only, images referenced by digest. ADR-019: one Python image (entrypoints are added in E0-T9).

Build `backend/Dockerfile` as a multi-stage build:
- `base`: `python:3.12-slim` referenced by `@sha256:` digest (resolve the current digest and add a comment with the tag).
- `builder`: installs a pinned Poetry version, runs `poetry check --lock` then `poetry install --no-root --only main --no-interaction` into a virtualenv at `/opt/venv` using `backend/poetry.lock`.
- `dev`: adds the `dev` dependency group, runs as non-root, keeps `CMD uvicorn src.main:app --reload --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000` (the override file mounts `src/` and `tests/`).
- `runtime` (the last stage, so a plain `docker build` produces it): main group only, source copied, non-root user, `CMD uvicorn src.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000`.
- Add `backend/.dockerignore` excluding `.venv`, `.env`, `__pycache__`, `.pytest_cache`, `.mypy_cache`, `.ruff_cache`.
- Pin the poetry-core build requirement in `backend/pyproject.toml` (`requires = ["poetry-core==<locked version>"]`) so builds do not float.
- Leave `docker-compose.yml` ports/services alone (E0-T11 rewrites it); only make sure `docker-compose.override.yml` `target: dev` now resolves.

Out of scope: the `api | worker | jobs` entrypoint dispatcher (E0-T9), compose rewrite (E0-T11), CI (E0-T13), Trivy image scan (E0-T14).
acceptance_criteria: Given a clean checkout, when `docker build --target runtime -t fa-backend:test backend` runs, then it succeeds, and `docker run --rm fa-backend:test python -c "import fastapi,anthropic,langfuse,importlib.metadata as m; print(m.version('fastapi'), m.version('anthropic'), m.version('langfuse'))"` prints exactly the three versions listed in `backend/poetry.lock`.

Given `backend/pyproject.toml` has a new dependency added without re-locking, when the image is built, then the build fails at `poetry check --lock` (verified once by adding `rich` to pyproject and confirming a non-zero build exit).
`docker build --target dev` succeeds and `docker run --rm <dev-image> pytest --version` exits 0, while `docker run --rm fa-backend:test pytest --version` exits non-zero (no dev tools in runtime).
`docker run --rm fa-backend:test id -u` prints a non-zero uid.
Every `FROM` line in `backend/Dockerfile` contains `@sha256:` (checked by `! grep -E '^FROM' backend/Dockerfile | grep -v '@sha256:'`).

tickets.title: One typed config that fails boot on missing secrets
tickets.summary: A single pydantic-settings `Settings` holds the E0 keys from the config table, has no secret defaults, and the app refuses to start without its required keys.
tickets.description:
Why: G-25: `backend/src/config.py` has code defaults for secrets (`localdev` DB password, `sk-litellm-local`, `local-dev-secret`) and a missing variable falls back silently. §6.6: "One typed `Settings` class (pydantic-settings). No secret has a default; a missing required key fails boot." ADR-006: "Model ids only from config."

Rewrite `backend/src/config.py` (one class, `Settings(BaseSettings)`, env names are the upper-case keys below, secrets as `SecretStr`):
- `ENV_PROFILE` (`dev` | `demo` | `prod`, default `dev`).
- `DB_HOST`, `DB_PORT` (see questions; int, default 5432), `DB_NAME`, `DB_USER`, `DB_PASSWORD` (secret), `DB_POOL_SIZE`, `DB_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS`: no defaults except `DB_PORT`. Provide a `database_dsn` property (`postgresql+asyncpg://...`, URL-encoded password) replacing `database_url`.
- `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (secret, required), `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` (default `https://api.anthropic.com`).
- `LLM_MODEL_ANSWER` (default `claude-sonnet-5-5`), `LLM_MODEL_AUX` and `LLM_MODEL_JUDGE` (default `claude-haiku-5-5`), `LLM_MODEL_FALLBACK` (default `claude-sonnet-4-6`), `LLM_FALLBACK_ENABLED` (default `false`), `LLM_MAX_ITERATIONS` (default 3). A validator rejects `LLM_MODEL_JUDGE == LLM_MODEL_ANSWER` (§6.6: judge must differ from answer). The model-id values are not checked against the retirement table here (E0-T4 does that, and `/readyz` must still be able to boot and report it).
- `VOYAGE_API_KEY` (secret, required).
- `LANGFUSE_ENABLED` (default `false`), `LANGFUSE_HOST`, `LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY`, `LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY`; the three Langfuse values are required only when `LANGFUSE_ENABLED=true`.
- Keys still read by MVP code that E1 replaces: `PII_MODE` (default `regex`), `GCP_PROJECT_ID` (default empty), `JWT_SECRET` (secret, required, no default; E1 deletes it).
- Remove `openai_api_key`, `google_api_key`, `litellm_master_key`, `kong_url`, `llm_base_url`, `database_url`.
Only keys the E0 code consumes are added; later epics add theirs from §6.6.

Update every consumer: `backend/src/main.py` (build the engine from `database_dsn`, never log credentials), `backend/src/db/session.py` (`pool_size=DB_POOL_SIZE`, per-connection `statement_timeout` from `DB_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS`), `backend/src/pii/__init__.py`, `backend/scripts/ingest.py`, `backend/scripts/generate_corpus.py`, `backend/tests` fixtures. Tests get their values from an autouse fixture / `pytest` env setup that sets dummy non-secret-looking values; the code itself holds none. Rewrite `.env.example` with placeholders only (`REPLACE_ME`), listing exactly these keys.

Out of scope: embeddings model keys (E3), Kafka and other keys (their epics), swapping the LLM call sites to the new model keys (E0-T6), role/RLS config (E1).
acceptance_criteria: Given each of `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `VOYAGE_API_KEY`, `DB_PASSWORD`, `JWT_SECRET`, `DB_HOST`, `DB_NAME`, `DB_USER`, `DB_POOL_SIZE`, `DB_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS` removed in turn from an otherwise valid environment, when `Settings()` is built, then it raises `ValidationError` naming that key (parametrized unit test, `backend/tests/test_settings.py`).

Given `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is unset, when `uvicorn src.main:app` is started in a subprocess, then the process exits non-zero within 15 s, stderr names `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, and no secret value from the environment appears in stderr (subprocess test).
Given `LANGFUSE_ENABLED=true` with no Langfuse keys, `Settings()` raises; given `LANGFUSE_ENABLED=false` and no keys, it succeeds.
Given `LLM_MODEL_JUDGE` equal to `LLM_MODEL_ANSWER`, `Settings()` raises `ValidationError`.
`repr(Settings(...))` and `str(Settings(...))` contain none of the secret values, and `grep -rEn "localdev|local-dev-secret|sk-litellm" backend/src backend/scripts .env.example` returns no match.
`ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy src/` and the full existing `pytest` suite pass (97 passed before this ticket).

tickets.title: Add a retired-model check for configured model ids
tickets.summary: A tested function and CLI report any configured model id that is retired, soon retiring or deprecated, so CI and readiness can fail on it.
tickets.description:
Why: ADR-006: `claude-sonnet-4-20250514` retired 2026-06-15 (app and evals fail today); "Model ids only from config; CI and readiness fail on a retired or soon-retiring model." §7 failure modes: "Retired or soon-retiring model id: readiness check, CI check; `/readyz` fails; CI blocks."

Build `backend/src/model_lifecycle.py`:
- A static table of known lifecycle facts from ADR-006: `claude-sonnet-4-20250514` retired 2026-06-15; `claude-sonnet-4-5` retires 2026-11-30; `claude-haiku-4-5` deprecated about 2026-10-15 (retirement date not in the arch; see questions). Each row carries the source URL (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/model-deprecations).
- `check_models(settings, *, today: date) -> list[ModelProblem]` checks `LLM_MODEL_ANSWER`, `LLM_MODEL_AUX`, `LLM_MODEL_JUDGE` and `LLM_MODEL_FALLBACK` (the fallback is checked even while disabled). A problem is: retired (date <= today), soon retiring (within `SOON_RETIRING_DAYS`, one named module constant; value per questions, use 30 until answered) or deprecated. Each problem names the settings key and the model id and the reason code (`retired`, `retiring_soon`, `deprecated`). Ids absent from the table pass (denylist; see questions).
- CLI: `python -m src.model_lifecycle` builds `Settings()` from the environment, prints one line per problem, exits 1 on any problem and 0 otherwise. This is what CI (E0-T13) calls.

Out of scope: the `/readyz` endpoint (E0-T5), calling the Anthropic models API, the fallback eval gate.
acceptance_criteria: Given `LLM_MODEL_ANSWER=claude-sonnet-4-20250514`, `check_models(settings, today=date(2026,11,1))` returns a problem with key `LLM_MODEL_ANSWER` and reason `retired` (unit test).
Given `LLM_MODEL_AUX=claude-sonnet-4-5`, `check_models` returns `retiring_soon` for `today=date(2026,11,1)` and returns no problem for `today=date(2026,9,1)` (unit test with the injected clock).
Given the default models (`claude-sonnet-5-5`, `claude-haiku-5-5`, `claude-sonnet-4-6`), `check_models(..., today=date(2026,11,1))` returns an empty list.
Given `LLM_MODEL_FALLBACK=claude-sonnet-4-20250514` with `LLM_FALLBACK_ENABLED=false`, the check still reports it.
`LLM_MODEL_ANSWER=claude-sonnet-4-20250514 python -m src.model_lifecycle` exits 1 and prints the key name; the same command with default model ids exits 0 (subprocess test).

tickets.title: Add /healthz and /readyz with database and model checks
tickets.summary: The API exposes a liveness probe and a readiness probe that fails when the database is unreachable or a configured model is retired.
tickets.description:
Why: §6.1 and observability: `/healthz` (liveness) and `/readyz` (readiness, including "model availability (configured models not retired or soon-retiring)"). plan.md E0 done-when: "`claude-sonnet-4-20250514` in config makes CI and `/readyz` fail (test)". Docker healthchecks in E0-T11 use `/healthz`.

Build (root paths, not under `/api`; the existing `/api/health` stays until E4 replaces the router):
- `GET /healthz`: 200 `{"status": "ok"}`; touches no dependency.
- `GET /readyz`: runs `SELECT 1` on the app's DB engine with a 2 s timeout and `check_models(settings, today=date.today())` from E0-T4. 200 `{"status":"ready","checks":{"db":"ok","models":"ok"}}` when both pass; otherwise 503 `{"status":"not_ready","checks":{"db":"ok|fail","models":"ok|fail"}}`. Responses carry check names and codes only: no exception text, connection strings, key values (the arch rule that errors carry codes, not exception text). Log the failing key/model at warning level.
- The app must still start with a retired model id configured (so readiness can report it).

Out of scope (later epics add them to `/readyz`): DB role flags and FORCE RLS assertions (E1), pgvector >= 0.8 assertion, Kafka reachability (E5), firebase-admin verifier initialised (E1).
acceptance_criteria: Given the app with a stub DB that answers `SELECT 1` and default models, `GET /readyz` returns 200 and `checks.models == "ok"` (unit test).
Given `LLM_MODEL_ANSWER=claude-sonnet-4-20250514`, `GET /readyz` returns 503 with `checks.models == "fail"`, while `GET /healthz` still returns 200 (unit test).

Given a DB that raises on `SELECT 1`, `GET /readyz` returns 503 with `checks.db == "fail"`, and the response body contains neither the DB host nor the exception message (unit test asserting on `response.text`).
Integration test (`requires_db`): against the real pgvector Postgres, `/readyz` returns 200; with `DB_PORT` pointed at a closed port it returns 503 within 5 s.
mypy strict and ruff pass on the new routes.

tickets.title: Remove LiteLLM and Kong wiring; call Anthropic directly
tickets.summary: No LiteLLM service, config, dependency or doc remains; the backend calls Anthropic at `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` with model ids from Settings.
tickets.description:
Why: ADR-005: drop LiteLLM; its config shuffles Claude, GPT-4o and Gemini under one name (G-08) and its fallback key matches nothing (G-09). plan.md E0: "Remove LiteLLM and the Kong/LiteLLM wiring". The in-process `LLMClient` with same-provider fallback is E4; this ticket only removes the old path and makes the existing code call Anthropic directly. Kong returns in E2 with a new `kong.yml`; the MVP Kong config only fronts LiteLLM and posts to a non-existent audit route, so it goes.

Do:
- Delete `litellm/`, `kong/` (Dockerfile and kong.yml), `backend/tests/test_fallback_chain.py`, `backend/scripts/test_fallback_live.py`.
- `backend/src/main.py`: `anthropic.AsyncAnthropic(api_key=settings.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, base_url=settings.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL)`; remove the `kong_url` / `litellm_master_key` branch. Do not pass `temperature`, `top_p` or `top_k` anywhere (ADR-006: removed from the API, 400).
- Model ids from config at every call site: `backend/src/agent/orchestrator.py` (drop `DEFAULT_MODEL`; `model` becomes a required constructor argument, `backend/src/dependencies.py` passes `settings.LLM_MODEL_ANSWER`), `backend/scripts/run_eval.py` (`JUDGE_MODEL` from `LLM_MODEL_JUDGE`), `backend/scripts/generate_corpus.py` (`LLM_MODEL_AUX`). Update tests that referenced the old string (`tests/test_tracing.py` line 43 is replaced by E0-T8).
- `docker-compose.yml`: delete the `litellm` and `kong` services and the backend env `KONG_URL`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, the `depends_on: kong`. Pass `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` instead. (E0-T11 rewrites the file fully.)
- Update `README.md` (architecture diagram, stack table, directory list, "Fallback Chain" paragraph) and `CLAUDE.md` (routing and stack lines) to say: Anthropic direct, Kong arrives in E2. Update `.env.example` already done in E0-T3, confirm no leftovers.
- Add `scripts/check_no_litellm.sh`: fails if `git grep -il litellm` matches any tracked file outside the allowlist `Story-Reports/`, `TODO.md`, `mvp.md`, `architecture.md`, `docs/threat_model.md`, `scripts/check_no_litellm.sh` itself (historical MVP records; see questions), and fails if `backend/poetry.lock` or `backend/pyproject.toml` contains `litellm`.

Out of scope: Terraform (E0-T7), the LLMClient, fallback, circuit breaker (E4), the Kong egress route (E2).
acceptance_criteria: Given the repo after this change, `bash scripts/check_no_litellm.sh` exits 0; after temporarily adding the word `LiteLLM` to `backend/src/main.py` it exits 1 (verified in the PR description).
`git ls-files litellm kong` prints nothing, and `docker compose config --services` lists no `litellm` or `kong` service.

`grep -rEn "claude-sonnet-4-20250514|DEFAULT_MODEL|JUDGE_MODEL = " backend/src backend/scripts` returns no hard-coded model id, and a unit test asserts `FinAdvisorAgent` sends `model == settings.LLM_MODEL_ANSWER` to the (mocked) Anthropic client.
A unit test asserts the client built in `src.main.lifespan` has `base_url` equal to `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and the API key from `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
`ruff check`, `mypy src/` and `pytest` pass (the two deleted fallback test files are the only removed tests).

tickets.title: Remove LiteLLM and Kong resources from Terraform
tickets.summary: The Terraform files no longer define LiteLLM or the MVP Kong service and validate cleanly.
tickets.description:
Why: plan.md E0 done-when: "the repo contains no LiteLLM service, config or dependency". `terraform/cloud_run.tf` defines `google_cloud_run_v2_service.litellm` (line ~162) and a Kong service that fronts it, `secrets.tf` holds `litellm_master_key`, `variables.tf` has `litellm_image` and `kong_image`, `outputs.tf` exports `litellm_url` and `kong_url`, and the backend service sets `KONG_URL`. The target Terraform (Kong `fa-gateway`, worker pool, jobs) is rebuilt in E2 and E10.

Do in `terraform/`:
- Delete the litellm service, the MVP Kong service (its image is built from the `kong/` directory deleted in E0-T6), the `litellm_master_key` secret and any IAM bindings for them, the OpenAI and Google API key secrets if present, and the variables and outputs that referenced them.
- Backend service env: remove `KONG_URL`; add `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` (variable, default `https://api.anthropic.com`).
- Do not add new infrastructure; do not change anything unrelated.

Out of scope: any target-state Terraform (E2, E10).
acceptance_criteria: `cd terraform && terraform fmt -check -recursive` exits 0.
`cd terraform && terraform init -backend=false && terraform validate` exits 0.
`grep -rniE "litellm|KONG_URL|kong_image|openai|gemini" terraform` returns no match.
The backend Cloud Run service definition contains an `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` env entry (checked by grep in the PR).

tickets.title: Replace Langfuse v2 tracing with an SDK 5.x wrapper
tickets.summary: Tracing uses real Langfuse 5.x calls behind one wrapper with export masking and capture off on sensitive spans, and a tracing failure never fails a chat.
tickets.description:
Why: G-15: `backend/src/observability/tracing.py` calls `trace()/generation()/span()` which do not exist in the installed SDK, so chat fails with Langfuse keys set, and tests pass only because Langfuse is a `MagicMock`. ADR-018: "Langfuse Cloud Hobby with Python SDK 5.x behind one wrapper: `@observe` with `capture_input` / `capture_output` off on sensitive spans and `mask_otel_spans` for export masking (the legacy `mask=` does not cover OTel spans)". Use the exact parameter names recorded in `docs/spikes/langfuse-sdk5.md` from E0-T1.

Do:
- Rewrite `backend/src/observability/tracing.py` as the only module importing `langfuse`: `init_tracing(settings) -> Tracer | None` (returns `None` and creates no client when `LANGFUSE_ENABLED=false`), a span helper/decorator `traced(name, *, sensitive=True, tenant_id=None)` (sensitive spans record no input or output; tenant tag optional until E1), a masking function applied through `mask_otel_spans` that scrubs text with the existing `src/pii` redactor in regex mode, `flush()` and `shutdown()`. Prompt fetch (`get_prompt_from_langfuse`) stays, failing soft to the fallback prompt.
- Every call into the SDK is wrapped so an exception is logged (`tracing_error`, no payload) and swallowed.
- Update `backend/src/agent/orchestrator.py` (one trace per turn, one generation per LLM iteration, one span per tool call; tool inputs/outputs and message content are sensitive, so capture off) and `backend/src/main.py` (init in lifespan, shutdown on exit). Remove all Langfuse v2 method usage.
- Rewrite `backend/tests/test_tracing.py` against the real installed SDK (no `MagicMock` of the Langfuse class) using an in-memory OpenTelemetry span exporter.

Out of scope: tenant tagging values (E1), OTel exporters to Cloud Trace (later epic), eval datasets and scores (E7).
acceptance_criteria: Given the real SDK with an in-memory span exporter, when a `traced("x", sensitive=True)` span runs with input containing `ssn 123-45-6789` and output text, then the exported span has no input attribute and no output attribute.
Given a non-sensitive span whose input contains `jane@example.com`, the exported span attributes do not contain that string (the masking function ran) (unit test).
Given `LANGFUSE_ENABLED=false`, `init_tracing` returns `None`, no `Langfuse` object is constructed and the agent still completes a mocked turn (unit test).
Given an exporter or client that raises on every call, a mocked agent turn still yields its normal events and the failure is only logged (unit test); this is the regression for G-15.

A test builds `unittest.mock.create_autospec(langfuse.Langfuse, instance=True)` and runs the wrapper against it; it fails if the wrapper calls any method the installed SDK does not have (`trace`, `generation`, `span` as on v2).
`grep -rn "import langfuse\|from langfuse" backend/src` matches only `backend/src/observability/tracing.py`; ruff, mypy and pytest pass.

tickets.title: Alembic baseline from schema.sql and the migrate entrypoint
tickets.summary: `python -m src.entrypoint jobs migrate` upgrades an empty database to a schema identical to `backend/db/schema.sql`, and the image gets its `api` and `jobs` entrypoints.
tickets.description:
Why: G-12: `schema.sql` is never applied by the app and there is no migration tool. plan.md E0: "Alembic baseline created from `schema.sql`; `migrate` entrypoint"; done when "Alembic upgrade on an empty database equals the baseline schema". ADR-019: one image with entrypoints `api | worker | jobs`; §4.8: the `migrate` job runs Alembic upgrade before traffic (in the cloud as `fa_owner`; roles arrive in E1, so locally it runs as the configured `DB_USER`).

Build:
- Add Alembic 1.20 (stack.md) as a main dependency and re-lock.
- `backend/alembic.ini` (no URL inside), `backend/migrations/env.py` (async engine on asyncpg, URL from `Settings().database_dsn`), `backend/migrations/versions/0001_baseline.py` whose `upgrade()` creates exactly the objects in `backend/db/schema.sql` (extensions `vector` and `pgcrypto`, the four tables, indexes, RLS and policy, the guarded role creation) embedded as SQL in the migration so it stays immutable; `downgrade()` drops them. asyncpg runs one statement per execute: split statements or use a sync-style `exec_driver_sql` per statement. Keep `backend/db/schema.sql` untouched as the golden reference for the equality test.
- `backend/src/entrypoint.py`: `python -m src.entrypoint api` starts uvicorn (`0.0.0.0`, port from `PORT`, default 8000, one process); `python -m src.entrypoint jobs migrate` runs `alembic upgrade head`; any other command exits 2 with usage. Set the Dockerfile `ENTRYPOINT ["python","-m","src.entrypoint"]` and `CMD ["api"]` for the runtime stage (the dev stage keeps its reload command).
- Copy `alembic.ini` and `migrations/` into the image.

Out of scope: the target data model, partitioning, roles and RLS v2 (E1 adds further revisions), the `worker` entrypoint (E5; see questions), tenant onboarding flag.
acceptance_criteria: Given an empty Postgres (`pgvector/pgvector:0.8.5-pg16`), when `python -m src.entrypoint jobs migrate` runs, then it exits 0 and `SELECT version_num FROM alembic_version` returns `0001`; a second run exits 0 and changes nothing (integration test).

Given database A built with `psql -f backend/db/schema.sql` and database B built by the migrate entrypoint, `pg_dump --schema-only --no-owner --no-privileges` of both, normalised for the `alembic_version` table, is byte-identical (integration test; fails on any drift).
Given database B at head, `alembic downgrade base` leaves zero tables in `public` other than `alembic_version` (integration test).
Given `DB_PORT` pointing at a closed port, `jobs migrate` exits non-zero within 30 s and the output contains no DB password (subprocess test).
`docker run --rm fa-backend:test bogus` exits 2, and `docker run --rm fa-backend:test jobs migrate` against the compose Postgres exits 0 (checked in the PR).
`poetry check --lock`, ruff and mypy pass with the new files.

tickets.title: Add vitest and a frontend dev image
tickets.summary: The frontend has a working unit-test runner, a type-check script and a dev Dockerfile so CI and compose can use them.
tickets.description:
Why: plan.md E0 CI scope lists eslint, tsc and vitest, and the compose scope lists "a frontend dev image" (G-13: no frontend Dockerfile). ADR-019 moves the product frontend to a Vite SPA in E8; this ticket works on the current Next.js 14 app in `frontend/` and does not migrate it (see questions).

Do in `frontend/`:
- Add `vitest` (pin in `package-lock.json`) with `vitest.config.ts` (node or jsdom environment as needed), scripts `"test": "vitest run"` and `"typecheck": "tsc --noEmit"`; keep `"lint": "next lint"`.
- Add one real test file for the existing pure function `src/lib/parseCitations.ts` (plain text, one citation marker, multiple markers, malformed marker) so the suite asserts behaviour.
- Add `frontend/Dockerfile` with a `dev` target: Node 20 base referenced by `@sha256:` digest, `npm ci` from the lockfile, runs `npm run dev -- -H 0.0.0.0 -p 3000` as a non-root user; and `frontend/.dockerignore` (`node_modules`, `.next`, `.env*`).

Out of scope: Vite migration and any UI change (E8), Playwright, the compose service (E0-T11), CI wiring (E0-T13).
acceptance_criteria: `cd frontend && npm ci && npm test` exits 0 and reports at least 4 passing tests in `parseCitations`; changing the expected value of one assertion makes `npm test` exit non-zero (verified once).
`cd frontend && npm run typecheck` exits 0 on the repo and exits non-zero after introducing `const x: number = "a"` in a source file (verified once).
`cd frontend && npm run lint` exits 0 on the repo.
`docker build --target dev -t fa-frontend:dev frontend` succeeds; `docker run --rm -d -p 13000:3000 fa-frontend:dev` then `curl -fsS localhost:13000/` returns HTTP 200 within 60 s.
The `FROM` line of `frontend/Dockerfile` contains `@sha256:`.

tickets.title: Rewrite docker compose with healthchecks and env-driven host ports
tickets.summary: `docker compose up --wait` brings postgres, kafka, migrate, api and frontend healthy using the pinned pgvector image, with every host port overridable.
tickets.description:
Why: G-49: the override file targets a missing stage, nothing has healthchecks, `kong` waits only for start, host ports are fixed, and a duplicate standalone Langfuse compose conflicts on ports. ADR-019: "Local dev = docker compose with the same image." ADR-021 / stack.md: local and CI Postgres is `pgvector/pgvector:0.8.5-pg16` to match Cloud SQL; local Kafka is `apache/kafka:4.4.0` KRaft single node. G-25: no secret defaults.

Rewrite `docker-compose.yml` (and fix `docker-compose.override.yml`):
- `postgres`: `pgvector/pgvector:0.8.5-pg16`, credentials from `DB_NAME`, `DB_USER`, `DB_PASSWORD` (`${DB_PASSWORD:?set DB_PASSWORD in .env}`), named volume, `pg_isready` healthcheck; remove the `schema.sql` initdb mount (Alembic owns the schema).
- `kafka`: `apache/kafka:4.4.0` single-node KRaft, healthcheck using the bundled `kafka-broker-api-versions.sh`, an in-network listener for containers and a host listener whose advertised port equals `KAFKA_HOST_PORT`.
- `migrate`: same backend image, command `jobs migrate`, `depends_on: postgres: service_healthy`, `restart: "no"`.
- `api`: backend image (override uses the `dev` target with source mounts), `depends_on` migrate `service_completed_successfully`, healthcheck GET `/healthz` using Python's stdlib (slim image has no curl), env from Settings keys (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `VOYAGE_API_KEY`, `JWT_SECRET`, `DB_*`, pool and timeout keys), all secrets required via `${VAR:?...}`.
- `frontend`: `frontend/Dockerfile` dev target from E0-T10, `depends_on: api: service_healthy`, healthcheck on `/`.
- Host ports bound to `127.0.0.1` and env-driven with defaults: `POSTGRES_HOST_PORT`, `KAFKA_HOST_PORT`, `API_HOST_PORT`, `FRONTEND_HOST_PORT`.
- Remove the unused `redis`, the self-hosted `langfuse` and `langfuse-db` services and delete `langfuse/docker-compose.langfuse.yml` (ADR-018 rejected self-hosting; Langfuse Cloud is used when `LANGFUSE_ENABLED=true`; see questions).
- Update `backend/src/cli.py` (`finadvisor` launcher): stop piping `schema.sql` into the removed initdb path; run the `migrate` service and use `docker compose up --wait`. Update `.env.example` with the host-port variables.

Out of scope: Kong, Valkey, Schema Registry and the `worker` service (E2 / E5 add them), Terraform.
acceptance_criteria: Given a valid `.env`, `docker compose up -d --wait` exits 0 and `docker compose ps --format json` shows `postgres`, `kafka`, `api` and `frontend` as `healthy` and `migrate` as `exited (0)`.

Given a stray listener on 5432, 8000, 3000 and 9092 (for example `python -m http.server` on each) and `POSTGRES_HOST_PORT=15432 API_HOST_PORT=18000 FRONTEND_HOST_PORT=13000 KAFKA_HOST_PORT=19092`, `docker compose up -d --wait` still exits 0 (no fixed host-port collision), and a second project (`-p other`) with different ports runs side by side.
Given `DB_PASSWORD` unset, `docker compose config` exits non-zero with the `set DB_PASSWORD` message (no secret default).
`docker compose config | grep -E "image:"` shows `pgvector/pgvector:0.8.5-pg16` and `apache/kafka:4.4.0` and no `redis`, `langfuse`, `litellm` or `kong` image.

Given a clean DB volume, after `up --wait`, `docker compose exec postgres psql -U $DB_USER -d $DB_NAME -c "select version_num from alembic_version"` returns `0001`; `curl -fsS localhost:$API_HOST_PORT/healthz` returns 200 and `/readyz` returns 200.
`docker compose down -v` leaves no containers or volumes for the project (`docker compose ps -a` empty).

tickets.title: Split unit and integration tests and add a dependency start script
tickets.summary: Tests are marked unit or integration, integration tests cannot silently skip when services are required, and one command starts the dependencies and runs them.
tickets.description:
Why: the suite shows `97 passed, 25 skipped`: every DB test uses `requires_db`, which skips silently when Postgres is absent and hard-codes `localhost:5432` with the `localdev` password in `backend/tests/conftest.py`. A CI that skips them is green and dishonest (G-05 intent: CI can fail). builder:engineering needs "a way to start dependencies for integration tests".

Do:
- Register pytest markers `unit` (default for tests without a marker) and `integration` in `backend/pyproject.toml`; mark all DB-backed tests (`requires_db` users: test_rls, test_rls_context, test_rls_e2e, test_integration, test_search_kb and similar) as `integration`.
- `conftest.py`: build the test database URL from the Settings env keys (`DB_HOST`, `DB_PORT`, `DB_NAME`, `DB_USER`, `DB_PASSWORD`), not a literal. When env `REQUIRE_SERVICES=1` is set, an unreachable database makes the test fail (not skip).
- Add `backend/tests/integration/test_kafka_reachable.py`: lists topics through the Kafka admin client against `KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP` (test-only env var for now; add `confluent-kafka==2.16.1` to the dev group, stack.md pin) and fails if the broker is unreachable. The same test is skipped unless `REQUIRE_SERVICES=1` or the broker answers.
- Add a `Makefile` at the repo root with targets `deps-up` (`docker compose up -d --wait postgres kafka migrate`), `deps-down` (`docker compose down -v`), and `test-integration` (`deps-up` then `REQUIRE_SERVICES=1 pytest -m integration`, then `deps-down` on exit), plus `test-unit` (`pytest -m "not integration"`).

Out of scope: the CI workflow (E0-T13), the eval gate (E7), Kafka produce/consume logic (E5).
acceptance_criteria: `cd backend && pytest -m "not integration" -q` passes with Postgres stopped and reports 0 skipped.

Given Postgres stopped and `REQUIRE_SERVICES=1`, `pytest -m integration` fails (non-zero exit, tests reported failed, not skipped); given Postgres stopped and `REQUIRE_SERVICES` unset the tests skip with a reason naming the missing service.
`make test-integration` on a clean machine brings up postgres and kafka, runs the integration tests with 0 skipped and 0 failed, and removes the containers afterwards (`docker compose ps -a` empty).
`grep -rn "localdev" backend/tests` returns no match.
`pytest --collect-only -m integration -q` lists every test that previously used `requires_db` (count equals the 25 formerly skipped tests, none lost).

tickets.title: Rewrite CI: lockfile installs, service containers, all checks
tickets.summary: A pull request runs ruff, mypy, unit and integration tests, the model-id check, eslint, tsc and vitest from lockfiles, and any failure blocks the PR.
tickets.description:
Why: G-05: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `pip install -e ".[dev]"` but no `dev` extra exists, so ruff, mypy and pytest are not installed and CI fails at Lint; `eval-gate.yml` has the same install and cannot run (G-06, owned by E7). ADR-021: "Lockfile installs only. Python: ruff, mypy, pytest, import-linter; frontend: eslint, tsc, vitest". plan.md E0: "CI with lockfile installs, Postgres and Kafka service containers (`pgvector/pgvector:0.8.5-pg16`)". The security scans are E0-T14. Unit-testing import-linter contracts is a later epic (no contracts exist yet).

Replace `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Triggers `pull_request` to `main` and `push` to `main`; `permissions: contents: read`; concurrency cancels superseded runs; every `uses:` action pinned to a full commit SHA with the tag in a comment. Jobs:
- `backend-static`: Python 3.12, `pip install poetry==<pinned>`, `poetry check --lock`, `poetry install --with dev --no-interaction` from `backend/poetry.lock`; `ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .`, `mypy src/`; `python -m src.model_lifecycle` (E0-T4, with default env so the check runs on the configured ids); `bash scripts/check_no_litellm.sh` (E0-T6).
- `backend-unit`: same install; `pytest -m "not integration"`.
- `backend-integration`: service containers `pgvector/pgvector:0.8.5-pg16` and `apache/kafka:4.4.0` (KRaft, health options so the job waits for healthy), `postgresql-client-16` installed for `pg_dump`, `REQUIRE_SERVICES=1`, runs `python -m src.entrypoint jobs migrate` then `pytest -m integration`. Test-only DB credentials come from workflow env generated for the job (not repository defaults in code).
- `frontend`: Node 20, `npm ci`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build`.
- Delete `.github/workflows/eval-gate.yml` (it cannot run; E7 re-creates the gate on the service containers defined here; see questions).
- Document in `docs/ci.md` the job list and the negative-control procedure below.

Out of scope: trivy, gitleaks, pip-audit (E0-T14), terraform and `kong config parse` jobs (E2, E10), deploy and WIF (E10), eval gate (E7). Making the jobs required checks is a GitHub branch-protection setting, not a file in the repo (see questions).
acceptance_criteria: Given a clean clone of the PR branch, the `CI` workflow completes green on GitHub with all four jobs passing and installs coming only from `backend/poetry.lock` and `frontend/package-lock.json` (`poetry check --lock` and `npm ci` steps present).

Negative controls, each on a throwaway branch with the run link recorded in `docs/ci.md`: an unused import turns `backend-static` red (ruff); a wrong return type turns it red (mypy); a failing unit test turns `backend-unit` red; a failing integration test turns `backend-integration` red; an eslint error, a TypeScript error and a failing vitest test each turn `frontend` red.
Given `LLM_MODEL_ANSWER=claude-sonnet-4-20250514` in the job env, `backend-static` fails at the model-id step (negative control), and passes with the default.
In `backend-integration` the pytest summary reports 0 skipped (the job greps the summary line and fails if `skipped` appears).
`grep -rn "\.\[dev\]" .github` returns no match and `.github/workflows/eval-gate.yml` does not exist.
`actionlint` run on `.github/workflows/ci.yml` reports no errors, and every `uses:` line carries a 40-hex SHA.

tickets.title: Add trivy, gitleaks and pip-audit jobs that fail the PR
tickets.summary: Every PR is scanned for vulnerable dependencies, leaked secrets and image vulnerabilities, and findings fail the job.
tickets.description:
Why: G-05 / plan.md E0: CI runs "trivy, gitleaks, pip-audit" and "each ... runs and can fail a PR". ADR-021: security: trivy, gitleaks, pip-audit.

Add to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (or a `security.yml` called from it; tool and action versions pinned, actions by SHA):
- `pip-audit`: export the locked main and dev dependencies from `backend/poetry.lock` (`poetry export --with dev --without-hashes`, or the supported equivalent) and run `pip-audit -r <file> --strict`; non-zero on any known vulnerability.
- `gitleaks`: scan the full git history of the PR (`fetch-depth: 0`) with a repo `.gitleaks.toml` that extends the default rules; the only allowlist entries are `.env.example` placeholders and test fixtures with a written reason each.
- `trivy`: `fs` scan of the repo (lockfiles, Dockerfiles, IaC misconfig) and an `image` scan of the `runtime` backend image from E0-T2 and the frontend dev image, `--severity HIGH,CRITICAL --exit-code 1 --ignore-unfixed`, with `.trivyignore` entries allowed only with a comment and expiry date.
- If the first run reports existing findings, fix them by upgrading the locked dependency or base image; do not blanket-ignore. Record any unavoidable exception in `.trivyignore` / pip-audit `--ignore-vuln` with an expiry.
- Extend `docs/ci.md` with these jobs and their negative controls.

Out of scope: SBOM, image signing, Model Armor, `terraform` scanning of the target state (E10).
acceptance_criteria: Given a clean PR branch, the `pip-audit`, `gitleaks` and `trivy` jobs all pass on GitHub.
Negative control (recorded run links in `docs/ci.md`): adding a fake high-entropy cloud key such as `AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE` with a matching secret pattern to a tracked file turns `gitleaks` red.
Negative control: pinning a package with a known CVE in `backend/poetry.lock` (for example an old `urllib3` or `jinja2` version) turns `pip-audit` red.
Negative control: a Dockerfile base image with a known HIGH/CRITICAL OS vulnerability (an old `python:3.8` image) turns `trivy` red.
`gitleaks detect --source . --config .gitleaks.toml` run locally on the merged branch exits 0, and `.trivyignore` and the gitleaks allowlist contain only entries with a reason (checked in review).

tickets.title: Spike: verify Identity Platform tenant claim and billing
tickets.summary: The exact ID-token tenant claim, firebase-admin tenant-aware verification behaviour and the >2-tenant billing rule are confirmed against a real Identity Platform project and recorded as an ADR.
tickets.description:
Spike, first ticket of E1 (D14.17). Arch text to confirm: "the `firebase.tenant` claim names the IdP tenant, and `tenant_mgt.auth_for_tenant(tenant_id).verify_id_token(...)` checks signature, `aud`, `iss`, `exp` and raises `TenantIdMismatchError` on a tenant mismatch" (overview 4.5 `auth`; 8.2 step 4: "The claim name is verified in the first E1 ticket"). Also 8.2 step 7: "Identity Platform multi-tenancy needs billing enabled for more than 2 tenants; email/password tier free to 50k MAU".

Build a throwaway probe script `backend/scripts/spikes/idp_claim_probe.py` (not imported by app code). With a real GCP project that has Identity Platform and multi-tenancy enabled (project id from `IDP_PROJECT_ID`, credentials via ADC):
1. Create 3 IdP tenants (more than 2, to observe the billing requirement), enable email/password on each, create one user per tenant, sign in through the REST sign-in endpoint with the tenant id and obtain an ID token.
2. Decode each token (no verification) and record the exact JSON path of the tenant claim, plus `sub`, `aud`, `iss`.
3. Verify with `firebase_admin.tenant_mgt.auth_for_tenant(<tenant>).verify_id_token`: (a) token of tenant A against tenant A (ok), (b) token of tenant B against tenant A (expect `TenantIdMismatchError`), (c) an expired token, (d) a token with a different project audience. Record the exception class raised for each.
4. Record whether creating the 3rd tenant is rejected without billing and succeeds with billing (operator action: the project owner enables billing; note the date).
5. Add `firebase-admin` to the lockfile (pinned; stack.md says "pin at implementation") and record the version.

Record the result as `docs/adr/idp-multitenancy-claim.md` in this repo (the researcher copies it into `arch/decisions.md` as the next ADR number after merge; do not write to the harness repo) with: the claim path, the exceptions per case, the billing observation, the pinned firebase-admin version, whether the Firebase Auth emulator supports multi-tenancy (if yes, E1-T13 and CI use the emulator; if no, locally signed test JWTs with a test JWKS), and which one is chosen for E1-T13.

Out of scope: any production auth code (E1-T13), Terraform, SSO.
acceptance_criteria: Given a token issued by IdP tenant B, when `idp_claim_probe.py --check` verifies it with `auth_for_tenant(A)`, then it raises `TenantIdMismatchError`; the script exits non-zero if any of cases (a)-(d) behaves differently from the ADR's recorded outcome.

The ADR file `docs/adr/idp-multitenancy-claim.md` exists and names the exact claim JSON path found in a real decoded token (matching the claims printed by the probe and saved in `docs/adr/idp-probe-output.json`, which contains no secrets or raw tokens).
The ADR records, for 3 tenants in one project, whether the 3rd tenant creation succeeded and under which billing state, with the date.
`poetry.lock` contains a pinned `firebase-admin` version and the ADR states the same version (`poetry show firebase-admin` equals the ADR value).
The ADR states whether the Auth emulator supports multi-tenancy and names the single approach E1-T13 uses (emulator, else locally signed JWTs with a test JWKS).

tickets.title: Spike: LIST-partition pruning and planner cost at 52 partitions
tickets.summary: Partition pruning under the RLS current_setting policy and planning/query cost at about 52 chunks partitions are measured and recorded as an ADR.
tickets.description:
Spike. ADR-003: "Runtime pruning with the RLS `current_setting` policy confirmed by test on the 8-partition setup ("Subplans Removed: 6 of 8") ... planner and migration cost at ~50 partitions is unmeasured (E1 measures it); the pruning test must be repeated on LIST partitions." Scope line: "LIST-partition pruning with the RLS `current_setting` policy plus planner cost at ~52 partitions."

Build `backend/scripts/spikes/list_partition_probe.py` (throwaway, uses the `pgvector/pgvector:0.8.5-pg16` image from E0 compose/CI):
1. Create a scratch database and a `chunks` table `PARTITION BY LIST (tenant_id)` with 50 tenant partitions, 1 PUBLIC partition and 1 DEFAULT partition (52 total), columns reduced to those needed: `tenant_id, id, kind, content, tsv, embedding halfvec(1024), tier_required, jurisdiction`, with the per-partition indexes declared on the parent exactly as in overview 5.5 (HNSW `halfvec_cosine_ops` m=16 ef_construction=64 partial `WHERE kind='child'`, GIN on tsv, btrees).
2. Enable `ENABLE` + `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` and the `chunks_select_app` policy text from overview 5.4 (own tenant OR PUBLIC, tier, jurisdiction) for a non-owner NOBYPASSRLS role; seed 200 child chunks per partition with random embeddings.
3. As that role, in a transaction with `set_config('app.tenant_id', ..., true)` etc., run the dense leg and the FTS leg of the overview 5.6 hybrid statement with `SET LOCAL hnsw.iterative_scan = relaxed_order` and `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, VERBOSE)`; capture which partitions executed vs "never executed"/removed, planning time and execution time over 200 runs; repeat for 2, 8 and 52 partitions to show the trend.
4. Measure the wall time to create one partition with its indexes (the onboarding cost).

Record the result as `docs/adr/list-partition-pruning.md` in this repo (the researcher copies it into `arch/decisions.md` as the next ADR number after merge; do not write to the harness repo) with the numbers, the EXPLAIN excerpt, the fallback taken if a check failed, and a keep / change decision on LIST partitions.

Out of scope: production migrations (E1-T5), tuning HNSW parameters.
acceptance_criteria: Given 52 partitions and the RLS policy, when the probe runs `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE)` on the dense leg for one tenant, then no partition other than the caller's tenant partition, the PUBLIC partition and the DEFAULT partition is executed; the script exits non-zero otherwise and prints the 'Subplans Removed' value.

The probe's p95 of planning time + execution time over 200 runs of the hybrid statement at 52 partitions is <= 100 ms (the ADR-003 revisit trigger) and the planning-time p95 alone is <= 10 ms; the script exits non-zero if either is exceeded and prints both measured p95 values.
`docs/adr/list-partition-pruning.md` exists and contains a table of planning time p50/p95 for 2, 8 and 52 partitions and the measured time to create one partition with indexes.
The ADR ends with an explicit decision line (keep LIST partitions, or change with the reason); if the 52-partition check failed, the line names the fallback.

tickets.title: Bootstrap DB roles and the separate dagster database
tickets.summary: All ten database roles exist with the exact attributes the arch requires, created by an idempotent bootstrap script that compose and CI run.
tickets.description:
Implement overview 5.3: "One login role per process ... All are NOSUPERUSER, NOCREATEDB, NOCREATEROLE, NOBYPASSRLS. Runtime roles own nothing, with two explicit exemptions."

Create `backend/db/bootstrap/roles.sql` (idempotent: `DO` blocks / `\gexec`), run by the compose Postgres init and by the CI Postgres service step (E0 compose and CI files updated). Roles: `fa_owner` (login; used by `migrate` only), `fa_lookup` (NOLOGIN), `fa_app`, `fa_worker`, `fa_etl`, `fa_etl_public`, `fa_dbt`, `fa_maint`, `fa_eval`, `fa_dagster` (login). Passwords come from env vars (`DB_PASSWORD_<ROLE>`), none hard-coded. Database `dagster` is created and owned by `fa_dagster`; `fa_dagster` has no CONNECT on the app database (`REVOKE CONNECT ON DATABASE <app> FROM PUBLIC`, then grant CONNECT to the app roles only). `fa_owner` is the owner of the app database and (via later migrations) of all objects except schema `gold` and table `messages`. Create schema `gold` owned by `fa_dbt`.

Compose services get `DB_USER` set to their process role (`fa_app` for the api, `fa_worker` for the worker); `Settings` keys used: `DB_HOST`, `DB_NAME`, `DB_USER`, `DB_PASSWORD`.

Out of scope: Cloud SQL role creation and secrets (E10 Terraform), grants and policies on tables (E1-T8 to E1-T10).
acceptance_criteria: Given the bootstrap has run, when `tests/db/test_roles.py` queries `pg_roles`, then for each of the 10 roles `rolsuper`, `rolcreatedb`, `rolcreaterole` and `rolbypassrls` are all false, and `fa_lookup.rolcanlogin` is false while the other nine can log in.
Given the script is run twice on the same database, then the second run exits 0 and `pg_roles` is unchanged (test).
Given a connection as `fa_dagster`, when it tries to connect to the app database, then it fails with permission denied; and `pg_database` shows `dagster` owned by `fa_dagster` (test).
Given a connection as `fa_app`, when it runs `CREATE TABLE x(a int)` in schema public, then it fails with permission denied (runtime roles own nothing and cannot create objects).

tickets.title: Migration: tenants and advisors tables
tickets.summary: The tenants and advisors tables exist with all target columns, constraints and FORCE RLS, and the PUBLIC tenant row is seeded.
tickets.description:
Add an Alembic revision (0002 or later; E0 owns the immutable baseline 0001 = MVP schema.sql) creating, as `fa_owner`, the two identity tables per overview 5.2:

- `tenants` (key `id uuid`): `slug` unique, `display_name`, `kind` CHECK in (`firm`,`public`), `idp_tenant_id` unique (nullable for the PUBLIC row), `corpus_version bigint` default 0, `acl_version bigint` default 0, `budgets jsonb` default `{}` (values set in E4), `shard_id text` (seam, D2), `status`, `created_at`.
- `advisors` (key `(tenant_id, id)`): `idp_uid` (token `sub`) with unique `(tenant_id, idp_uid)`, `display_name`, `role` CHECK in (`advisor`,`compliance_officer`,`tenant_admin`), `tier smallint CHECK 1..4`, `jurisdictions text[]` CHECK subset of (`US`,`EU`,`UK`), `licenses text[]`, `entitlement_version bigint` default 0, `status`, FK `tenant_id` to `tenants(id)`.

Both tables: `ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; ... FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;` at creation (no policy yet, so they deny everything until E1-T9 adds policies and grants). Seed the reserved PUBLIC row: id = `PUBLIC_TENANT_ID` (from Settings, substituted by the migration), `kind='public'`, `slug='public'`. Every table in the target model carries `tenant_id uuid NOT NULL` (on `tenants` the key `id`).

Out of scope: policies and grants (E1-T9), the other tables (E1-T5 to E1-T7), advisor seeding (E1-T11).
acceptance_criteria: Given an empty database, when `alembic upgrade head` runs, then `tests/db/test_schema_identity.py` passes: both tables exist with `relrowsecurity` and `relforcerowsecurity` true in `pg_class`.
Given an insert of an advisor with `tier = 5`, or `jurisdictions = '{XX}'`, or an unknown `role`, then each raises a CheckViolation (three test cases).
Given two advisors with the same `(tenant_id, idp_uid)`, then the second insert raises a UniqueViolation; the same `idp_uid` in two different tenants succeeds.
Given the migration ran with `PUBLIC_TENANT_ID=<uuid>`, then `SELECT kind FROM tenants WHERE id = '<uuid>'` returns `public` (test run as `fa_owner`).

tickets.title: Migration: content tables with LIST-partitioned chunks
tickets.summary: documents, chunks (LIST by tenant), suitability_rules and ingest_rejects exist in the target shape with composite FKs, raw_content dropped, and the PUBLIC and DEFAULT partitions.
tickets.description:
Add an Alembic revision (0002 or later; baseline 0001 is immutable) as `fa_owner` that replaces the MVP content tables with the target shape of overview 5.2 and 5.5. The MVP `documents.raw_content` column is dropped (G-03: "No `raw_content` column"). The service has never been deployed, so the revision drops and recreates the MVP content tables without a data migration.

Tables, all `FORCE` + `ENABLE` RLS at creation, all with `tenant_id uuid NOT NULL`:
- `documents (tenant_id, id)`: columns per 5.2 (`title, doc_type, jurisdiction, tier_required CHECK 1..4, regulatory_ref, last_reviewed_at, product_category, risk_level, source CHECK in (edgar, synthetic), source_uri, bronze_uri, bronze_sha256, parser_version, status CHECK in (active, superseded, deleted), created_at`); unique `(tenant_id, bronze_sha256)`; index `(tenant_id, doc_type, jurisdiction)`.
- `chunks (tenant_id, id)` `PARTITION BY LIST (tenant_id)`; columns per 5.2 including `embedding halfvec(1024)` and `tsv tsvector GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('simple', coalesce(context_header,'') || ' ' || content)) STORED`; composite FKs `(tenant_id, document_id)` to documents and `(tenant_id, parent_id)` self; unique `(tenant_id, chunk_hash, embed_model)`. Indexes declared on the parent so each partition gets its own: HNSW on `embedding halfvec_cosine_ops` `m=16, ef_construction=64` partial `WHERE kind = 'child'`; GIN on `tsv`; btree `(tenant_id, document_id)`, `(tenant_id, parent_id)`, `(tenant_id, tier_required, jurisdiction)`.
- `suitability_rules (tenant_id, id)`: per 5.2, composite FK `(tenant_id, source_document_id)`, `client_risk_profile` CHECK 3 values (use the values already in the MVP schema).
- `ingest_rejects (tenant_id, id)`: per 5.2.
Partitions: one for the PUBLIC tenant (`chunks_public`) and a DEFAULT partition (`chunks_default`); rows in DEFAULT are a bug. Write a reusable function `src/db/partitions.create_chunks_partition(conn, tenant_id)` (partition name from the uuid, no `GRANT`) that E1-T11 reuses. The partitions are created without any grants.

If E1-T2's ADR changed the partition design, follow the ADR.

Out of scope: policies and grants (E1-T8), tenant partitions (E1-T11), changing the retrieval code that reads these tables (E3).
acceptance_criteria: Given `alembic upgrade head` on an empty database, then `tests/db/test_schema_content.py` passes: `chunks` has `relkind='p'` and `partstrat='l'`, partitions `chunks_public` and `chunks_default` exist, and `documents` has no column named `raw_content`.
Given a chunk row whose `(tenant_id, document_id)` points to a document of another tenant, when inserted as `fa_owner`, then it raises a ForeignKeyViolation (composite FK; test).

Given the PUBLIC partition, then `pg_indexes` shows for it an HNSW index with `halfvec_cosine_ops`, `m='16'`, `ef_construction='64'` and predicate `kind = 'child'`, a GIN index on `tsv`, and the unique index on `(tenant_id, chunk_hash, embed_model)` (test).

Given `create_chunks_partition(conn, <uuid>)` is called, then a partition bound to that uuid exists and `has_table_privilege` for `fa_app`, `fa_worker`, `fa_etl`, `fa_etl_public` and `fa_dbt` on it is false for every privilege (test).
Given two chunks with the same `(tenant_id, chunk_hash, embed_model)`, then the second insert raises a UniqueViolation.

tickets.title: Migration: conversation, message and cache tables
tickets.summary: conversations, messages (monthly partitions, owned by fa_maint), turn_events, escalations, feedback and answer_cache exist in the target shape.
tickets.description:
Add an Alembic revision (0002 or later; baseline 0001 is immutable) as `fa_owner` creating the user-activity tables per overview 5.2 and 5.5. All have `tenant_id uuid NOT NULL`, `ENABLE` + `FORCE` RLS at creation, and composite FKs starting with `tenant_id`.

- `conversations (tenant_id, id)`: `advisor_id` (composite FK to advisors), `title`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `deleted_at`; index `(tenant_id, advisor_id, updated_at DESC)`.
- `messages (tenant_id, id, created_at)` `PARTITION BY RANGE (created_at)` monthly: `conversation_id` (composite FK), `advisor_id` (composite FK; used by the owner clause), `turn_id`, `role` CHECK (user, assistant), `content`, `status` CHECK (pending, streaming, complete, refused, failed), `model`, `prompt_version`, `citations jsonb`, `retrieval_chunk_ids uuid[]`, `retrieval_degraded boolean`, `usage jsonb`, `refusal_code`; local index `(tenant_id, conversation_id, created_at)`. A DEFAULT partition catches misses. The parent is owned by `fa_maint` ("Postgres requires ownership of the parent for partition DDL"); create the initial partitions (current month and 3 months ahead) in the migration and `ALTER ... OWNER TO fa_maint` on the parent and those partitions. Put the partition-creation SQL in a reusable function `src/db/partitions.create_messages_partitions(conn, months_ahead)` that E1-T12 reuses. No grants on partitions.
- `turn_events (tenant_id, turn_id, seq)`: `request_hash` (text, hash of the request body, used by E4 for idempotency-key reuse detection), `advisor_id`, `event`, `data jsonb`, `created_at`, `expires_at`; no FK.
- `escalations (tenant_id, id)`: `advisor_id` (composite FK), `reason`, `product_class`, `licenses`, `status`, `message_id`, `created_at`.
- `feedback (tenant_id, id)`: `message_id` (logical, no FK because the partitioned PK includes `created_at`), `advisor_id`, `score CHECK in (-1, 1)`, `comment`, `created_at`.
- `answer_cache (tenant_id, cache_key)`: UNLOGGED; `answer, citations jsonb, source_document_ids uuid[], created_at, expires_at`; index `(expires_at)` and GIN on `source_document_ids`.

This revision creates every remaining overview 5.2 table in full (including `answer_cache`, `turn_events`, `escalations`); later epics add only indexes/classes, not these tables.

Out of scope: policies and grants (E1-T10), the maintenance job (E1-T12), writing to these tables from `agent` (E4).
acceptance_criteria: Given `alembic upgrade head`, then `tests/db/test_schema_activity.py` passes: `answer_cache.relpersistence = 'u'`; `messages` is `relkind='p'`, `partstrat='r'`, owned by `fa_maint`, with partitions for the current month and the next 3 months plus a DEFAULT partition.
Given a conversation insert whose `(tenant_id, advisor_id)` references an advisor of another tenant, then it raises a ForeignKeyViolation (test).

Given `pg_constraint`, then `turn_events` has a `request_hash` column, `feedback` has no foreign key to `messages`, and every foreign key in the activity tables lists `tenant_id` as its first column (test iterating `pg_constraint`).
Given `create_messages_partitions(conn, 3)` is called twice, then the second call creates nothing and does not raise (idempotent), and no partition of `messages` has a grant to a runtime role.

tickets.title: Migration: ACL, eval, outbox, dedupe and tenant_usage tables
tickets.summary: acl_change_requests, eval_scores, outbox, processed_events and tenant_usage exist with their keys and indexes.
tickets.description:
Add an Alembic revision (0002 or later; baseline 0001 is immutable) as `fa_owner` creating the five tables per overview 5.2 (the outbox is written in E4 and relayed in E5). All have `tenant_id uuid NOT NULL`, `ENABLE` + `FORCE` RLS at creation.

- `acl_change_requests (tenant_id, id)`: `requested_by` (composite FK `(tenant_id, requested_by)` to advisors), `target_type` CHECK (`document`), `document_id`, `action` CHECK (`update_acl`,`delete`), `new_tier_required`, `new_jurisdiction`, `status` CHECK (`pending`,`applied`,`failed`) default `pending`, `error_code`, `requested_at`, `applied_at`.
- `eval_scores (tenant_id, id)`: `message_id` (logical), `judge_model`, `metric`, `score real`, `rationale`, `created_at`.
- `outbox (tenant_id, id)`: `topic`, `key`, `event_type`, `schema_version`, `payload jsonb`, `created_at`, `published_at`, `attempts int default 0`; `id` is the Kafka `event_id`; partial index on `(tenant_id, created_at) WHERE published_at IS NULL`.
- `processed_events (tenant_id, consumer, event_id)` key, `processed_at`.
- `tenant_usage (tenant_id, day)` key: `day date` (UTC day), `tokens_in bigint NOT NULL default 0`, `tokens_out bigint NOT NULL default 0`; counters for the per-tenant daily token budget (R47), written by chat-api in E4 instead of Valkey. FK `tenant_id` to `tenants(id)`.

Out of scope: policies and grants (E1-T10), writers (E4, E5).
acceptance_criteria: Given `alembic upgrade head`, then `tests/db/test_schema_pipeline.py` passes: the five tables (including `tenant_usage` with columns `tenant_id, day, tokens_in, tokens_out`) exist, each with `relrowsecurity` and `relforcerowsecurity` true.
Given `pg_indexes`, then `outbox` has an index whose definition contains `WHERE (published_at IS NULL)` on `(tenant_id, created_at)` (test).

Given an `acl_change_requests` row with `action = 'purge'`, or with `status = 'done'`, then each raises a CheckViolation; one whose `(tenant_id, requested_by)` names an advisor of another tenant raises a ForeignKeyViolation.
Given two `processed_events` rows with the same `(tenant_id, consumer, event_id)`, then the second raises a UniqueViolation.

tickets.title: RLS v2 policies and grants for content tables
tickets.summary: documents, chunks, suitability_rules and ingest_rejects have the own-or-PUBLIC read policies, own-tenant-only write policies, column grants and the fa_etl_public-only PUBLIC write.
tickets.description:
Add an Alembic revision implementing overview 5.4 and the 5.3 grants for the content tables. `<PUBLIC>` is the `PUBLIC_TENANT_ID` uuid literal substituted by the migration; `fa_eval` policies use the `EVAL_TENANT_ID` literal. Policies call `current_setting('app.x')` without `missing_ok`, so an unset setting raises (fail closed).

Policies (policy text for `chunks` is the arch text; `documents` and `suitability_rules` are identical in shape, `suitability_rules` uses `min_tier_required`):
- `*_select_app TO fa_app FOR SELECT`: `(tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id')::uuid OR tenant_id = '<PUBLIC>'::uuid) AND tier_required <= current_setting('app.tier')::int AND jurisdiction = ANY (string_to_array(current_setting('app.jurisdictions'), ','))`.
- `*_select_pipe TO fa_worker, fa_etl, fa_etl_public, fa_dbt FOR SELECT`: own tenant only.
- `*_ins_tenant`, `*_upd_tenant`, `*_del_tenant TO fa_worker`: own tenant and `tenant_id <> '<PUBLIC>'` (USING and WITH CHECK on UPDATE). `fa_etl` gets INSERT and UPDATE on `documents` with the same own non-PUBLIC clause, and SELECT on `chunks`.
- `*_all_public TO fa_etl_public FOR ALL`: USING and WITH CHECK `tenant_id = '<PUBLIC>'::uuid`.
- `fa_eval`: the `fa_app` policies with the tenant literal of the `eval` tenant plus PUBLIC reads.
- `ingest_rejects`: tenant match for the roles holding grants, no PUBLIC clause.
`fa_app` has no INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE policy or grant on `chunks`, `documents`, `suitability_rules` ("document ACL changes and deletes are applied by the `acl-applier` worker (ADR-022)").

Grants per 5.3: `fa_app` SELECT only; `fa_worker` on `chunks` SELECT, INSERT, DELETE and UPDATE (`tier_required`, `jurisdiction`) only, on `documents` SELECT, INSERT, DELETE and UPDATE (`tier_required`, `jurisdiction`, `status`, `parser_version`), on `suitability_rules` SELECT, INSERT, DELETE, on `ingest_rejects` SELECT, INSERT; `fa_etl` SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE (`status`, `parser_version`, `bronze_uri`) on `documents` and SELECT on `chunks`; `fa_etl_public` write on the content tables; `fa_dbt` SELECT; `fa_eval` the `fa_app` grants. Never `GRANT ... ON ALL TABLES` (partitions get no grants).

Out of scope: tenants/advisors (E1-T9), other tables (E1-T10), the full leak matrix (E1-T19, E1-T20).
acceptance_criteria: Given a principal for tenant A (tier 2, jurisdictions US), when `fa_app` selects from `chunks` after `set_config(..., true)`, then it sees tenant A and PUBLIC rows only, never tenant B rows, never rows with `tier_required = 3`, never rows with `jurisdiction = 'EU'` (`tests/db/test_rls_content.py`, parametrised over `chunks`, `documents`, `suitability_rules`).
Given `fa_app`, when it runs INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE on `chunks`, `documents` or `suitability_rules`, then each fails with permission denied (no grant).

Given `fa_worker` bound to tenant A, when it inserts a chunk with `tenant_id` = B, or with `tenant_id` = PUBLIC, then each raises a row-level-security violation; and when it updates `documents.title`, then it fails with permission denied (column grant).
Given `fa_etl_public`, when it inserts a chunk into the PUBLIC tenant, then it succeeds; when it inserts into tenant A, then it raises a row-level-security violation.
Given `fa_eval` with `app.tenant_id` set to tenant A, when it selects from `documents`, then it sees only `EVAL_TENANT_ID` and PUBLIC rows.
Given no `app.tenant_id` set in the transaction, when `fa_app` selects from `chunks`, then it raises `unrecognized configuration parameter` (fail closed) and returns no rows.

tickets.title: RLS for tenants and advisors, and fa_tenant_lookup
tickets.summary: tenants and advisors policies and grants are in place, advisors cannot self-escalate, and the single SECURITY DEFINER function fa_tenant_lookup exists.
tickets.description:
Add an Alembic revision implementing the `tenants` and `advisors` items of overview 5.4 and the 5.3 grants.

`tenants`: `tenants_select_app TO fa_app FOR SELECT USING (id = current_setting('app.tenant_id')::uuid OR id = '<PUBLIC>'::uuid)`; `tenants_lookup TO fa_lookup FOR SELECT USING (true)`; `tenants_owner TO fa_owner` for SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE; `tenants_upd_worker TO fa_worker FOR UPDATE USING / WITH CHECK (id = app.tenant_id AND id <> <PUBLIC>)`; `tenants_upd_public TO fa_etl_public FOR UPDATE USING / WITH CHECK (id = <PUBLIC>)`. Column grants: `fa_app` SELECT on (`id`, `slug`, `corpus_version`, `acl_version`, `budgets`) only; `fa_lookup` SELECT on the columns the function returns plus `slug`; UPDATE limited to `corpus_version` and `acl_version` for `fa_worker` and to `corpus_version` for `fa_etl_public`.

`advisors`: SELECT `TO fa_app` when `tenant_id = app.tenant_id AND (id = app.user_id OR idp_uid = app.idp_uid OR app.role = 'tenant_admin')`; UPDATE `TO fa_app` only when `tenant_id = app.tenant_id AND app.role = 'tenant_admin'`, `WITH CHECK (tenant_id = app.tenant_id)`. Column grants: UPDATE on `tier, jurisdictions, licenses, role, status, entitlement_version` only (`tenant_id` immutable). No self-escalation: "an advisor cannot raise their own tier or role".

`fa_tenant_lookup(p_slug text DEFAULT NULL, p_idp_tenant_id text DEFAULT NULL)`: `SECURITY DEFINER`, owned by `fa_lookup` (not `fa_owner`), explicit `SET search_path`, returns `(id, display_name, idp_tenant_id)`, serves both slug discovery and the `idp_tenant_id` to `tenants.id` mapping (D14.4); `REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM PUBLIC; GRANT EXECUTE ... TO fa_app;`. It is the only `SECURITY DEFINER` function allowed in the database. With both arguments NULL it returns no rows.

Out of scope: the HTTP endpoint (E1-T16), the principal that calls the function (E1-T14).
acceptance_criteria: Given a principal of tenant A, when `fa_app` selects from `tenants`, then it sees exactly the tenant A row and the PUBLIC row; selecting a column outside the grant (e.g. `idp_tenant_id`) fails with permission denied; any UPDATE on `tenants` by `fa_app` fails with permission denied (`tests/db/test_rls_identity.py`).
Given an advisor with `app.role = 'advisor'`, when it runs `UPDATE advisors SET tier = 4, role = 'tenant_admin' WHERE id = app.user_id`, then rowcount is 0 and the stored tier and role are unchanged.

Given `app.role = 'tenant_admin'` of tenant A, when it updates the tier of an advisor of tenant A then it succeeds; of an advisor of tenant B then rowcount is 0; `UPDATE advisors SET tenant_id = ...` fails with permission denied.

Given `fa_tenant_lookup(p_slug => 'acme')` called as `fa_app`, then it returns exactly the columns `id, display_name, idp_tenant_id`; called as `fa_worker` it fails with permission denied; `has_function_privilege('public', ...)` is false.
Given `pg_proc`, then exactly one function with `prosecdef = true` exists in the app schemas, it is `fa_tenant_lookup`, and its owner is `fa_lookup` (test).
Given `fa_tenant_lookup(NULL, NULL)` called as `fa_app`, then it returns zero rows (test).

tickets.title: RLS and grants for activity, pipeline and usage tables
tickets.summary: conversations, messages, turn_events, feedback, escalations, acl_change_requests, eval_scores, outbox, processed_events and answer_cache have their owner-clause policies and grants.
tickets.description:
Add an Alembic revision implementing the "Other tables" part of overview 5.4 and the matching 5.3 grants.

Policies:
- `conversations`, `messages`, `turn_events`, `feedback`: tenant match AND `advisor_id = current_setting('app.user_id')::uuid` (an advisor sees only their own rows) for `fa_app` (SELECT / INSERT / UPDATE as granted).
- `escalations`: tenant match AND (`advisor_id = app.user_id` OR `app.role = 'compliance_officer'`).
- `acl_change_requests`: SELECT and INSERT `TO fa_app` when the tenant matches and `app.role = 'tenant_admin'`; UPDATE of (`status`, `applied_at`, `error_code`) `TO fa_worker` on the own non-PUBLIC tenant.
- `eval_scores`, `outbox`, `processed_events`: tenant match for the roles that hold grants, no PUBLIC clause; `eval_scores` has no grant to `fa_app`.
- `tenant_usage`: tenant match for `fa_app` (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE; chat-api writes it) and `fa_eval` pinned to the eval tenant; no PUBLIC clause.
- `answer_cache`: tenant match for `fa_app` and `fa_worker` (worker: DELETE only); `fa_maint` may DELETE expired rows only (`expires_at < now()`); same limit for `fa_maint` on `turn_events`.
- `outbox`: `fa_app` SELECT / INSERT / UPDATE, `fa_worker` SELECT / INSERT / UPDATE, `fa_maint` SELECT (`id`, `published_at`) limited to unpublished rows.
- `messages` owned by `fa_maint`: `fa_maint` has no policy and so no row access.
- `fa_eval`: the `fa_app` policies pinned to the `EVAL_TENANT_ID` literal plus PUBLIC reads where `fa_app` has them.

Grants exactly per overview 5.3 (fa_app: SELECT / INSERT / UPDATE on `conversations, messages, turn_events, escalations, feedback, answer_cache, outbox`; SELECT / INSERT / UPDATE on `tenant_usage`; SELECT / INSERT on `acl_change_requests`; fa_worker lines for `acl_change_requests`, `eval_scores`, `answer_cache`, `outbox`, `processed_events`). No `GRANT ... ON ALL TABLES`; partitions of `messages` get no grants.

Out of scope: writers of these tables (E4, E5, E6).
acceptance_criteria: Given advisors X and Y of tenant A with conversations, when `fa_app` bound to X selects from `conversations`, `messages`, `turn_events` and `feedback`, then it sees only X's rows (`tests/db/test_rls_activity.py`).

Given an `escalations` row of advisor Y, when a principal with `app.role = 'compliance_officer'` in tenant A selects, then it sees it; with `app.role = 'advisor'` and another `user_id` it does not; a compliance officer of tenant B does not.

Given `app.role = 'advisor'`, when it inserts into `acl_change_requests`, then it raises a row-level-security violation; with `tenant_admin` it succeeds; `fa_worker` updating `acl_change_requests.document_id` fails with permission denied (column grant).

Given an expired and a live row in `answer_cache`, when `fa_maint` runs `DELETE FROM answer_cache`, then only the expired row is deleted; `fa_maint` selecting from `messages` returns no rows (no policy).

Given `fa_app`, when it selects from `eval_scores`, then it fails with permission denied; `fa_worker` inserting an `outbox` row with another tenant's `tenant_id` raises a row-level-security violation.

Given `tenant_usage` rows for tenants A and B, when `fa_app` bound to A selects, inserts or updates, then it sees and changes only A's rows, and inserting a row with B's `tenant_id` raises a row-level-security violation (`tests/db/test_rls_activity.py`).

tickets.title: Tenant onboarding and advisor seeding in the migrate job
tickets.summary: `migrate --onboard-tenant` creates a tenant's chunks LIST partition with indexes, its tenants row and the IdP mapping, idempotently and without partition grants.
tickets.description:
Implement the onboarding step in the `migrate` entrypoint (E0 created the entrypoint; Cloud Run job, role `fa_owner`): overview 4.8 "`migrate` ... tenant onboarding (`--onboard-tenant <slug>`: LIST partition + indexes, `tenants` row, IdP mapping; the IdP tenant itself is provisioned by an onboarding script in E1 ...)". ADR-003: "Tenant onboarding creates its partition and indexes in the `migrate` job."

CLI: `migrate --onboard-tenant <slug> --display-name <name> --idp-tenant-id <id> [--tenant-id <uuid>] [--kind firm|public]`. In one transaction as `fa_owner`: insert the `tenants` row (`status='active'`, new uuid unless `--tenant-id`), call `create_chunks_partition` (E1-T5; partition plus the parent-declared indexes), commit. Rerunning with the same slug is a no-op that exits 0. If rows for that tenant already sit in the DEFAULT partition, exit non-zero with a clear message (do not move rows). The dedicated `eval` tenant is onboarded with `--tenant-id $EVAL_TENANT_ID`. The PUBLIC tenant already exists (E1-T4, E1-T5). Partitions get no grants. Print the new `tenants.id`.

Seed command (R18): `migrate --seed-advisors <file>` reads a JSON file of advisors (`tenant_slug, idp_uid, display_name, role, tier, jurisdictions, licenses`), resolves the tenant by slug, and inserts the `advisors` rows as `fa_owner` (upsert on `(tenant_id, idp_uid)`, idempotent). It is the only way the first advisors are created (demo setup uses it); there is no auto-provision on first login. Unknown tenant slug, invalid tier/role/jurisdiction, or malformed file exits non-zero and inserts nothing.

Out of scope: creating the IdP tenant (E1-T21), Terraform (E10), a tenant-creation HTTP endpoint ("Tenant onboarding (partition creation) is a job, not an endpoint").
acceptance_criteria: Given an empty database after migrations, when `migrate --onboard-tenant acme --display-name Acme --idp-tenant-id idp-acme` runs, then `tests/db/test_onboarding.py` passes: one `tenants` row with slug `acme` exists, `chunks` has a partition bound to its id, and `fa_tenant_lookup(p_idp_tenant_id => 'idp-acme')` returns that id.
Given the same command is run a second time, then it exits 0 and `SELECT count(*) FROM tenants WHERE slug = 'acme'` is 1 and `chunks` still has exactly one partition for it.
Given a chunk inserted for the onboarded tenant by `fa_owner`, then `tableoid::regclass` is the tenant's partition and `chunks_default` is empty (test).

Given the new partition, then none of `fa_app, fa_worker, fa_etl, fa_etl_public, fa_dbt, fa_eval` has any privilege on it (`has_table_privilege`), and the same indexes as `chunks_public` exist on it (compared by definition).
Given rows of the tenant already in `chunks_default`, when onboarding that tenant runs, then the command exits non-zero and creates no partition.

Given a seed file with one valid advisor and one with an unknown `tenant_slug`, when `migrate --seed-advisors` runs, then it exits non-zero and the `advisors` table has no new rows; given only valid entries it inserts them, and a second run leaves the row count unchanged (`tests/db/test_seed_advisors.py`).

tickets.title: Maintenance job: messages partitions and expired-row purge
tickets.summary: The maintenance job, running as fa_maint, creates messages partitions 3 months ahead, drops partitions past retention, and purges expired answer_cache and turn_events rows.
tickets.description:
Add the `maintenance` entrypoint to the `jobs` image (overview 4.8): role `fa_maint`; "Purges expired `answer_cache` and `turn_events` rows; creates `messages` partitions 3 months ahead and drops those past retention". Scheduling is E10; `demo-up` triggering is E10; this ticket makes the job runnable (`python -m src.cli maintenance`) and tested.

Behaviour:
1. `create_messages_partitions(conn, 3)` (E1-T6), idempotent.
2. Drop `messages` partitions whose whole range is older than the retention window. Retention is the config key `MESSAGES_RETENTION_MONTHS` (default 6), added to Settings. Never drop the DEFAULT partition.
3. `DELETE FROM answer_cache WHERE expires_at < now()` and `DELETE FROM turn_events WHERE expires_at < now()` (policy limits `fa_maint` to expired rows).
4. Log counts (structured, no row content). Exit non-zero if the DEFAULT partition of `messages` is non-empty after the run ("alert if non-empty").
Connects with `DB_USER=fa_maint` via Settings.

Out of scope: Cloud Scheduler, `demo-ttl` (E10), alert wiring (E9).
acceptance_criteria: Given the current month plus 3 months of partitions already exist, when `maintenance` runs, then no partition is created and exit code is 0; given the newest partition is only 1 month ahead, when it runs, then partitions up to current month + 3 exist afterwards (`tests/jobs/test_maintenance.py`).

Given `MESSAGES_RETENTION_MONTHS=6` (the default) and a partition whose range ends more than 6 months ago, when `maintenance` runs, then that partition is dropped, a partition within 6 months is kept, and the DEFAULT partition is untouched.
Given one expired and one live `turn_events` row and one expired and one live `answer_cache` row, when `maintenance` runs, then only the expired rows are removed.
Given a row in the `messages` DEFAULT partition, when `maintenance` runs, then it exits non-zero.
Given the job's DB connection, then `current_user = 'fa_maint'` and an attempt to `SELECT` from `chunks` fails with permission denied.

tickets.title: auth module: tenant-aware ID token verification
tickets.summary: A FastAPI dependency verifies the Identity Platform ID token tenant-aware with firebase-admin and returns (sub, idp_tenant_id), replacing the X-User-Id header.
tickets.description:
Implement the `auth` module (overview 4.5): "verifies the `Authorization: Bearer <Identity Platform ID token>` with firebase-admin tenant-aware verification: the `firebase.tenant` claim names the IdP tenant, and `tenant_mgt.auth_for_tenant(tenant_id).verify_id_token(...)` checks signature, `aud`, `iss`, `exp` and raises `TenantIdMismatchError` on a tenant mismatch. Output: `(sub, idp_tenant_id)`. Never reads identity from headers." Fixes G-01. Follow the claim name and exception classes recorded by the E1-T1 ADR. Tests use the Firebase Auth emulator in CI if the E1-T1 ADR says it supports multi-tenancy; otherwise locally signed test JWTs with a test JWKS (as the ADR records).

Build `src/auth/verifier.py`: `async verify_bearer(authorization: str | None) -> VerifiedIdentity(sub, idp_tenant_id)`. Steps: parse the Bearer header; decode the unverified payload to read the tenant claim; get `tenant_mgt.auth_for_tenant(tenant)`; verify; the firebase-admin app is initialised from `IDP_PROJECT_ID`. Blocking firebase-admin calls run in a threadpool. Any failure (missing header, malformed token, bad signature, expired, wrong audience or issuer, `TenantIdMismatchError`, missing tenant claim) raises the app's `UNAUTHENTICATED` error mapped to HTTP 401 with a body that does not reveal the cause. Remove `src/auth/mock_users.py`, the `X-User-Id` reading and `python-jose` use (`src/auth/jwt.py`); the identity of a request is never read from any header other than `Authorization`.
