The benchmark script is committed and re-runnable with one command and exits non-zero if the template is unreachable.

tickets.title: Spike: Presidio latency and recall on synthetic corpus
tickets.summary: Measure Presidio en_core_web_sm latency and PII recall on the synthetic corpus.
tickets.description: Spike. No official figure exists (ADR-009). With presidio-analyzer 2.2.x and spaCy en_core_web_sm (PRESIDIO_SPACY_MODEL), run on (a) 500 synthetic advisor questions with injected PII (names, emails, phones, account numbers, national ids, addresses) and (b) 1000-char and 4000-char inputs. Record warm per-call p50/p95, cold-start time, memory, and per-entity recall and precision. Test pseudonymization round-trip (placeholders stable within a turn). Record as an ADR-009 addendum; propose INPUT_MAX_CHARS and the entity list/score threshold. Out of scope: wiring into chat.
acceptance_criteria: Given the 500-question set, when the benchmark runs, then per-entity recall and precision and latency p50/p95 are recorded in the ADR addendum.
If overall recall on injected PII is below 0.90 the ADR lists the missed entity classes and a mitigation (custom recognizer or lower threshold); the verdict is stated either way.
The proposed INPUT_MAX_CHARS is justified by the 4000-char latency measurement.

tickets.title: Spike: Sonnet 5.5 prompt-cache hit behaviour with versioned tools
tickets.summary: Measure prompt-cache hits for system prompt plus tools on claude-sonnet-5-5.
tickets.description: Spike. Using the Anthropic SDK against claude-sonnet-5-5 (cache minimum 512 tokens per ADR-006), put cache_control on the end of tools+system and send 20 sequential and 20 concurrent requests with varying tenant/user/date text after the breakpoint. Record cache_read_input_tokens vs cache_creation_input_tokens, hit rate, TTFT with and without hit, and show that changing one tool definition invalidates the cache. Repeat once for claude-sonnet-4-6 (1,024-token minimum) to feed the fallback. Record as an ADR-006 addendum. Out of scope: the production LLMClient.
acceptance_criteria: Given 20 sequential requests with a stable prefix, when run, then the hit rate and cache_read tokens are recorded and the ADR states whether the prefix reaches the 512-token minimum.
Given one tool definition is edited, when the next request is sent, then cache_read_input_tokens is 0 and cache_creation is >0; the result is recorded.
TTFT p50 with hit and without hit are both recorded.

tickets.title: Add E4 settings keys and the stable error-code mapping
tickets.summary: Typed Settings for E4 keys and a single error-code to HTTP/SSE mapping with fixed messages.
tickets.description: Add to the pydantic-settings Settings class (6.6), no secret default, missing required key fails boot: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, LLM_MODEL_ANSWER, LLM_MODEL_AUX, LLM_MODEL_FALLBACK, LLM_FALLBACK_ENABLED(false), LLM_MAX_ITERATIONS(3), LLM_MAX_TOKENS, LLM_TIMEOUT_S, LLM_RETRIES, LLM_BREAKER_*, PROMPT_VERSION, INPUT_MAX_CHARS, MODEL_ARMOR_TEMPLATE, MODEL_ARMOR_TIMEOUT_MS(500), MODEL_ARMOR_FAIL_OPEN(false), PRESIDIO_SPACY_MODEL, TENANT_TOKEN_BUDGET, TENANT_MAX_CONCURRENCY, SSE_HEARTBEAT_S, SSE_REPLAY_TTL_S, TURN_LEASE_S, HISTORY_MAX_TURNS(6), HISTORY_MAX_TOKENS(3000), EVAL_SAMPLE_RATE. Values marked 'set in E4' come from the spikes and are documented in .env.example. Implement guardrails error mapping (6.1): UNAUTHENTICATED 401, FORBIDDEN 403, INPUT_TOO_LONG 413, INPUT_BLOCKED, GUARD_UNAVAILABLE, RATE_LIMITED 429 with Retry-After, TENANT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED, LLM_UNAVAILABLE, RETRIEVAL_UNAVAILABLE, TURN_INTERRUPTED, IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED 409, INTERNAL. HTTP error body is {"error":{"code","message","request_id","retryable"}} with a fixed message per code, never exception text. Replaces the MVP src/errors.py behaviour that leaks exceptions.
acceptance_criteria: Given a missing required key, when Settings loads, then boot raises (unit test per key group).

Given each exception class raised in a handler, when mapped, then the response body has the stable code and the fixed message and contains no substring of the exception text (parametrized test over every code).
X-Request-Id from Kong is echoed in error.request_id (test).

tickets.title: LLMClient: streaming, timeouts, jittered retries, config-only models
tickets.summary: In-process LLMClient over the Anthropic SDK with streaming, timeouts and retries.
tickets.description: Implement src/llm (ADR-005). stream(messages, tools, system, model=None) yields normalized events (text delta, tool_use, usage, stop_reason). Explicit connect/read timeouts from LLM_TIMEOUT_S; retries LLM_RETRIES with exponential backoff and full jitter on 429/5xx/overloaded/connection errors only (never on 4xx other than 429); max_tokens=LLM_MAX_TOKENS always set; model ids only from Settings; base URL from ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. The request builder must never send temperature, top_p or top_k (removed 2026-10-21, 400). Replaces LiteLLM use in the MVP (litellm/ dir out of scope to delete unless E1 owns it). Out of scope: breaker, fallback, caching.
acceptance_criteria: Given a stubbed 529 twice then 200, when streaming, then exactly 3 attempts are made with sleeps drawn from the jitter range (seeded test).
Given a 400 response, when streaming, then no retry occurs and LLM_UNAVAILABLE-mappable error is raised.
Given any request, when captured at the HTTP layer, then the body has no temperature, top_p or top_k keys and has max_tokens (test).
Given no hardcoded model string in src/llm, a grep-based test fails if a literal 'claude-' id appears outside config/tests.

tickets.title: LLMClient: circuit breaker and eval-gated same-provider fallback
tickets.summary: Add a circuit breaker and a fallback to LLM_MODEL_FALLBACK only when LLM_FALLBACK_ENABLED is true.
tickets.description: Extend LLMClient. Breaker params from LLM_BREAKER_* (failure threshold, window, open duration, half-open probes); when open, calls fail fast with LLM_UNAVAILABLE. Fallback: after primary exhausts retries or the breaker is open, if and only if LLM_FALLBACK_ENABLED is true, retry once on LLM_MODEL_FALLBACK (claude-sonnet-4-6; same provider only, never another vendor); the usage record carries the model actually used. Fallback has its own prompt cache and 1,024-token minimum (use spike result). Config default false until the eval gate passes (E7). Quote ADR-005: 'same-provider fallback only ... enabled only if it passes the eval gate'.
acceptance_criteria: Given primary forced to fail and LLM_FALLBACK_ENABLED=false, when streaming, then LLM_UNAVAILABLE is raised and the fallback model is never called (test).
Given primary forced to fail and LLM_FALLBACK_ENABLED=true, when streaming, then the fallback model is used and usage.model equals LLM_MODEL_FALLBACK; no temperature/top_p/top_k sent.
Given N consecutive failures, when the breaker opens, then the next call fails without a network request until the open duration passes (fake clock test); half-open success closes it.

tickets.title: LLMClient: prompt caching, versioned tools, model retirement check
tickets.summary: Cache system prompt plus tools, version them with PROMPT_VERSION and fail readiness on retired models.
tickets.description: Place cache_control at the end of tools then system (cache order tools, system, messages); tenant/user/date text only in messages after the breakpoint. Tool definitions and system prompt are built by one function keyed on PROMPT_VERSION; a test hashes them so a change without a PROMPT_VERSION bump fails CI. Apply the spike (E4-T3) result: if the prefix is under the model minimum, log a warning with token count. Add a retirement table (model id -> retirement date) in config and a check used by /readyz (model availability item, 6.1) and a CI test that fails when a configured model is retired or retires within 30 days. Record cache_read/creation tokens in usage. Quote ADR-006: 'tool definitions are versioned with the prompt because changing them invalidates the cache'.
acceptance_criteria: Given two consecutive requests with the same prefix against the stub, when built, then the system/tools blocks are byte-identical and carry cache_control; tenant/user/date text appears only after the breakpoint (test).
Given a tool schema edited without a PROMPT_VERSION bump, when CI runs, then the hash test fails.
Given LLM_MODEL_ANSWER set to a retired id, when /readyz is called, then it reports not ready; and the CI retirement test fails for a model retiring within 30 days.
Usage events include cache_read_input_tokens and cache_creation_input_tokens.

tickets.title: Guard-in: input cap and Presidio pseudonymization
tickets.summary: Cap input length and pseudonymize PII before embed, LLM, traces and logs.
tickets.description: In src/guardrails: reject over INPUT_MAX_CHARS with INPUT_TOO_LONG (413) before any other work; Presidio AnalyzerEngine (spaCy PRESIDIO_SPACY_MODEL=en_core_web_sm, loaded once per process at startup, entity list/threshold from spike E4-T2) returns the redacted text plus a placeholder map held only in request memory. The redacted text is the only text passed to embedding, Model Armor, LLM, Langfuse, OTel attributes and logs. Replace the MVP src/pii fallback. Quote ADR-009: 'Presidio in-process pseudonymization ... before embed / LLM / traces / logs'. Out of scope: output redaction.
acceptance_criteria: Given a question containing an email, a phone number and a person name, when guard-in runs, then the returned text has none of them and contains typed placeholders (unit test).
Given input of INPUT_MAX_CHARS+1, when guard-in runs, then INPUT_TOO_LONG is raised before the Presidio engine is invoked (mock call count 0).
Given the benchmark corpus from E4-T2, recall is at least the value recorded in the ADR (regression test with threshold).
Warm p95 latency on a 1000-char input stays within the ADR-recorded bound (marked perf test).

tickets.title: Model Armor input screen client, fail closed
tickets.summary: Screen redacted input via Model Armor with a 500 ms timeout that fails closed.
tickets.description: Client in src/guardrails calling Model Armor sanitizeUserPrompt with MODEL_ARMOR_TEMPLATE on the redacted text; timeout MODEL_ARMOR_TIMEOUT_MS (500). Verdict match -> INPUT_BLOCKED (not an LLM call, SSE error or HTTP per 6.1). Timeout, 5xx or auth error -> GUARD_UNAVAILABLE and the turn stops, unless MODEL_ARMOR_FAIL_OPEN is true (default false; boot warns in prod profile if true). The screen runs concurrently (asyncio.gather) with the Voyage embed; if the screen blocks or fails, the embed result is discarded and no retrieval SQL runs. The REST API only detects; the app acts (ADR-009). Use verdict/latency findings from E4-T1.
acceptance_criteria: Given Model Armor stubbed to delay 600 ms, when screened, then GUARD_UNAVAILABLE is returned at about 500 ms and no retrieval call is made (test with timing assertion <700 ms).
Given a blocked verdict, when screened, then INPUT_BLOCKED is raised and neither Anthropic nor DB retrieval is called.
Given the embed and screen stubs each sleeping 300 ms, when run together, then total wall time is under 450 ms (concurrency test).
Given MODEL_ARMOR_FAIL_OPEN=false and a 5xx, the result is GUARD_UNAVAILABLE (never pass-through).

tickets.title: Tool dispatcher: JSON tool_result, validation, max iterations
tickets.summary: Dispatch the four tools with Pydantic validation, JSON-encoded results and no exception text.
tickets.description: In src/agent/tools, per 6.3: unknown tool names rejected; arguments validated by Pydantic models (search_firm_kb top_k bounded; lookup_product_factsheet product_name; lookup_suitability_rule product_category and enum client_risk_profile); no tool accepts tenant, tier, jurisdiction or licenses (tests assert the schemas lack those fields); output is model_dump_json(); failures return {"error_code": ...} with no exception text; iterations capped at LLM_MAX_ITERATIONS (3). Retrieved text only ever appears in a tool_result block, never in system. Tools call the E3 services (search_firm_kb, factsheet, suitability) through RetrievalService(principal); this ticket does not reimplement them. Tool definitions registered for the prompt-cache builder (E4-T7).
acceptance_criteria: Given a tool call with an unknown name, when dispatched, then the result is {"error_code":"UNKNOWN_TOOL"} and no service is called.
Given a tool raising ValueError('secret sql'), when dispatched, then the tool_result JSON contains error_code and the string 'secret sql' appears nowhere in it (test).
Given every tool's JSON schema, when inspected, then no property named tenant_id, tier, jurisdiction or licenses exists.
Given a model that requests tools 4 times, when the loop runs, then it stops after 3 iterations.

tickets.title: CitationVerifier implementation and server citation events
tickets.summary: Deterministic verifier: every [n] in retrieved chunk ids with quote overlap; server emits citation events.
tickets.description: Implement the CitationVerifier Protocol defined in E3 (the cache hit path in E3-T14 already depends on it). Rules (ADR-009, 8.1 LLM05): every [n] in the answer maps to a retrieved chunk of this turn (id set from the retrieval result); a cited claim must overlap the chunk text by a deterministic quote/token-overlap threshold (threshold a config value tuned in evals, default documented). On accept, build the SSE 'citation' event {index, chunk_id, source_title, regulatory_ref, last_reviewed_at, stale, excerpt}; excerpt passes through the output redactor (G-16); stale is computed server-side. The model never emits citation events itself. Verifier failure behaviour: drop the uncited sentence marker and set finish_reason accordingly or return refusal; choose per arch (see questions). Uses retrieval.fetch_chunks(ids) for chunk data.
acceptance_criteria: Given an answer citing [4] when retrieved ids map only to 1..3, when verified, then it is rejected and no citation event is emitted (verifier test).
Given an answer whose [n] set is a subset of retrieved chunks and with quote overlap above threshold, when verified, then one citation event per distinct n is returned with a redacted excerpt.
Given a chunk excerpt containing an email, when the event is built, then the excerpt contains no email (test).
Property test: for random answers, every [n] present in emitted citation events is in the retrieved chunk-id set.

tickets.title: Sentence-buffered output PII redaction
tickets.summary: Buffer streamed text to sentence boundaries and redact PII before emitting delta events.
tickets.description: In src/guardrails: wrap the LLM text stream; accumulate until a sentence boundary (or max buffer length to bound latency, config), run Presidio on the sentence (and restore pseudonym placeholders only if arch allows; default: leave redacted), then emit. Flush remaining buffer at end of stream. Must handle [n] markers split across chunks without breaking them. Quote ADR-009: 'sentence-buffered output PII redaction ... adds a small latency to first visible tokens'. Record the added first-delta latency in the PR.
acceptance_criteria: Given a stream chunked mid-sentence containing an email split across two chunks, when redacted, then no emitted delta contains the email in full or in part (test).
Given a stream ending without a final period, when finished, then the remaining text is flushed (test).
Given the marker '[1' and '2]' split across chunks, when processed, then the emitted text contains '[12]' unchanged or '[1]' per original (no corruption; parametrized test).
Added latency before first delta is measured on a stub and reported; test fails if the buffer exceeds the configured max.

tickets.title: turn_events store and SSE v2 event encoding
tickets.summary: Persist ordered events per turn and encode them as SSE with ids and a client-safe schema.
tickets.description: Define event models (6.2): turn, meta, tool, delta, citation, refusal, error, done with exact data shapes; encode as 'id: <seq>\nevent: <name>\ndata: <json>'. Implement an EventSink that assigns strictly increasing seq per turn (turn at seq 0), inserts into turn_events (table from E1 schema; if absent see questions) in short transactions, batching delta events (documented interval) so the DB is not hit per token, and sends heartbeat comment lines every SSE_HEARTBEAT_S. Client-visible events are built only from these models: tool events carry tool name, status, tool_use_id; no payloads, inputs or exception text (G-04); error events carry {code, retryable} only. Do not make DB calls while holding a stream open longer than a short tx.
acceptance_criteria: Given events of every type are emitted in a test turn, when serialized, then none contains tool input/output payloads or exception text (test over all event types with a poisoned tool result and exception).
Given a turn, when events are persisted, then seq is 0,1,2,... strictly increasing with no gaps and turn is seq 0.
Given SSE_HEARTBEAT_S=1 and no events for 3 s, when streaming, then at least 2 comment lines ': hb' are sent.
Delta batching: 1000 token deltas produce fewer than 1000 inserts (assert insert count).

tickets.title: POST /v1/chat with Idempotency-Key and replay
tickets.summary: Idempotent chat endpoint: same key and body replays, different body returns 409.
tickets.description: POST /v1/chat requires header Idempotency-Key and body {conversation_id?, message}. turn_id derived from the Idempotency-Key (deterministic, per principal/tenant namespace). Short tx: insert turn_events seq 0 ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING plus store a request-body hash with the turn; if the row existed with the same hash, stream a replay of persisted events (then tail until done) instead of generating; a different hash returns 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED. Missing header -> 400 with a stable code. Auth and principal first. Streams text/event-stream; Kong passes it unbuffered. Orchestrator call is a stub interface here (implemented in the orchestrator tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Given the same Idempotency-Key and body sent twice, when the second arrives, then the LLM stub is called once and the second response replays identical events (test counting stub calls).
Given the same key with a different body, when posted, then status is 409 with code IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED.
Given two concurrent requests with the same key, when both arrive, then exactly one generation runs (race test).
Given a different tenant using the same key string, when posted, then it is a distinct turn (no cross-tenant replay).

tickets.title: GET /v1/chat/{turn_id}/events resume and TURN_INTERRUPTED
tickets.summary: Resume a dropped stream from Last-Event-ID, tail to done, and detect dead producers.
tickets.description: Endpoint (6.1/6.2): owner of the turn only (403/404 otherwise, RLS-scoped); header Last-Event-ID; replay turn_events with seq > Last-Event-ID, then tail (poll or LISTEN, documented) until done; heartbeat as in E4-T13. If the last persisted event is older than TURN_LEASE_S and no done/error exists, append once error {code: TURN_INTERRUPTED, retryable: true} and end; the append must be idempotent across concurrent resumers. Events older than SSE_REPLAY_TTL_S are no longer replayable (410 or documented code).
acceptance_criteria: Given a turn of 20 events and a client that disconnects after seq 7, when it reconnects with Last-Event-ID 7, then it receives exactly seq 8..N with no duplicates or gaps (test).
Given the producer stops and TURN_LEASE_S passes, when two resumers connect concurrently, then exactly one TURN_INTERRUPTED error row exists in turn_events.
Given another advisor's turn_id, when requested, then no events are returned (403/404 test).
Given Last-Event-ID absent, the stream starts from seq 0.

tickets.title: Conversations and messages persistence with history window
tickets.summary: Persist conversations/messages and load the last 6 turns within 3k tokens.
tickets.description: Repository in src/agent (using E1 tables conversations and messages, monthly range partitions, columns incl. retrieval_degraded and citations (redacted)). Functions: create/get conversation (owner = principal), insert user message (redacted text only) and assistant message, load history = last HISTORY_MAX_TURNS turns trimmed to HISTORY_MAX_TOKENS (token count method documented), soft delete via DELETE /v1/conversations/{id} (204), GET /v1/conversations and /messages with cursor. All in short, tenant-scoped transactions. Stored text is the redacted text.
acceptance_criteria: Given 10 prior turns, when history loads, then at most 6 turns are returned and total tokens <= 3000 (test with a long-turn fixture).
Given another advisor's conversation id, when GET messages, then 404/403 (RLS test).
Given DELETE then GET, the conversation is excluded and returns 204 once.
Given a user message containing PII, the stored content equals the redacted text (test).

tickets.title: Follow-up condensation with Haiku
tickets.summary: Rewrite a follow-up into a standalone query only when history exists.
tickets.description: When history is non-empty, call LLMClient with LLM_MODEL_AUX (claude-haiku-5-5), small max_tokens, input = redacted history + redacted question, output = standalone redacted question used for embed/retrieval/cache key. No history -> no call. Failure or timeout falls back to the original question (not an error). Output re-passes the guard-in redactor. No temperature/top_p/top_k.
acceptance_criteria: Given empty history, when preparing a turn, then the aux LLM stub is called 0 times.
Given history and the stub returning a rewritten query, when prepared, then retrieval receives the rewritten query.
Given the aux call timing out, when prepared, then the original question is used and the turn continues.
Given a rewritten query containing an email, then it is redacted before use (test).

tickets.title: Orchestrator pre-LLM stages: cache, screen+embed, retrieval, gate
tickets.summary: Retrieve-first pipeline up to the gate, with the meta event and refusal path.
tickets.description: src/agent orchestrator order (4.5, Flow 1): guard-in (cap, Presidio) -> condensation (if history) -> answer_cache lookup (E3-T13/T14 store, key from the normalized redacted question; hit re-fetches via fetch_chunks, re-runs the CitationVerifier, a miss on invisible chunk) -> on miss: Model Armor screen in parallel with Voyage embed -> RetrievalService search+rerank+gate (E3) in short transactions -> emit 'meta' {retrieval_degraded, reason?} once after rerank and store messages.retrieval_degraded. Gate failure emits 'refusal' {NO_FIRM_DOCUMENTATION, escalate_offer} then done(finish_reason gate) with no LLM call. Cache hit path emits delta/citation events from the verified cached answer and skips screen and embed. Failures map to one error event with a code (RETRIEVAL_UNAVAILABLE etc). Cache write after a verified, non-escalating turn is in the next ticket's persist step.
acceptance_criteria: Given the gate stub failing, when a turn runs, then events are turn, meta, refusal, done(gate) and the LLM stub is called 0 times.
Given the reranker stub returning 429, when run, then meta.retrieval_degraded is true with reason rerank_429 and the stored messages.retrieval_degraded is true (equality test across both).
Given a cache hit, when run, then Model Armor and Voyage stubs are called 0 times and chunks are fetched via fetch_chunks.
Given a cache hit citing a chunk no longer visible to the principal, then it behaves as a miss.
Given Model Armor timeout, the turn ends with error GUARD_UNAVAILABLE and no retrieval SQL.

tickets.title: Orchestrator LLM loop: streaming with tools, verifier and redaction
tickets.summary: One streaming LLM call with tools, max 3 iterations, wired to verifier and output redaction.
tickets.description: After the gate passes (parent expansion and staleness via E3), inject retrieval as a JSON-encoded tool_result for a synthetic search_firm_kb tool_use, then stream via LLMClient with tools (4 tools, E4-T10 dispatcher), prompt cache (E4-T7) and the versioned system prompt (update MVP src/agent/system_prompt.py: no secrets or tenant data, 'today' and tenant/user text after the cache breakpoint, instruct citing with [n]). Emit 'tool' events (name/status/tool_use_id) on tool_use start and result; text goes through sentence-buffered redaction to 'delta'; when the answer completes (or per sentence), the CitationVerifier runs and citation events are emitted; verifier rejection handled per questions. Max LLM_MAX_ITERATIONS. finish_reason in (end_turn, max_tokens, refusal, gate). LLM failures after breaker/fallback -> error LLM_UNAVAILABLE.
acceptance_criteria: Given the LLM stub citing [n] not in retrieved ids, when the turn runs, then no citation event for that n is emitted and the verifier outcome is recorded (end-to-end verifier test).
Given a tool raising an exception with sensitive text, then no emitted event or tool_result contains that text.
Given the LLM stub requesting tools forever, then the loop stops at 3 iterations and done is emitted.
Given the retrieved text contains 'ignore previous instructions', it appears only inside a tool_result block in the captured Anthropic request, never in system (test).
Delta events contain no PII injected in the stubbed answer.

tickets.title: escalate_to_compliance persistence and GET /v1/escalations
tickets.summary: Persist escalations with server-side licenses and an outbox event; list endpoint.
tickets.description: Tool (6.3): input {reason, product_class}; licenses read from Principal/advisors.licenses (never tool args); insert into escalations (E1 table) and an outbox row in one transaction; returns {escalation_id, status:'pending_review'}; client sees tool name+status only (G-18). A turn that calls it is flagged side_effect so it is never written to answer_cache. GET /v1/escalations: compliance_officer sees tenant escalations, others only their own (RLS + role check). Reason text is redacted before persist.
acceptance_criteria: Given a tool call, when executed, then exactly one escalations row and one outbox row exist, in the same transaction (rollback test: failure of the outbox insert leaves no escalation).
Given an advisor with licenses X, the stored license snapshot equals advisors.licenses and any 'licenses' argument from the model is rejected by schema validation.
Given a non-officer, GET /v1/escalations returns only own rows; officer returns tenant rows; other tenant rows never appear.
Given a turn that escalated, the answer cache write is skipped (test).

tickets.title: Outbox writer and turn persist transaction
tickets.summary: Write chat.audit, chat.usage and sampled eval.sample outbox rows in the turn-persist transaction.
tickets.description: Module events (4.5): insert-only outbox writer taking the current transaction; no Kafka client or credentials in chat-api (import-linter contract + test). Turn persist = one short transaction: assistant message (retrieval_degraded, finish_reason, redacted citations), final turn_events flush, outbox rows chat.audit and chat.usage (tokens in/out, cache tokens, model used, latency, tenant) and, with probability EVAL_SAMPLE_RATE on completed turns, eval.sample.v1; answer_cache write (E3 store) when eligible (no side-effect tool, verifier passed). Payloads use redacted text only. Event schema names/versions follow the 6.4 topic catalogue (verify against it).
acceptance_criteria: Given a completed turn, when persisted, then one chat.audit and one chat.usage outbox row exist in the same transaction as the assistant message (kill-after-message test: no orphan rows).
Given EVAL_SAMPLE_RATE=1.0 an eval.sample row is written; at 0.0 none (seeded-RNG test).
Given chat-api code, importing a kafka client fails the import-linter contract.
Given PII in the stubbed answer, outbox payloads contain only redacted text (test).

tickets.title: Per-tenant token budget and concurrency limits
tickets.summary: Enforce TENANT_TOKEN_BUDGET and TENANT_MAX_CONCURRENCY before generation.
tickets.description: Before the LLM call, check the tenant's token usage against TENANT_TOKEN_BUDGET (window defined in questions; source: usage rows already written, no new infra unless arch lists one) and in-flight turns against TENANT_MAX_CONCURRENCY. Exceeded budget -> TENANT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED; concurrency -> RATE_LIMITED 429 with Retry-After. Concurrency slot released in finally. Both limits are per tenant, not per instance (state in Postgres or Valkey per questions).
acceptance_criteria: Given budget exhausted, when a turn starts, then error TENANT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED is returned and the LLM stub is called 0 times.
Given TENANT_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2 and 3 simultaneous turns, then the third gets 429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After; after one finishes a new turn is accepted.
Given a turn that raises, the concurrency slot is released (test).

tickets.title: Admin: PATCH /v1/admin/advisors/{id}
tickets.summary: Tenant admins update advisors directly, bumping entitlement_version with an outbox event.
tickets.description: Endpoint (6.1): role tenant_admin via principal; body {role?, tier?, jurisdictions?, licenses?, status?} validated; direct UPDATE advisors (policy allows tenant_admin only), bump entitlement_version, outbox AdvisorEntitlementChanged in the same transaction; own-tenant only (RLS). Takes effect within ENTITLEMENT_CACHE_TTL_S (no Kafka invalidation).
acceptance_criteria: Given a tenant_admin, when patching tier, then 200, entitlement_version increments by 1 and one outbox row exists.
Given a non-admin, then 403 FORBIDDEN and no row changes.
Given an advisor of another tenant, then 404 and no change (RLS test).
Given an invalid tier value, 422/400 with a stable code.

tickets.title: Admin: ACL change and delete requests with status endpoint
tickets.summary: ACL change/delete returns 202 and writes one acl_change_requests row plus one outbox row.
tickets.description: Endpoints (6.1, ADR-022): POST /v1/admin/documents/{id}/acl-changes {tier_required?, jurisdiction?} and DELETE /v1/admin/documents/{id} (action=delete), role tenant_admin; in one transaction insert acl_change_requests (pending) and outbox AclChangeRequested (acl.changes.v1) and return 202 {request_id}; validate that the document is visible to the admin's tenant by reading via RetrievalService (no write to content tables). GET /v1/admin/acl-changes/{request_id} returns {status: pending|applied|failed, applied_at}. The acl-applier worker is not in this epic. chat-api's DB role fa_app has no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on documents, chunks, suitability_rules.
acceptance_criteria: Given a tenant_admin POST, then 202 and exactly one acl_change_requests row and one outbox row are created in one transaction (count test; failure of outbox insert rolls back both).
Given a non-admin, 403 and zero rows.
Given the fa_app role, a privilege test asserts no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE grant on documents, chunks and suitability_rules (information_schema.role_table_grants query).
Given a request id of another tenant, GET status returns 404.

tickets.title: Leak tests: PII never reaches Voyage, Anthropic, logs, Langfuse
tickets.summary: End-to-end test that injected PII is absent from every outbound call, log line and trace.
tickets.description: Integration test: run the full orchestrator with stubs capturing (a) Voyage embed and rerank request bodies, (b) Anthropic requests incl. aux condensation, (c) Model Armor request, (d) captured log records and OTel/Langfuse span attributes, (e) outbox payloads and turn_events. Inject PII (email, phone, name, account number) in the question and in history. Assert none of the raw values appear anywhere; also assert client SSE events contain no tool payloads or exception text across all event types. Ensure Langfuse masking is wired if LANGFUSE_ENABLED (mask before export).
acceptance_criteria: Given PII in the question, when a turn runs, then a scan of all captured outbound bodies, logs, spans and outbox rows finds zero occurrences of the raw values (test fails if one leaks).
Given a poisoned tool exception text, the full SSE capture contains no part of it.
Given LANGFUSE_ENABLED=true with a capture exporter, span attributes contain redacted text only.

tickets.title: Resume, idempotency and failure end-to-end tests
tickets.summary: Integration tests for dropped connections, key reuse, fallback gating and meta consistency.
tickets.description: Add the epic's integration tests against a real Postgres: (1) drop the connection mid-stream, resume with Last-Event-ID, final event list equals an uninterrupted run; (2) same Idempotency-Key twice -> one LLM call; different body -> 409; (3) meta.retrieval_degraded equals messages.retrieval_degraded for degraded and non-degraded turns; (4) with primary forced to fail, fallback used only when LLM_FALLBACK_ENABLED is true; (5) Model Armor 500 ms timeout -> GUARD_UNAVAILABLE; (6) every emitted [n] is within retrieved chunk ids. Wire into CI.
acceptance_criteria: Test (1) fails if any event is missing or duplicated after resume.
Test (2) fails if the LLM stub call count is not 1, or the status is not 409 on a different body.
Test (3) fails if the two flags differ for either case.
Tests (4)-(6) fail as described in their assertions and run in CI on every PR.

tickets.title: TTFT benchmark on 10k-chunk corpus with a real LLM
tickets.summary: Measure TTFT p50/p95 against the overview 2.1 target and fail if above.
tickets.description: Script and CI-manual job: load the 10k-chunk synthetic corpus (E3-T16 fixture), real Voyage and Anthropic (claude-sonnet-5-5), Model Armor and Presidio on, prompt cache warm; run at least 200 turns including 30% follow-ups and a cache-hit mix reported separately. TTFT = request received to first delta event. Report p50/p95, stage breakdown (guard, embed/screen, retrieval, rerank, LLM first token). Targets from overview 2.1: p50 < 2.0 s, p95 < 3.5 s; script exits non-zero above them. Save results in the repo docs and an ADR note.
acceptance_criteria: Given the 10k corpus and real LLM, when the benchmark runs 200 turns, then p50 < 2.0 s and p95 < 3.5 s or the command exits non-zero.
The report lists per-stage p50/p95 so a regression is attributable.
Cache-hit and cache-miss turns are reported as separate distributions.

tickets.title: Spike: Docling on EDGAR 497K HTML and inline XBRL
tickets.summary: Measure Docling parse quality and Voyage token sizes on 497K filings and record the result as an ADR.
tickets.description: Arch (overview.md 4.14, Flow 2 notes): 'Docling on 497K and inline-XBRL tables is a spike (section 10).' Plan E6: 'Spikes first. Docling on the 497K HTML and inline-XBRL tables (chunk sizes measured with Voyage count_tokens).' Take a sample of at least 30 real EDGAR 497K filings (include some with inline-XBRL tables), parse each with Docling, chunk structure-aware (children 256-512 tokens, parents ~1k tokens per 4.7), and count tokens with the Voyage `count_tokens` API (EMBED_MODEL voyage-4). Measure per filing: parse seconds, peak memory, table fidelity (rows/cols preserved, hand-checked on 5), and the distribution (p50/p95/max) of child and parent token counts. Decide whether Docling is usable in-process in `etl-public` and what fallback is needed for tables (the arch names Document AI only as an OCR fallback). Write the result to `docs/adr/docling-497k.md` in the FinAdvisor repo with the measurements, the sample list (accession numbers), the decision and the pinned Docling version. The researcher copies it into decisions.md later. Out of scope: building the pipeline; fetching more than the sample (respect SEC access rules, declared User-Agent, rate limit under 10 req/s).
acceptance_criteria: `docs/adr/docling-497k.md` exists and contains a table of >=30 filings with parse time, peak memory and child/parent token p50/p95/max
The ADR states a keep/change decision for Docling and lists the pinned version; `grep -c 'Decision' docs/adr/docling-497k.md` >= 1
Child chunk token p95 is reported against the 512 limit and parent p95 against ~1k; any filing type exceeding them is listed
Spike script is committed under `backend/scripts/spikes/` and reruns with one command documented in the ADR

tickets.title: Scaffold the ETL package and daemon-less Dagster
tickets.summary: Create the etl package with a Dagster definitions module that materializes in a Cloud Run job and runs locally with dagster dev.
tickets.description: Arch (4.8, `etl` job): 'Daemon-less: `dagster asset materialize` in a Cloud Run job; run and event storage in Postgres (`dagster-postgres`, database `dagster` on the same Cloud SQL instance, owned by role `fa_dagster`, no access to app schemas); `dagster dev` locally.' Build: package `backend/src/etl/` with `definitions.py` (Dagster `Definitions`), `dagster.yaml` selecting `dagster-postgres` storage from config `DAGSTER_PG_DB`, `DAGSTER_PG_USER`, `DAGSTER_PG_PASSWORD` (defaults `dagster`, `fa_dagster`), a `jobs` entrypoint subcommand `etl` that runs `dagster asset materialize --select <assets> --partition <tenant|dt>`, and a multi-dimensional partition def (tenant x date). Pin dagster, dagster-postgres, docling, pandera, presidio versions in pyproject. Local: `dagster dev` uses SQLite/in-memory run storage from a dev config. Out of scope: any real asset logic (later tickets), the Cloud Run job resource and Scheduler (infra epic).
acceptance_criteria: Given a Postgres with the `dagster` database from E1-T3, when `jobs etl --select noop_asset --partition tenant=a|dt=2026-01-01` runs, then the run record exists in the `dagster` DB and exit code is 0 (integration test)
Given role `fa_dagster`, when it queries any app-schema table, then permission is denied (test)
`dagster dev` starts locally with `docker compose` Postgres absent (smoke test with the dev config)
No dagster-daemon or sensor process is required: `grep -r 'dagster-daemon' backend/ terraform/` returns nothing

tickets.title: Synthetic per-tenant corpus generator
tickets.summary: Generate a deterministic synthetic document corpus for each tenant, including suitability-rule documents.
tickets.description: Plan E6: 'Synthetic per-tenant corpus.' ADR-014 data input: synthetic per-tenant corpus plus a real public source. Existing seed data lives in `data/corpus/` (compliance_memos, jurisdiction_disclosures, product_factsheets, suitability_rules). Build `backend/src/etl/synthetic/` with a seeded generator `generate(tenant_slug, seed, n_docs)` writing documents to a local dir (HTML or Markdown) with fields: title, doc_type, jurisdiction, tier_required (1..4), regulatory_ref, last_reviewed_at, product_category, risk_level. Per tenant, include at least 3 suitability-rule documents covering the 3 client risk profiles (conservative, moderate, aggressive) and documents containing synthetic PII (names, emails, SSN-like strings) so the Presidio stage has something to scrub. Documents differ per tenant (tenant-specific names and thresholds) so cross-tenant leakage is detectable. Out of scope: uploading to GCS (E6-T4), real EDGAR data (E6-T13).
acceptance_criteria: Given the same seed twice, when the generator runs, then the output files have identical sha256 (test)
Given two tenants, when generated, then no document sha256 appears in both (test)
Each tenant corpus contains >=3 suitability-rule docs spanning conservative, moderate, aggressive (test counts by profile)
Each tenant corpus contains planted PII strings recorded in a sidecar manifest file used by E6-T5/T14 tests

tickets.title: Bronze asset: GCS by sha256, register documents, publish
tickets.summary: Fetch source documents into immutable GCS bronze, register a documents row and publish docs.bronze.v1.
tickets.description: Arch (4.8 `etl`; 4.10; Flow 2): 'Dagster run of tenant bronze assets (fetch, GCS by sha256, register `documents`, publish `docs.bronze.v1`)'. Bucket `GCS_DATA_BUCKET`, object `bronze/{tenant_id}/{sha256}` holding raw immutable bytes plus source URL and fetch time (object metadata); skip upload if the object exists. Register `documents` (5.2): `title, doc_type, jurisdiction, tier_required, regulatory_ref, last_reviewed_at, product_category, risk_level, source ('synthetic'|'edgar'), source_uri, bronze_uri, bronze_sha256, parser_version NULL, status 'active'`; unique `(tenant_id, bronze_sha256)` so re-registering is a no-op (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING). No `raw_content` anywhere. Publish `docs.bronze.v1` keyed by tenant_id with the E5 envelope via the E5 idempotent producer; payload carries ids and bronze_uri only, never text. Runs as DB role `fa_etl` with `app.tenant_id` set. Asset is partitioned tenant x dt. Source adapter for synthetic corpus from E6-T3. Out of scope: EDGAR source (E6-T13).
acceptance_criteria: Given a doc already in bronze, when the asset reruns, then no GCS write occurs and no new `documents` row (asserted by counting GCS puts and rows, integration with fake-gcs)
Given a new doc, when materialized, then exactly one `docs.bronze.v1` message with key == envelope.tenant_id and no content field is produced (test on payload schema)
Given `fa_etl` and tenant A context, when inserting a documents row for tenant B, then RLS denies it (test)
`documents` has no column named raw_content/content (reuse E1-T17 assertion passes)

tickets.title: Silver transform: Docling parse, Presidio scrub, chunking
tickets.summary: Implement the pure silver transform that turns a bronze document into redacted structure-aware chunks with token counts.
tickets.description: Arch (4.7 `silver`): 'Docling parse, Presidio scrub, structure-aware chunking (256-512-token children, ~1k-token parents, token counts from Voyage `count_tokens`)'. Build `etl/silver/transform.py`: `transform(doc_bytes, doc_meta) -> list[Chunk]` where Chunk has `kind` (child|parent), `chunk_index`, `parent_ref`, `content` (redacted), `section_path`, `token_count`, `chunk_hash` (sha256 of the redacted content plus section_path, stable across runs), plus ACL fields copied from the document (`tier_required, jurisdiction, regulatory_ref, last_reviewed_at, source_title`). Scrub with Presidio before anything is written (reuse `backend/src/pii/redactor.py` where it fits; pseudonymization is in-process, ADR-009). Use the chunk-size findings and Docling version from docs/adr/docling-497k.md. Voyage `count_tokens` is called through a thin injectable client so tests can fake it. Out of scope: Pandera, Parquet and Kafka (E6-T6/T7), headers (E6-T8).
acceptance_criteria: Given the planted-PII manifest from E6-T3, when a document is transformed, then no planted PII string appears in any chunk content (test)
Given a doc, when transformed twice, then the chunk_hash list is identical (test)
Child chunks have token_count in 256..512 except a final short chunk per section; parents <= 1100 (property test over the synthetic corpus)
Each child references a parent present in the output (test)

tickets.title: Pandera validation, ingest_rejects and silver Parquet
tickets.summary: Validate chunks with Pandera, route failures to ingest_rejects and write redacted silver Parquet partitioned by tenant and date.
tickets.description: Arch (4.7 `silver`, 5.2 `ingest_rejects`, 5.8): 'Pandera validation, rejects to `ingest_rejects`, writes silver Parquet to the data bucket under `silver/tenant_id=<id>/dt=<date>/`'. `ingest_rejects` columns: `(tenant_id, id)`, `document_id`, `bronze_sha256`, `stage`, `rule` (Pandera check), `detail` (redacted), `created_at`. Define a Pandera schema `ChunkSchema` (non-empty content, token_count within bounds, tier_required 1..4, jurisdiction in US/EU/UK, chunk_hash 64 hex, valid parent link, content free of detected PII entities via a re-scan). A failing row never goes to Parquet; one `ingest_rejects` row is written per failed check with `detail` redacted (no raw content) and the document-level outcome recorded. Write passing chunks as Parquet to `silver/tenant_id=<id>/dt=<date>/<document_id>.parquet`. Out of scope: consumer wiring (E6-T7).
acceptance_criteria: Given a chunk set with 3 deliberately invalid rows (empty content, tier 9, bad jurisdiction), when validated, then `ingest_rejects` gains exactly 3 rows with `rule` naming each check and none appear in the Parquet (test)
Given a rejected row, when `detail` is inspected, then it contains no substring of the original content longer than 20 chars (test)
Parquet path matches `silver/tenant_id=<id>/dt=<date>/` and a reader recovers the same chunk_hash set (test)
Re-running the same document writes the same Parquet object path without duplicating reject rows (unique-by-rule test)

tickets.title: silver worker role: consume bronze, emit silver
tickets.summary: Wire the silver transform into an E5 worker consumer that reads docs.bronze.v1 and emits docs.silver.v1.
tickets.description: Arch (4.7): role `silver` consumes `docs.bronze.v1`, writes silver Parquet and rejects, emits `docs.silver.v1`. Implement the handler on the E5 consumer framework (envelope check, `processed_events` dedupe in the sink transaction, retries, then `dlq.v1`, `app.tenant_id` set from the event key). Handler: read bronze bytes from GCS by `bronze_uri`, run E6-T5 transform and E6-T6 validation, update `documents.parser_version`, produce `docs.silver.v1` (ids and silver URI, no text). Register under `WORKER_ROLES=silver`. Per 4.7, an envelope with a PUBLIC tenant or key mismatch goes to `dlq.v1` (framework behaviour; assert it). Out of scope: framework itself (E5).
acceptance_criteria: Given a docs.bronze.v1 message, when consumed, then Parquet exists, `docs.silver.v1` is emitted once and `processed_events` has the event_id (integration)
Given the same message delivered twice, when consumed, then only one `docs.silver.v1` is emitted (test)
Given an envelope whose tenant_id differs from the key, when consumed, then it lands in `dlq.v1` with a reason and nothing is written (test)
Given a message for the PUBLIC tenant, when consumed by the silver role, then it goes to `dlq.v1` (test)

tickets.title: contextualizer: Haiku batch context headers behind a flag
tickets.summary: Generate contextual headers for chunks via the Haiku Batch API when CONTEXTUAL_RETRIEVAL_ENABLED is true.
tickets.description: Arch (4.7 `contextualizer`, ADR-016): 'Haiku 5.5 Batch API contextual headers (behind flag `CONTEXTUAL_RETRIEVAL_ENABLED`)', model `LLM_MODEL_AUX` (claude-haiku-5-5), input is redacted text only. Consume `docs.silver.v1`, read the silver Parquet, submit one Batch per document (the header prompt gets the redacted parent/section and the chunk), poll the batch, fill `context_header` on each child, emit `chunks.contextualized.v1` (ids, silver URI, no text). When the flag is false, pass chunks through with `context_header` NULL and make zero Anthropic calls. Header changes alter the text feeding `tsv`, but the embedding input and `chunk_hash` rules stay as the indexer defines (E6-T10). Batch failures retry then DLQ. Out of scope: suitability extraction (E6-T9), the L1 ablation that decides the flag default (E3-T16).
acceptance_criteria: Given the flag false, when a silver message is consumed, then `chunks.contextualized.v1` is emitted with null headers and the fake Anthropic client records 0 calls (test)
Given the flag true, when consumed, then each child chunk has a non-empty header and the request used the Batch API with `claude-haiku-5-5` (test on the fake client)
Given a request payload, when inspected, then it contains only redacted chunk text (scan test against planted PII manifest)
Given a failed batch, when retries are exhausted, then the message lands in `dlq.v1` (test)

tickets.title: Suitability-rule extraction, validation and lookup
tickets.summary: Extract suitability rules with Haiku structured output, validate them and write suitability_rules.
tickets.description: Arch (4.7 `contextualizer`; 5.2 `suitability_rules`; Flow 2): 'suitability-rule extraction (Haiku structured output, validated) into `suitability_rules`'. Columns: `rule_name, product_category, client_risk_profile` (CHECK conservative/moderate/aggressive), `min_tier_required`, `jurisdiction`, `regulatory_ref`, `rule_text` (redacted), `source_document_id` (composite FK), `extractor_model`, `validated_at`, `last_reviewed_at`. Run in the contextualizer for documents with `doc_type` indicating suitability rules; use a Pydantic output schema; validation rejects rows with an out-of-enum risk profile, tier outside 1..4, or missing regulatory_ref and records them in `ingest_rejects` (stage `suitability`) instead of inserting. Valid rows are upserted idempotently (key on tenant, source_document_id, rule_name, product_category, client_risk_profile). `validated_at` is set only on validated rows. Out of scope: the `lookup_suitability_rule` tool itself (E3-T11).
acceptance_criteria: Given the synthetic corpus for tenant A, when the pipeline completes, then `suitability_rules` has >=1 row for each of conservative, moderate, aggressive and every row has `validated_at` not null (integration)
Given a model output with risk profile 'reckless', when validated, then no row is inserted and an `ingest_rejects` row with stage 'suitability' exists (test)
Given a rerun, when extraction repeats, then the row count is unchanged (test)
Given a real DB with the corpus loaded, when E3's `lookup_suitability_rule('equities','moderate')` runs for tenant A, then it returns >=1 row (integration test)

tickets.title: indexer: hash-gated embed, upsert, supersede, corpus_version
tickets.summary: Implement the indexer role that embeds only new (tenant_id, chunk_hash, embed_model) chunks and bumps corpus_version.
tickets.description: Arch (4.7 `indexer`; Flow 2; 5.2 `chunks`): 'consumes `chunks.contextualized.v1`: Voyage `voyage-4` document embeddings only for chunks whose `(tenant_id, chunk_hash, embed_model)` is new, upserts `chunks`, deletes superseded chunks, then bumps the tenant's `corpus_version` (UPDATE on its own tenant row by policy), emits `chunks.indexed.v1`.' Use `EMBED_MODEL`/`EMBED_DIM` (voyage-4, 1024) and the E3-T3 embeddings client with `input_type='document'`. Per message in one transaction with `processed_events`: look up existing `(chunk_hash, embed_model)`; embed only the missing children (parents have NULL embedding); upsert with unique `(tenant_id, chunk_hash, embed_model)` (`ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` of ACL/metadata columns only, no re-embed); delete chunks of the document not in the new hash set; `UPDATE tenants SET corpus_version = corpus_version + 1` only if anything changed. Embedding calls batched. Runs as `fa_worker`. Out of scope: columns/indexes (E3-T4).
acceptance_criteria: Given a document ingested once, when the identical message is processed again, then the Voyage fake records 0 embed calls, `chunks` row count is unchanged and `corpus_version` is unchanged (test, count asserted)
Given a document with one paragraph edited, when reprocessed, then exactly the changed children are embedded and the superseded chunk rows are deleted (test asserts the embed call input count)
Given a first ingest, when processed, then `tenants.corpus_version` increases by exactly 1 per message with changes (test)
Given `fa_worker` in tenant A context, when it writes a chunk with tenant B id, then RLS denies it (test)

tickets.title: Partition replay and ACL-change tests with zero embed calls
tickets.summary: Prove that replaying a partition and an ACL metadata change cost no embeddings.
tickets.description: Plan E6 done-when: 'Re-running the same partition re-embeds zero unchanged chunks (count asserted); an ACL change updates metadata with zero embed calls.' Arch (Flow 2 notes): 'A backfill or re-embed is a replay: Dagster re-publishes `docs.bronze.v1` for the partition (bronze is immutable), and unchanged chunk hashes cost nothing.' Write an end-to-end test (compose: Postgres, Redpanda or the E5 test broker, fake GCS, fake Voyage/Anthropic) that (1) materializes tenant x dt through all stages, (2) re-materializes the same partition and asserts embed calls == 0, chunk count and `corpus_version` unchanged, (3) creates an `acl_change_requests` row (`update_acl`, new tier) with its outbox event, lets the E5 acl-applier apply it, and asserts `chunks.tier_required`/`documents.tier_required` updated with 0 embed calls. If the applier does not update the denormalised chunk columns, fix it here only within the ETL stages; the applier itself is E5. Out of scope: building the applier.
acceptance_criteria: Replay test: second materialization of the same partition yields 0 Voyage embed calls (counter asserted == 0) and an unchanged `chunks` count
ACL test: after the applier processes the change, every chunk of the document has the new `tier_required` and the Voyage counter delta == 0
The tests run in CI as part of the integration suite and fail if the indexer is changed to embed unconditionally (mutation check documented)

tickets.title: Dagster partitions and the etl job entrypoint
tickets.summary: Make tenant x dt partitions materialize end to end as one Cloud Run job invocation.
tickets.description: Arch (4.8 `etl`; Flow 2): 'trigger tenant x date partition' from Cloud Scheduler; 'Daemon-less'. Add the bronze asset (E6-T4) to the Dagster definitions with a static tenant partition set read from `tenants` (kind='firm') crossed with a daily partition; `jobs etl --tenant <slug> --dt <date>` (and `--backfill-from/--to`) materializes that partition and exits non-zero on failure; downstream stages are Kafka consumers so the job only produces `docs.bronze.v1`. Replays republish `docs.bronze.v1` for the partition without refetching. Role `fa_etl`. Out of scope: Terraform for Cloud Run job and Scheduler (infra epic).
acceptance_criteria: Given tenant slug and date, when `jobs etl --tenant a --dt 2026-01-01` runs, then only that partition's documents are published (test counts messages)
Given an invalid tenant slug, when run, then exit code != 0 and nothing is published (test)
Given `--backfill-from/--to` over 3 days, when run, then 3 partition runs are recorded in the dagster DB (integration)

tickets.title: etl-public: in-process EDGAR 497K pipeline as fa_etl_public
tickets.summary: Run all stages in-process for PUBLIC EDGAR 497K filings and publish only analytics events.
tickets.description: Arch (4.8 `etl-public`; Flow 2 notes; 4.7): 'runs every stage in-process and publishes only analytics topics (`ingest.analytics.v1`); the only writer of PUBLIC rows'; 'bumps the PUBLIC `corpus_version` itself'; 'worker consumers reject PUBLIC'. Build `jobs etl-public`: fetch 497K filings from EDGAR (declared User-Agent, rate limit under 10 req/s per SEC rules), bronze to `bronze/PUBLIC_TENANT_ID/{sha256}`, then call the same transform/validation/contextualize/embed functions from E6-T5..T10 in-process (no Kafka between stages), writing as DB role `fa_etl_public` with the PUBLIC tenant id, then bump PUBLIC `corpus_version`. Publish only `ingest.analytics.v1` events (counts, durations, reject counts; no text). Apply Docling decisions from docs/adr/docling-497k.md. Out of scope: schema of `ingest.analytics.v1` beyond what E5 defines (see questions).
acceptance_criteria: Given fa_etl_public, when the job ingests a fixture 497K filing, then `documents` and `chunks` rows exist with PUBLIC tenant id and PUBLIC `corpus_version` increased by 1 (integration)
Given role `fa_worker`, when it inserts a PUBLIC chunk, then the policy denies it (test)
Given a PUBLIC event published on `docs.bronze.v1`, when a worker consumer receives it, then it is sent to `dlq.v1` (test)
Given a run, when topics are inspected, then the only topic written is `ingest.analytics.v1` and no payload contains chunk text (scan test)

tickets.title: Raw-text scan test across documents, chunks, events, BigQuery
tickets.summary: Add a test that fails if raw document text exists anywhere except GCS bronze.
tickets.description: Plan E6 done-when: 'no raw document text exists outside GCS bronze (scan test of `documents`, `chunks`, events, BigQuery)'. Using the planted-PII manifest from E6-T3, run the full synthetic pipeline, then scan (a) every column of `documents`, `chunks`, `suitability_rules`, `ingest_rejects`, (b) every payload captured from pipeline topics, (c) the BigQuery tables fed by the pipeline (use the BQ emulator or recorded sink rows), for planted raw strings and for any substring of a bronze document body longer than a threshold. Also assert every Pandera failure in a seeded bad-input run has an `ingest_rejects` row. Out of scope: new product code, except fixing leaks found.
acceptance_criteria: Given the full pipeline run, when scanning all four stores, then 0 planted PII strings and 0 raw bronze substrings (>=40 chars) are found
Given a deliberately leaky stub (test-only toggle writing raw text into an event), when scanned, then the test fails (negative control)
Given a seeded bad-input run with N invalid rows, when finished, then `ingest_rejects` count for that run == N

tickets.title: dbt project and Postgres gold models as fa_dbt
tickets.summary: Create the dbt project with gold models documents_current, stale_documents and corpus_stats.
tickets.description: Arch (5.2 Gold layer; 4.8 `dbt`): 'Gold layer (dbt, `fa_dbt`, which owns schema `gold`...): models `gold.documents_current`, `gold.stale_documents` and `gold.corpus_stats`; views with `security_invoker = true`, or incremental models with a tenant predicate (never full-table rebuilds)'; 'per tenant run on a dedicated connection'. Create `dbt/` project with `dbt-postgres`; the three models as `security_invoker` views over RLS-protected tables (documents status='active' for current; stale = `last_reviewed_at` older than the staleness config; corpus_stats counts docs/chunks/tokens per tenant). Run per tenant via `jobs dbt --tenant <slug>` setting `app.tenant_id` on a dedicated connection. A custom materialization/post-hook sets `security_invoker = true`. Out of scope: BigQuery marts (E6-T18), CI assertions (E6-T16).
acceptance_criteria: Given tenants A and B, when dbt runs as fa_dbt for tenant A, then `gold.documents_current` returns only tenant A rows (integration)
Given the built views, when `pg_class.reloptions` is read, then each gold view has `security_invoker=true` (test)
Given a doc with `last_reviewed_at` > staleness limit, when queried, then it appears in `gold.stale_documents` (dbt test)
`dbt test` passes in CI against the compose Postgres

tickets.title: CI assertions: tenant tables RLS and no dbt full rebuild
tickets.summary: Add CI checks that every tenant-schema table has RLS and that dbt never full-rebuilds a tenant table.
tickets.description: Plan E6 done-when: 'dbt gold models pass the CI assertion that every tenant-schema table has RLS enabled, forced, with policies, and no dbt run does a full-table rebuild of a tenant table; only `fa_tenant_lookup` is `SECURITY DEFINER`.' Build a test script (pytest against compose Postgres after migrate + dbt run): (1) every table with a `tenant_id` column in the app schemas has `relrowsecurity` and `relforcerowsecurity` true and >=1 policy; (2) `pg_proc` has exactly one SECURITY DEFINER function, `fa_tenant_lookup` (extend, do not duplicate, E1-T17 if it exists); (3) a static check over dbt models that rejects `materialized='table'` for any model reading a tenant table, and a runtime check that no `DROP TABLE`/`CREATE TABLE AS` for tenant tables appears in the dbt run's executed SQL log. Gate in CI.
acceptance_criteria: Given a new table with tenant_id and no RLS, when the assertion runs, then it fails naming the table (negative test)
Given a dbt model with `materialized='table'` over `chunks`, when the check runs, then it fails (negative test)
Given the clean repo, when run, then the only SECURITY DEFINER function is `fa_tenant_lookup`
The checks are wired into the CI workflow and block merge

tickets.title: BigQuery dataset: partitioned tables, authorized views, row policies
tickets.summary: Create fa_analytics tables with day partitioning, tenant clustering, per-tenant authorized views and row access policies.
tickets.description: Arch (4.11, 5.8): dataset `fa_analytics`, tables `chat_audit`, `chat_usage`, `eval_events`, `gateway_audit`, `acl_changes`, `ingest_events`; 'day-partitioned, clustered by `tenant_id`; per-tenant authorized views (primary isolation) plus row access policies (second layer); `maximum_bytes_billed` on every query'; 'redacted text only'. Implement DDL as code in the repo (`bigquery/` SQL or Python module `etl/bq/schema.py`, applied by an idempotent `jobs`-callable command) with `BQ_DATASET` and `BQ_MAX_BYTES_BILLED`; partition by `DATE(event_time)` with `require_partition_filter`; cluster by `tenant_id`; per-tenant authorized view created on tenant onboarding (a function `ensure_tenant_view(tenant_id)`) in a separate views dataset, authorized on the base dataset; a row access policy per tenant as second layer. All query helpers pass `maximum_bytes_billed=BQ_MAX_BYTES_BILLED`. Out of scope: the bq-sink writer, onboarding hook wiring beyond a callable function.
acceptance_criteria: Given the applied DDL, when table metadata is read, then each of the 6 tables has `time_partitioning.type=DAY` and `clustering_fields[0]=='tenant_id'` (test against BQ emulator or real test dataset)
Given rows for tenants A and B, when a query runs through tenant A's authorized view, then only tenant A rows return (integration)
Given a client helper, when a query is built, then `maximum_bytes_billed` equals `BQ_MAX_BYTES_BILLED` and a query without it is rejected by the wrapper (unit test)
Running the DDL command twice is a no-op (idempotency test)

tickets.title: dbt-bigquery marts and ingest_events feed
tickets.summary: Build dbt-bigquery marts over fa_analytics and land ingest analytics events into ingest_events.
tickets.description: Arch (4.11, 4.8 `dbt`, 5.8): 'Marts are built by `dbt-bigquery`'; 'bq-sink: consumes audit, usage, eval, ingest and ACL topics; writes BigQuery with event-id dedupe' (bq-sink framework is E5; PUBLIC analytics events are exempt from the envelope check). Add a dbt-bigquery target with incremental, partition-aware marts (e.g. daily ingest summary per tenant from `ingest_events`, rejects per rule per day) using insert_overwrite on day partitions, `maximum_bytes_billed` set in the profile, and a `partition_filter` on every source read. Implement the `ingest_events` row mapping for `ingest.analytics.v1` and the ingest topic events so the E5 bq-sink role can write them with event-id dedupe. Out of scope: chat/eval/gateway marts (other epics) and the sink framework.
acceptance_criteria: Given duplicate `ingest.analytics.v1` events with the same event_id, when mapped and written twice, then `ingest_events` has one row (test)
Given the dbt-bigquery profile, when parsed, then `maximum_bytes_billed` is set and equals `BQ_MAX_BYTES_BILLED` (test)
Given a mart run twice over the same day, when finished, then the row count equals the first run (no duplicates, no full-table rewrite: query log shows only that day partition)
A PUBLIC analytics event is written with PUBLIC tenant id and visible only to the PUBLIC view (test)

tickets.title: BigQuery tenant isolation and byte-cap acceptance test
tickets.summary: Prove tenant views isolate rows and queries are capped.
tickets.description: Plan E6 done-when: 'BigQuery tables are day-partitioned, clustered by `tenant_id`, with `maximum_bytes_billed` set; a tenant's authorized view returns only that tenant's rows.' Add a test that provisions two tenants' views from E6-T17, inserts rows for both, and checks (1) tenant A's view never returns B's rows including via `SELECT *`, filters on B's id and a join on the base dataset (denied for tenant A's principal), (2) a deliberately large scan exceeding `BQ_MAX_BYTES_BILLED` is rejected with `bytesBilledLimitExceeded`, (3) table metadata partitioning and clustering. Runs in CI against the emulator, and a gated job against a real test project if the emulator cannot enforce authorized views (record which in the test docs).
acceptance_criteria: Tenant A principal selecting from tenant A's view returns 0 rows with tenant_id != A (assertion on result set)
Tenant A principal querying the base table directly is denied (test)
A query estimated above `BQ_MAX_BYTES_BILLED` fails with `bytesBilledLimitExceeded`

tickets.title: Spike: calibrate the Haiku judge against ~30 human labels
tickets.summary: Measure Cohen's kappa between the Haiku 5.5 judge and ~30 human labels and record whether L2 numbers can be trusted.
tickets.description: Spike (must finish before any L2 number is trusted). Build a calibration set of ~30 (question, answer, cited excerpts) items drawn from the existing data/eval/golden_qa.json and a few saved model answers, each with a human label for faithfulness (pass/fail) and citation correctness (pass/fail) stored in data/eval/judge_calibration.json (labels entered by the operator; the ticket supplies the file schema, a labelling CLI `python -m scripts.label_calibration`, and the runner). Run the judge (`LLM_MODEL_JUDGE` = claude-haiku-5-5, must differ from `LLM_MODEL_ANSWER`) with the existing data/eval/judge_prompt.txt as the starting prompt, in both A/B and swapped order where the prompt is pairwise (MT-Bench swap-order check). Compute Cohen's kappa per metric. Write the result to docs/adr/judge-calibration.md with: n, kappa per metric, confusion matrix, prompt version, and a go/no-go statement. Quote ADR-017: "Haiku 5.5 judge ... calibrated on ~30 human labels (Cohen's kappa)"; trigger to revisit: "Judge kappa below acceptable". Out of scope: the Ragas runner (E7-T8), choosing a different judge model (a no-go result is reported, not fixed here).
acceptance_criteria: Given the ~30 labelled items, `python -m scripts.calibrate_judge` prints kappa for faithfulness and citation and exits 0; a unit test with a fixed fake judge and known labels asserts the kappa value equals the hand-computed value (e.g. 0.6) to 3 decimals.
docs/adr/judge-calibration.md exists in the repo and contains n >= 30, a kappa value per metric, the judge model id and the prompt file hash; a CI check (grep test) fails if any of these is missing.
Unit test: the calibration runner raises if LLM_MODEL_JUDGE equals LLM_MODEL_ANSWER.
The ADR states an explicit threshold used for go/no-go and the decision (go or no-go) next to the measured kappa.

tickets.title: Define the golden-set schema and loader with tenant parameters
tickets.summary: Give the golden set a validated, tenant-parameterised schema and migrate the existing 50-or-fewer cases into it.
tickets.description: The repo already has data/eval/golden_qa.json and scripts/run_eval.py (MVP). Define a Pydantic model `GoldenCase` {id, category (answerable, adversarial, refusal, cross_tenant, tier, jurisdiction), question, persona (advisor tier, jurisdictions, licenses, role as a template, never a hard-coded tenant id), tenant_param (placeholder resolved to the `eval` tenant via `EVAL_TENANT_ID` at run time), expected_chunk_ids or expected_doc_refs (for L1), must_cite_refs, must_not_contain, expected_refusal (code or null), reference_answer (optional, for Ragas), notes}. Add a loader `load_golden(path)` that validates every case, rejects duplicate ids and unknown categories, and resolves tenant parameters. Convert the existing cases to the schema (target: 50 cases at this ticket). Quote ADR-017: "Golden set 50 growing to ~300, tenant-parameterised." Out of scope: adding cases beyond 50 (E7-T3), runners.
acceptance_criteria: Given a golden file with a duplicate id, `load_golden` raises ValueError naming the id (unit test).
Given a case with a hard-coded tenant uuid instead of the placeholder, validation fails (unit test).
`pytest backend/tests/test_golden_set.py` passes and asserts the shipped file holds >= 50 cases covering every category name at least once except where E7-T3 adds them.
With EVAL_TENANT_ID set to uuid X, every resolved case reports tenant_id == X (unit test).

tickets.title: Add adversarial, refusal and leak-probe cases to the golden set
tickets.summary: Extend the golden set with adversarial, refusal, and cross-tenant / tier / jurisdiction probe cases.
tickets.description: Add at least 40 cases to the golden set: prompt-injection attempts in the question and in retrieved text, requests the system must refuse (no firm documentation -> NO_FIRM_DOCUMENTATION refusal, out-of-jurisdiction, above-tier content), and cross-tenant probes (a question whose only matching content belongs to another tenant, so the right answer is a refusal and no foreign chunk id may appear). Each case sets expected_refusal or must_not_contain. Add seed fixtures (a second synthetic tenant with distinct content, plus restricted-tier and other-jurisdiction documents inside the `eval` tenant) under data/eval/fixtures/ so that probes have something to leak. Quote ADR-017 L3: "cross-tenant / tier / jurisdiction refusal and promptfoo red team" and OWASP table LLM01/LLM08 tests. Out of scope: the runner that executes them (E7-T10).
acceptance_criteria: `pytest backend/tests/test_golden_set.py` asserts >= 40 cases in categories adversarial, refusal, cross_tenant, tier, jurisdiction, with at least 5 in each.
Test asserts every cross_tenant case names a foreign-tenant chunk id in a `forbidden_chunk_ids` field that exists in the fixtures.
Loading the fixtures into a test database via the existing seed path creates documents for two tenants and the test fails if the second tenant has no chunks.

tickets.title: Grow the golden set to about 300 curated cases
tickets.summary: Reach ~300 golden cases, curated per tenant and balanced by category.
tickets.description: Grow data/eval/golden_qa.json to 280-320 cases across answerable, adversarial and refusal categories, parameterised by tenant (the `eval` tenant plus the second fixture tenant). Cases are authored from the corpus documents (regulatory refs and chunk ids must resolve). Add a coverage script `python -m scripts.golden_stats` that prints counts per category and per document and fails on unresolved expected chunk ids. Quote ADR-017: "Golden set 50 growing to ~300"; consequence: "the golden set must be curated per tenant". Out of scope: the human calibration labels (E7-T1).
acceptance_criteria: `python -m scripts.golden_stats` exits 0 and reports total between 280 and 320.
A test fails if any expected_chunk_id / expected_doc_ref does not exist in the seeded eval-tenant corpus.
A test fails if any category has fewer than 5% of total cases or any single document is referenced by more than 10% of answerable cases.

tickets.title: Build the eval job entrypoint, Langfuse datasets and run record
tickets.summary: Provide a `jobs eval` entrypoint that runs as fa_eval against the eval tenant, syncs the golden set to Langfuse and emits EvalRunCompleted.
tickets.description: Add the `eval` Cloud Run job entrypoint on the existing `jobs` image entrypoint (arch 4.8: `eval` | `fa_eval` | "Full or subset eval run (L1-L3) against the dedicated `eval` tenant; results to Langfuse and `eval.events.v1`"). Arguments: `--subset pr|full`, `--layers l1,l2,l3`, `--model answer|fallback`. It opens DB connections as `fa_eval` only (role created in E1), pinned to `EVAL_TENANT_ID`; it must refuse to start if EVAL_TENANT_ID is unset or if the connected role is not fa_eval. It syncs the golden set to a Langfuse dataset (`run_experiment`), writes a JSON result file (metrics, git sha, model ids, prompt version) and produces `EvalRunCompleted` on `eval.events.v1` with the `eval` service-account Kafka key using an idempotent producer (event_id derived from run id). The ~60-question PR subset is selected by a `subset: pr` flag on cases (stratified, set in this ticket for existing cases). Out of scope: metric computation (T6, T8, T10), CI wiring (T12).
acceptance_criteria: Given DB user fa_app, the entrypoint exits non-zero with a message naming the role mismatch (unit test).
Given EVAL_TENANT_ID unset, the entrypoint exits non-zero before any DB or LLM call (unit test).
`--subset pr` selects between 55 and 65 cases and every category is represented (unit test on the shipped golden set once T3 is merged).
Integration test with the CI Kafka container: a dry run produces exactly one EvalRunCompleted message; running it twice with the same run id yields one logical event (dedupe on event_id).

tickets.title: Implement L1 retrieval metrics: recall@k, MRR and nDCG
tickets.summary: Compute retrieval quality metrics for a retrieval configuration over the golden set.
tickets.description: In `backend/src/evals/l1.py` (or the repo's existing eval package location) compute recall@k (k in 5, 10, 15), MRR and nDCG@10 per case and aggregate, calling the production `RetrievalService.search` path under the `fa_eval` role and the `eval` tenant so RLS applies exactly as in chat. Accept a config object {mode: dense|fts|hybrid|hybrid_rerank, rerank_candidates, contextual_headers: bool}, which sets the corresponding settings for the run only (RRF_K 60, HNSW settings from config). Record p50/p95 latency of the first stage and of rerank per config. Only answerable cases with expected chunk ids are scored. Output JSON per config. Quote ADR-008: "RRF k = 60 in one SQL statement with RLS on both legs" and ADR-017 L1. Out of scope: choosing the winning config (E7-T7).
acceptance_criteria: Unit test with a fake retriever and hand-built ranked lists asserts recall@5, MRR and nDCG@10 equal hand-computed values to 4 decimals.
Integration test (real pgvector in CI) runs mode=dense and mode=hybrid on 5 seeded cases and returns metrics with latency fields non-null.
Test asserts the L1 run opens its connection as fa_eval and that a query using a foreign tenant id returns zero results.

tickets.title: Spike: retrieval ablation for rerank and contextual retrieval
tickets.summary: Run dense / FTS / hybrid / rerank (with and without contextual headers) ablation and record the decisions.
tickets.description: Spike. Using E7-T6, run these configs over the full golden set: dense, FTS, hybrid (RRF k=60), hybrid + rerank with RERANK_CANDIDATES in {10, 15, 20, 30}, each with CONTEXTUAL_RETRIEVAL_ENABLED on and off (requires the corpus re-indexed with and without `chunks.context_header`). Record recall@5/10/15, MRR, nDCG@10 and first-stage / rerank p95 latency. Write docs/adr/retrieval-ablation.md with the table and these decisions: RERANK_ENABLED (kept or dropped), RERANK_CANDIDATES (value in range 10-30), CONTEXTUAL_RETRIEVAL_ENABLED (kept or dropped). Quote ADR-008: "kept or dropped by the eval ablation on recall and latency; `RERANK_CANDIDATES` default 15 (range 10-30), set by the L1 ablation (D14.1)" and ADR-016: "The L1 ablation decides whether it stays." The ticket also records the latency budget check: first stage p95 < 300 ms, rerank p95 < 700 ms. Out of scope: GATE_MIN_SCORE (set in E3-T16). Applying the chosen values to config defaults is part of this ticket (config change only).
acceptance_criteria: docs/adr/retrieval-ablation.md exists with one row per config containing recall@10, MRR, nDCG@10 and p95 latency as numbers; a grep test fails on empty cells.

The ADR states RERANK_ENABLED, RERANK_CANDIDATES (between 10 and 30) and CONTEXTUAL_RETRIEVAL_ENABLED each as kept/dropped or a value, with the recall delta in points and latency delta in ms that justify it.
The default values in `Settings` equal the ADR decisions (unit test reads both).
Rerun of the winning config reproduces recall@10 within 1 point of the ADR value (command recorded in the ADR).

tickets.title: Implement L2 Ragas runner with CI lower bounds
tickets.summary: Score answers with Ragas collections using the Haiku judge and report metrics with confidence-interval lower bounds.
tickets.description: Implement the L2 runner: for each answerable case run the real chat pipeline (answer model from `--model`) as fa_eval on the eval tenant, then score with Ragas collections API (pinned version): faithfulness, context precision, context recall, noise sensitivity, plus the deterministic citation score from the E4 CitationVerifier output (do not reimplement the verifier; call E4-T11). Judge model is `LLM_MODEL_JUDGE`; the runner refuses to run if judge == answer model. Report each metric as mean plus a bootstrap 95% confidence interval and its lower bound (ARES-style, arXiv 2311.09476). Refuse to emit gate-eligible numbers unless docs/adr/judge-calibration.md records a go decision (read a machine-readable `judge_calibration.json` written by E7-T1 containing kappa and `go`). Out of scope: the gate comparison (T11).
acceptance_criteria: Unit test: bootstrap CI on a fixed score vector with fixed seed returns the hand-verified lower bound to 3 decimals.
Unit test: runner raises when judge model equals answer model.
Unit test: runner raises a clear error when judge_calibration.json is missing or has go=false.
Integration test with a stub LLM and stub judge on 5 cases produces a result JSON with mean, ci_low, ci_high for faithfulness, context_precision, context_recall, noise_sensitivity and citation.

tickets.title: Implement L3 refusal, tier, jurisdiction and cross-tenant runner
tickets.summary: Execute the refusal and leak-probe golden cases and count leaks.
tickets.description: Run all cases in categories refusal, cross_tenant, tier, jurisdiction, adversarial through the real chat API path as fa_eval/eval tenant personas. A leak is defined as: any returned citation, SSE event, or answer text containing a chunk id, document id or marker from `forbidden_chunk_ids`, or an answer where expected_refusal is set but no refusal event occurred. Output {refusal_pass_rate, leaks} and the offending case ids. Quote ADR-017: "Gate: ... leaks = 0" and OWASP LLM02/LLM08 tests. Add a way to plant a leak for self-tests: env flag `EVAL_PLANT_LEAK=1` is NOT allowed in production code; instead the runner accepts an injected `retriever_override` used only by tests. Out of scope: promptfoo red team (T15).
acceptance_criteria: Unit test with a fake chat client that returns a forbidden chunk id: runner reports leaks == 1 and names the case.
Unit test with a fake client that answers instead of refusing on a refusal case: refusal_pass_rate < 1.0.
Integration test (real DB, stub LLM) with the shipped probes: leaks == 0 and the run exits 0 on the unmodified pipeline.
Test asserts no production module reads an EVAL_PLANT_LEAK-style env flag (grep test).

tickets.title: Add the gate evaluator with thresholds and recall baseline
tickets.summary: Compare run results to the gate thresholds and the stored recall baseline and fail with a clear reason.
tickets.description: Implement `python -m scripts.eval_gate result.json --baseline data/eval/baseline.json` that exits non-zero if: citation < 0.95, faithfulness < 0.90 (judged on the CI lower bound when the full run, on the point estimate on the PR subset), leaks > 0, or recall@10 drops by more than 2 points versus baseline. Thresholds are constants in config (not scattered). Add `scripts.eval_baseline_update` to write a new baseline (manual, reviewed in PR). Quote ADR-017: "Gate: citation >= 0.95, faithfulness >= 0.90, leaks = 0, recall regression <= 2 pts" and "gate thresholds need re-tuning when the corpus grows". Output a one-line failure reason per breached rule. Out of scope: running the metrics (T6, T8, T9) and CI wiring (T11).
acceptance_criteria: Parametrised unit tests: citation 0.949 fails, 0.95 passes; faithfulness 0.899 fails, 0.90 passes; leaks 1 fails; recall drop 2.1 points fails, 2.0 passes.
Each failing case prints the rule name and the measured and required values (asserted by output match).
A missing baseline file makes the gate exit non-zero with a message (unit test), never pass silently.

tickets.title: Wire the path-filtered PR eval job in CI
