tickets.summary: Run the ~60-question subset as the blocking `eval` job on relevant PRs.
tickets.description: Add a GitHub Actions workflow `eval-pr.yml` extending the E0 CI (Postgres with pgvector and Kafka service containers already exist): path filter on backend/src/{retrieval,agent,guardrails,llm,prompts}, data/eval, and prompt files; steps: migrate, seed the eval tenant, run `jobs eval --subset pr --layers l1,l2,l3` as fa_eval, then `scripts.eval_gate`; upload result JSON as an artifact; fail the check on gate failure. Secrets for Anthropic and Voyage come from GitHub secrets; the job runs only when secrets exist (fork PRs skip with a visible neutral status). Out of scope: the weekly workflow (T13); the L0 jobs (E0/E1).
acceptance_criteria: On a PR touching backend/src/retrieval the workflow runs and the check named `eval` appears; on a docs-only PR it does not run (verified by a workflow path-filter test via `act` or recorded run links in the PR description).
A forced gate failure (E7-T12 fixtures) turns the `eval` check red; the green path posts the metrics table as an artifact.
The job's DB user is fa_eval (assert in a CI step that `select current_user` equals fa_eval).

tickets.title: Prove the gate with four deliberate-regression test PRs
tickets.summary: Show that the PR gate fails for each of four seeded regressions.
tickets.description: Create four regression patches kept as reviewed fixtures under tests/eval_gate/regressions/: (1) break the citation verifier call so citation < 0.95; (2) change the system prompt to encourage unsupported claims so faithfulness < 0.90; (3) plant a cross-tenant leak by dropping the tenant predicate in a retriever double used by the eval run (via the retriever_override from E7-T9, not by editing production RLS); (4) lower RERANK_CANDIDATES / disable the FTS leg so recall@10 drops by more than 2 points. Add a workflow `eval-gate-selftest.yml` (manual dispatch) that applies each patch to a throwaway branch, runs the PR eval job, and asserts the gate fails with the expected rule. Open four draft PRs and record their links and the failing rule in docs/eval/gate-proof.md. Quote the epic done-when: "The PR gate fails a deliberate regression in each of: citation < 0.95, faithfulness < 0.90, a planted cross-tenant leak, recall drop > 2 points (four test PRs)."
acceptance_criteria: For each of the four patches, the selftest workflow reports the eval job failed with the rule name citation, faithfulness, leaks or recall respectively (four recorded run URLs in docs/eval/gate-proof.md).
A fifth control run with no patch passes the gate.
A test fails if docs/eval/gate-proof.md lists fewer than four PR links or any entry lacks the measured value.

tickets.title: Add the weekly full eval run with CI lower bounds
tickets.summary: Run the full golden set weekly and before demos, reporting lower bounds.
tickets.description: Add a scheduled workflow `eval-full.yml` (cron weekly plus workflow_dispatch for before-demo runs) that runs `jobs eval --subset full --layers l1,l2,l3` against the answer model, applies `scripts.eval_gate` using CI lower bounds for faithfulness and citation, publishes a Markdown report (metrics, CI low/high, per-category breakdown, comparison with baseline) to the workflow summary and to Langfuse, and emits EvalRunCompleted. Quote ADR-017: "the full set runs weekly and before demos". Cloud Scheduler/Cloud Run job scheduling is E10; this ticket is the CI/GitHub-hosted run only.
acceptance_criteria: After a workflow_dispatch run the summary contains ci_low for faithfulness and citation as numbers; a test on the report generator fails if any is missing.
The run uses the full set (>= 280 cases) asserted by the result JSON `n_cases`.
A forced faithfulness lower bound below 0.90 in a stub run makes the job fail (unit test on the report/gate step).

tickets.title: Full eval on the fallback model gates LLM_FALLBACK_ENABLED
tickets.summary: Evaluate claude-sonnet-4-6 once and make enabling the fallback depend on that result.
tickets.description: Run `jobs eval --subset full --model fallback` using LLM_MODEL_FALLBACK (claude-sonnet-4-6) and store the result as data/eval/fallback_result.json with the gate verdict. Add a startup check in config validation: `LLM_FALLBACK_ENABLED=true` is rejected unless data/eval/fallback_result.json (or the configured eval-record location) shows pass for the same fallback model id and a prompt version equal to current PROMPT_VERSION. Quote config table: "`LLM_FALLBACK_ENABLED` ... `false` until the gate passes against it" and ADR-017: "once against the fallback model".
acceptance_criteria: Unit test: Settings with LLM_FALLBACK_ENABLED=true and no passing record raises at boot.
Unit test: a passing record for a different model id or different PROMPT_VERSION still raises.
A fallback full-run result exists in the repo with model id claude-sonnet-4-6 and the gate verdict recorded as pass or fail with numbers.

tickets.title: Add the promptfoo red-team job
tickets.summary: Run a promptfoo red team against the API as fa_eval in the redteam job.
tickets.description: Add a promptfoo config (pinned version) under evals/redteam/ targeting the chat API in an ephemeral environment, with plugins for prompt injection, system prompt leakage, PII, cross-tenant/BOLA-style probes and excessive agency, mapped to OWASP LLM01, LLM02, LLM06, LLM07 (arch 8.1 tests column). Add the `redteam` job entrypoint (DB role `fa_eval`, eval tenant) and a CI workflow step on the weekly workflow; a failing probe category fails the job. Out of scope: golden-set L3 (T9).
acceptance_criteria: `promptfoo redteam run` in CI against the stub-LLM stack produces a report artifact and exits non-zero when a seeded vulnerable prompt (test fixture) leaks the system prompt.
Config test asserts plugins cover LLM01, LLM02, LLM06, LLM07 (named mapping in the file).
The redteam job fails to start if the connected DB role is not fa_eval (unit test).

tickets.title: Emit eval.sample.v1 outbox rows and thumbs feedback events
tickets.summary: Have chat-api sample EVAL_SAMPLE_RATE of completed turns into the outbox and send feedback to eval.events.v1.
tickets.description: In chat-api's end-of-turn transaction (arch flow 1: "persist assistant message, turn_events, outbox rows (chat.audit, chat.usage, sampled eval.sample)") add the sampled `TurnSampled` outbox row {message_id, redacted question, redacted answer, cited excerpts (redacted)} for a fraction `EVAL_SAMPLE_RATE` (default 0.05, allowed 0.05-0.10, validated). Sampling is deterministic from message_id hash so tests are repeatable. Ensure `POST /v1/messages/{id}/feedback` (`{score: -1|1, comment?}`) writes `feedback` and an outbox `FeedbackRecorded` for `eval.events.v1`. Only redacted text enters the payload. Do this only if E4/E6 have not already implemented the pieces: check the repo and implement the missing parts. Out of scope: the relay (E5).
acceptance_criteria: Unit test: with EVAL_SAMPLE_RATE=0.10 over 1000 synthetic message ids between 8% and 12% are sampled; with 0 none; the setting rejects 0.5.
Integration test: a completed turn selected by the sampler leaves one outbox row of type TurnSampled whose payload contains no raw PII fixture value.
Integration test: POST feedback with score 1 creates a feedback row and a FeedbackRecorded outbox row; score 2 returns 422.

tickets.title: Implement the eval-judge worker role
tickets.summary: Consume eval.sample.v1, judge with Haiku 5.5 and write Langfuse scores and eval_scores.
tickets.description: Add worker role `eval-judge` (selected via WORKER_ROLES) on the E5 Kafka consumer framework, group `cg.eval-judge`. For each `TurnSampled`: envelope check (tenant_id equals key and not PUBLIC, else dlq.v1), dedupe on message_id + metric via `processed_events`, score faithfulness and citation with `LLM_MODEL_JUDGE` (claude-haiku-5-5, must differ from the answer model) using the calibrated prompt from E7-T1, in one transaction with `app.tenant_id` set insert rows into `eval_scores` {message_id, judge_model, metric, score, rationale (redacted), created_at} as `fa_worker`, send scores to Langfuse (no Langfuse-side evaluators), and write a `JudgeScored` outbox row for `eval.events.v1`. Quote 4.7: "scores the redacted question / answer / cited excerpts with `claude-haiku-5-5` ..., writes scores to Langfuse and `eval_scores`, emits `JudgeScored` on `eval.events.v1`." Out of scope: the sampler (T16), the table and grants (E1).
acceptance_criteria: Unit test: a message whose envelope tenant_id differs from the key goes to dlq.v1 with a reason and writes no score.
Unit test: delivering the same message twice yields one eval_scores row per metric.
Unit test: worker raises at boot if the judge model equals the answer model.
Integration test (CI Postgres + Kafka, stub judge): a TurnSampled message produces rows in eval_scores for the right tenant and an outbox JudgeScored row.

tickets.title: Verify eval-judge end to end with RLS on eval_scores
tickets.summary: Show one sampled turn scored into Langfuse and eval_scores with tenant isolation and no fa_app access.
tickets.description: Add an end-to-end test and a short runbook docs/eval/online-judge.md: chat turn on the eval tenant sampled at rate 1.0 in test -> outbox -> relay -> eval.sample.v1 -> eval-judge -> row in eval_scores and a Langfuse score (Langfuse local container or recorded API call in CI). Also assert the DB-level properties: tenant B's session cannot read tenant A's eval_scores rows; `fa_app` has no privilege on the table. tickets.title: Map API error codes to UI states with 401 and 429 handling
tickets.summary: Every API error renders a fixed, code-keyed message and 401 and 429 never crash the app.
tickets.description: Implements overview 4.4 'error states keyed by error code' and 6.1 error shape `{"error":{code,message,request_id,retryable}}`. Add src/lib/errors.ts: parse the error body into ApiError; a table keyed by every 6.1 code (UNAUTHENTICATED, FORBIDDEN, INPUT_TOO_LONG, INPUT_BLOCKED, GUARD_UNAVAILABLE, RATE_LIMITED, TENANT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED, NO_FIRM_DOCUMENTATION, LLM_UNAVAILABLE, RETRIEVAL_UNAVAILABLE, TURN_INTERRUPTED, IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED, INTERNAL) to client-owned copy and a retry hint; unknown codes fall back to INTERNAL copy. Never display server `message` text verbatim as HTML; show request_id for support. 401: refresh token once, retry once, else return to sign-in. 429: read `Retry-After`, show a countdown and disable send until it elapses. Add an error boundary. Out of scope: SSE-specific handling (E8-T5/T6).
acceptance_criteria: Given each code in the 6.1 list, when mapped, then a non-empty message exists (table-driven vitest over all codes) and an unknown code maps to the INTERNAL copy.
Given a 429 with `Retry-After: 5`, when the chat send is attempted, then the send button is disabled and a countdown shows, re-enabling after 5 s (fake timers).
Given a 401 whose retry after token refresh also returns 401, when it occurs, then the sign-in view shows and no uncaught exception is logged.
Given a render error in a child, when thrown, then the error boundary shows a fallback (unit test).

tickets.title: Build fetch-based SSE client with resume and idempotency
tickets.summary: A typed SSE client posts a chat turn with an Idempotency-Key and resumes from Last-Event-ID after a drop.
tickets.description: Implements overview 6.2 and 6.1. src/lib/sse.ts, fetch + ReadableStream (not EventSource, because of the Authorization header and POST), parsing with eventsource-parser. Typed discriminated union for events turn, meta, tool, delta, citation, refusal, error, done with the 6.2 data shapes. `sendTurn({conversation_id?, message})`: generate `Idempotency-Key` (crypto.randomUUID) per user submit, POST /v1/chat, record `turn_id` from the `turn` event and the last `id:` seq. On a transport drop before `done`/`error`, reconnect to `GET /v1/chat/{turn_id}/events` with `Last-Event-ID: <last seq>`, bounded retries with backoff (config constants), ignoring events with seq <= last seen (no duplicate deltas). If the drop happens before the `turn` event, retry POST with the same key. `error` event with TURN_INTERRUPTED retryable: surface to caller, which resubmits with a NEW key. 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED surfaces as an ApiError. Support AbortController. Ignore heartbeat comment lines. Out of scope: server side (E4).
acceptance_criteria: Given a stream cut after seq 3, when the client reconnects, then the GET carries `Last-Event-ID: 3` and the output has no duplicated delta text (vitest with a fake fetch).
Given a drop before the `turn` event, when retried, then the POST reuses the same Idempotency-Key.
Given an `error {TURN_INTERRUPTED, retryable:true}`, when received, then the client emits it to the caller and does not auto-resume; a resubmit uses a different key (unit test).
Given a heartbeat comment line and a replayed event with seq <= last seen, when parsed, then neither reaches the caller.
Given an unknown event name, when received, then it is ignored without throwing.

tickets.title: Render the streamed turn with meta notice and refusal
tickets.summary: The chat view shows deltas as they arrive, tool status, a degraded-retrieval notice, refusals and errors.
tickets.description: Implements overview 6.2 behaviour in the UI. Rewrite useChat (zustand store) on top of E8-T5: `turn` sets ids; `delta` appends to the in-progress assistant message; `tool` shows a status chip (tool name and status only); `meta` with retrieval_degraded=true shows a visible notice ('answer built with reduced ranking quality', reason optional), stored on the message; `refusal` NO_FIRM_DOCUMENTATION shows the refusal message and, if escalate_offer, an escalation hint (no endpoint call beyond arch); `error` shows the code-keyed state from E8-T4 with Retry when retryable; `done` finalises with message_id and finish_reason (max_tokens shows a 'truncated' note). Disable input while streaming; Stop button aborts. Remove client-side citation parsing of `[n]` (server emits citations; E8-T7). Out of scope: markdown (E8-T7), history (E8-T8).
acceptance_criteria: Given a scripted event sequence turn, delta x3, done, when processed, then the message text equals the concatenated deltas and finish state is set (vitest store test).
Given `meta {retrieval_degraded:true}`, when received, then the degraded notice is in the DOM; given false, it is absent.
Given `refusal {escalate_offer:true}`, when received, then the refusal view and escalation hint render and no assistant text is shown.
Given `error {code:'LLM_UNAVAILABLE',retryable:true}`, when received, then the mapped message and a Retry button show; given retryable false, no Retry button.
Given the Stop button, when clicked mid-stream, then the fetch is aborted and input is re-enabled.

tickets.title: Render sanitized markdown, citations with excerpts and stale badges

Renders sanitized markdown only' and the `citation` event `{index, chunk_id, source_title, regulatory_ref, last_reviewed_at, stale, excerpt}`. Markdown via react-markdown with no raw HTML (no rehype-raw), plus an explicit sanitiser (rehype-sanitize with a minimal allowlist; links limited to http/https/mailto and rel=noopener noreferrer; images not rendered). Citation panel lists source_title, regulatory_ref, last_reviewed_at, excerpt (as text, never HTML) and a StaleBadge when stale=true. Reuse/adapt existing MarkdownContent, CitationPanel, StaleBadge, SourcesPanel. Also used for history messages (E8-T8). Out of scope: client-side citation verification.

Given a `citation` event with stale=true, when rendered, then the stale badge shows; with stale=false it does not.

Given a citation with index 1, when `[1]` is clicked, then the panel entry for index 1 is highlighted.

tickets.title: Structured JSON logging with redaction processor
tickets.summary: Every log line is JSON with the 9.3 field set and passes through a redactor that drops bodies, queries, prompts and exception text.
tickets.description:
Implements overview.md 9.3: "Structured JSON to stdout, redacted before writing: ts, severity, trace, request_id, tenant_id, advisor_hash, event, error_code. No request bodies, queries, prompts, tool payloads or exception text for clients."
Extend backend/src/observability/logging.py (structlog already present; it currently binds user_id and renders exception info). Build:
- Processors producing exactly the keys ts, severity, trace (Cloud Trace id from the current OTel span, empty if none), request_id, tenant_id, advisor_hash (sha256 of advisor_id, never the raw id), event, error_code, plus event-specific scalar fields.
- A redaction processor with a denylist of keys (body, query, prompt, message, messages, content, tool_input, tool_output, sql, params, exc_info, exception, traceback, authorization, token) that replaces the value with "[redacted]", and runs the E4 PII scrubber (backend/src/pii) over remaining string values.
- Remove format_exc_info: log error_code and exception class name only.
- bind_request_context takes request_id, tenant_id, advisor_id (hash applied inside).
Out of scope: Kong file-log (E2-T15), Langfuse masking (E0-T8), spans (E9-T2), log-based metric definitions (E9-T11).
acceptance_criteria: Given logger.info('x', body='secret text', query='SELECT 1', error_code='INTERNAL'), When captured by a test sink, Then the JSON has body and query equal to '[redacted]', contains the keys ts, severity, trace, request_id, tenant_id, advisor_hash, event, error_code, and the test fails if any other key carries the secret text (pytest backend/tests/observability/test_logging.py).

Given logger.exception inside an except ValueError('card 4111 1111 1111 1111'), When captured, Then the line has no 'traceback' or 'exc_info' key and the string '4111' does not appear anywhere in the line.
Given bound advisor_id='adv-123', When a line is logged, Then advisor_hash is a 64-hex sha256 and 'adv-123' does not appear in the line.

Given an active OTel span, When a line is logged, Then trace equals the span's trace id in Cloud Trace format projects/

/traces/; with no span it is an empty string.

tickets.title: OpenTelemetry bootstrap for chat-api and workers
tickets.summary: One shared init function configures OTel tracing with FastAPI, asyncpg and HTTP client instrumentation, SQL parameter capture off, exporting to the OTLP endpoint.
tickets.description:
Implements overview.md 9.1: "OpenTelemetry end to end: Kong opentelemetry (traceparent) to chat-api (FastAPI, asyncpg / SQLAlchemy, Voyage and Anthropic HTTP calls) to workers ... to Cloud Trace. SQL parameter capture off; no request bodies in spans (D13o)." Stack: OpenTelemetry SDK + exporters, versions pinned at implementation (stack.md).
Build backend/src/observability/tracing.py (exists; rework) with init_tracing(service_name) used by the chat-api app factory and by the worker/job entrypoints:
- TracerProvider with resource service.name, deployment.environment = ENV_PROFILE; OTLP exporter to OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT (config key, required); BatchSpanProcessor.
- W3C traceparent propagation; FastAPI instrumentation continues the traceparent Kong sends.
- asyncpg / SQLAlchemy instrumentation with parameter capture controlled only by OTEL_DB_CAPTURE_PARAMS (default false; the db.statement attribute is replaced by the operation and table, no literals).
- httpx/aiohttp instrumentation for Voyage and Anthropic calls with request/response body and header capture disabled.
- A SpanProcessor that deletes any attribute whose key is in the E9-T1 denylist or that is longer than 256 characters.
- init is a no-op when the endpoint is unset in dev profile.
Out of scope: span names in the turn pipeline (E9-T3), worker spans (E9-T4), the Kong plugin (E2-T15).
Export path (resolution R77): direct OTLP to the Google Cloud Telemetry API endpoint (telemetry.googleapis.com) authenticated with Application Default Credentials; no sidecar. FIRST step of this ticket is a verification: send a test span from a Cloud Run service (or a scratch project with ADC) and confirm it appears in Cloud Trace. Write the outcome to docs/adr/otel-export.md. If direct export fails, the fallback is an OTel Collector sidecar on Cloud Run; record that decision, the evidence and the changed deployment in the same ADR before building it. OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is set accordingly.
acceptance_criteria: Given OTEL_DB_CAPTURE_PARAMS=false, When a query 'SELECT * FROM advisors WHERE email = $1' runs with a parameter 'a@b.com' under an in-memory exporter, Then no exported span attribute value contains 'a@b.com' (pytest test_tracing_sql.py).
Given a request with a traceparent header, When it hits GET /healthz, Then the exported server span has the same trace_id and its parent_span_id equals the header's span id.
Given an httpx call to a stubbed api.anthropic.com with a JSON body containing 'SECRETPROMPT', When exported, Then no span attribute contains 'SECRETPROMPT'.
Given an attribute named 'body' or a 300-char value is set on a span, When the span ends, Then the exported span lacks it.

Given the verification run, When a span is exported with ADC to the Telemetry API endpoint, Then it is returned by the Cloud Trace API (gcloud/REST get trace) within 60 s, and docs/adr/otel-export.md exists with the result and the fallback decision (CI file-presence check fails if the ADR is missing).

tickets.title: Instrument the chat turn with the named spans
tickets.summary: The chat turn emits chat.turn and its child spans with the 9.1 names and only non-sensitive attributes.
tickets.description:
Implements the span-name list of overview.md 9.1: chat.turn, auth.verify, principal.load, guard.input, guard.model_armor, embed.query, retrieval.hybrid_sql, retrieval.rerank, retrieval.gate, llm.stream, guard.output, persist.turn.
Add backend/src/observability/spans.py: constants for the names above and a helper span(name, **attrs) that rejects (raises in tests, drops in prod) attributes outside an allowlist (tenant_id, turn_id, model, token counts, chunk_count, degraded, gate_result, cache_hit, error_code). Wrap the existing call sites in auth, principal, guardrails, retrieval, llm, agent and persistence code in the matching span. chat.turn is the parent; llm.stream carries model, input/output/cache-read token counts; retrieval.gate carries gate_result. Spans must not carry query text, prompts, chunk text or SQL parameters.
Out of scope: changing the behaviour of those stages; Langfuse generations (E0-T8); worker spans (E9-T4).
acceptance_criteria: Given one stubbed POST /v1/chat that is answered, When spans are collected with an in-memory exporter, Then all twelve span names exist, share one trace_id, and every one except chat.turn has a parent in the trace (pytest test_turn_spans.py).
Given a refusal turn (gate refuses), When collected, Then retrieval.gate has gate_result='refused' and no llm.stream span exists.
Given span('x', query='abc'), When run under pytest, Then it raises ValueError; with ENV_PROFILE=prod it drops the attribute and the exported span lacks it.
Given the turn, When exported, Then llm.stream has integer attributes for input, output and cache-read tokens.

tickets.title: Link consumer spans to producer spans over Kafka headers
tickets.summary: outbox.relay and consumer.<role> spans are emitted and each consumer span carries a span link to the producing span from the traceparent header.
tickets.description:
Implements overview.md 9.1: "workers (traceparent carried in Kafka headers)", spans outbox.relay and consumer.<role>. The producer wrapper already sets traceparent (E5-T6) and the consumer base class exists (E5-T7).
Build: in the outbox-relay role (E5-T10) wrap each publish in an outbox.relay span, writing the current context into the Kafka traceparent header (via the E5-T6 wrapper, do not duplicate it). In the consumer base (E5-T7) start consumer.<role> for each message with a Link to the SpanContext extracted from traceparent (a link, not a parent, so batch/retry does not stretch traces); retries and DLQ publishing (E5-T8) stay inside the span. Attributes: topic, partition, offset, tenant_id, role, outcome. No payloads.
Out of scope: producer header logic, consumer semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Given a message produced inside a span S through the E5-T6 wrapper and consumed by the E5-T7 base in a test with an in-memory exporter, When the handler finishes, Then a span named 'consumer.<role>' exists whose links contain S's trace_id and span_id (pytest test_consumer_links.py).
Given a message without a traceparent header, When consumed, Then consumer.<role> is still emitted with no links and no exception.
Given a handler that raises, When retried then sent to the DLQ, Then the span has outcome='dlq' and error_code set, and its attributes contain no payload text.
Given the outbox-relay role publishes 3 rows, When collected, Then three outbox.relay spans exist, each with topic and tenant_id attributes.

tickets.title: Shared metrics module and 9.2 metric registry
tickets.summary: One module owns metric names, types and labels from the 9.2 table and records them to OTel and to a log line for log-based metrics.
tickets.description:
Implements overview.md 9.2: "Metrics (log-based and OTel, in Cloud Monitoring)". Create backend/src/observability/metrics.py:
- A registry listing every metric in the table with name, kind (counter, histogram, gauge), unit and allowed labels: chat_ttft_ms, chat_total_ms, retrieval_first_stage_ms, rerank_ms, rerank_fallback_total{reason}, rerank_429_total, retrieval_degraded_ratio, gate_refusals_total, guard_blocks_total{guard}, llm_fallback_total, llm_breaker_state, answer_cache_hit_ratio, outbox_oldest_age_s, consumer_lag{group}, acl_apply_lag_s, dlq_messages_total, tenant_budget_rejections_total{tenant}, default_partition_rows, db_connections_in_use.
- record(name, value, **labels) that rejects unknown names or labels and records through the OTel metrics API (OTLP) and also writes one structured log line (event='metric', metric, value, labels) through the E9-T1 logger so log-based metrics work.
- Existing emitters from E3-T9, E4 and E5 are migrated to call record() where they currently do something else; do not change their values.
Out of scope: dashboards, alerts, new emitters (E9-T6, E9-T7).
Add to the registry (resolutions R73, R74): llm_cost_usd_total{provider,model} (counter, USD), readiness_failing (gauge 0/1) and model_retirement_days (gauge, days until the earliest retirement of a configured model). The registry now has 22 metrics; the 9.2 table copy in backend/tests/observability/metrics_9_2.txt includes these three (the architecture table §9.2 gains these rows). Earlier epics emit with plain OTel meters; this ticket moves them to the registry (R71).
acceptance_criteria: Given record('not_a_metric', 1), When called, Then it raises KeyError; given record('rerank_fallback_total', 1, reason='x', extra='y'), Then it raises on the unknown label (pytest test_metrics_registry.py).

Given the registry, When compared with the metric names parsed from the overview.md 9.2 table copied into backend/tests/observability/metrics_9_2.txt, Then the sets are equal (the test fails if one is added or missing).
Given record('chat_ttft_ms', 1200), When captured, Then one OTel data point and one log line with event='metric', metric='chat_ttft_ms' and value 1200 exist.
Given a label value tenant_id longer than 64 chars or containing newline, When recorded, Then it is rejected or truncated so the log line stays a single JSON line.

Given record('llm_cost_usd_total', 0.01, provider='anthropic', model='x'), When captured, Then it is accepted; with a label other than provider and model it raises; the registry has exactly the 22 names in metrics_9_2.txt.

tickets.title: Emit chat latency, cache, budget, DB pool and LLM cost metrics
tickets.summary: The chat path emits the 9.2 metrics no other epic owns: TTFT, total latency, cache ratio, tenant budget rejections and connection use.
tickets.description:
Implements the 9.2 rows for chat_ttft_ms, chat_total_ms, answer_cache_hit_ratio, tenant_budget_rejections_total{tenant} and db_connections_in_use. Retrieval metrics are emitted by E3-T9, guard and LLM metrics (guard_blocks_total, llm_fallback_total, llm_breaker_state, gate_refusals_total) by E4, acl_apply_lag_s by E5; do not touch those.
Using metrics.record (E9-T5): in the chat orchestrator record chat_ttft_ms at the first delta event and chat_total_ms at done (also on errors, with the elapsed time); record answer_cache_hit_ratio as a rolling ratio gauge over the last N turns (window config constant, default 100); record tenant_budget_rejections_total when TENANT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED is returned; sample db_connections_in_use from the asyncpg pool every 15 s in a background task (pool size is DB_POOL_SIZE; budget is 300 connections overall, 9.2).
If E4 already emits any of these names, keep one emitter and delete the duplicate (check with grep before coding).
Also emit llm_cost_usd_total{provider,model} (R73): cost = input/output/cache-read/cache-write token counts from each Anthropic call (and Voyage embed/rerank usage) multiplied by a price table in config (new Settings key LLM_PRICE_TABLE_JSON, a mapping provider/model to USD per million tokens by token kind; a missing model logs a warning and records 0 with a label-free counter llm_cost_unpriced). Recorded in the llm client after each call; no payloads.
acceptance_criteria: Given a stubbed turn with the first delta after 1.2 s and done after 3.0 s using a fake clock, When it completes, Then chat_ttft_ms=1200 and chat_total_ms=3000 are recorded exactly once each (pytest test_chat_metrics.py).
Given 3 cache hits and 1 miss, When answer_cache_hit_ratio is read, Then it is 0.75.
Given a tenant over its budget, When POST /v1/chat is called, Then the response error code is TENANT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED and tenant_budget_rejections_total{tenant} increments by 1.
Given a pool with 4 connections acquired, When the sampler runs, Then db_connections_in_use=4. A grep test asserts each of these five names is recorded in exactly one module.

Given a stubbed call with 1000 input and 500 output tokens on a model priced at $3 and $15 per million, When completed, Then llm_cost_usd_total{provider='anthropic',model=<m>} increases by 0.0105 (pytest test_llm_cost.py).
Given a model absent from LLM_PRICE_TABLE_JSON, When called, Then no exception is raised and llm_cost_unpriced increments by 1.

tickets.title: Emit event-pipeline and partition health metrics
tickets.summary: outbox_oldest_age_s, consumer_lag, dlq_messages_total and default_partition_rows are emitted on a schedule.
tickets.description:
Implements the 9.2 rows for outbox_oldest_age_s, consumer_lag{group}, dlq_messages_total and default_partition_rows ("rows in the DEFAULT chunks / messages partitions (bug signal)"). acl_apply_lag_s is E5's.
Using metrics.record (E9-T5):
- Worker background task (every 30 s, in roles outbox-relay and the consumer roles): outbox_oldest_age_s = now - min(created_at) of unpublished outbox rows (0 if none), read through the worker's tenant-safe path; consumer_lag{group} = end offset minus committed offset summed over the group's partitions; dlq_messages_total incremented in the E5-T8 DLQ publisher.
- default_partition_rows: count rows in chunks_default and messages_default (names as created by E1 migrations; check the schema) recorded as a gauge, emitted from the maintenance job (E1-T12) after its checks, with the job still exiting non-zero as E1-T12 defines.
Out of scope: alerting (E9-T15), the maintenance job's exit code.
The maintenance job runs every 15 min in demo mode (E10 schedules it, R76), so default_partition_rows is refreshed at that cadence.
acceptance_criteria: Given an unpublished outbox row created 90 s ago in a test DB, When the sampler runs, Then outbox_oldest_age_s is between 90 and 95; with no unpublished rows it is 0 (pytest test_pipeline_metrics.py, integration with Postgres).
Given a consumer group committed at offset 10 with end offset 25 on one partition in the local Kafka, When sampled, Then consumer_lag{group}=15.
Given a message that exhausts retries, When published to dlq.v1, Then dlq_messages_total increments by 1.
Given one row inserted into the DEFAULT messages partition, When the maintenance job runs, Then default_partition_rows=1 is recorded and the job exits non-zero; with none it records 0 and exits zero.

tickets.title: Complete /readyz with the 9.4 checks
tickets.summary: /readyz asserts every item in the 9.4 list and returns a per-check result, with Kafka failing only as degraded.
tickets.description:
Implements overview.md 6.1 and 9.4: "/readyz (DB role flags, FORCE RLS, partition grants, pgvector >= 0.8, Kafka reachability (degraded for chat), model availability, verifier initialised)". E0-T5 built /healthz and /readyz with database and model checks; E4-T7 added the retired-model check. Extend, do not rewrite:
- Checks: db_reachable, role_flags (fa_app and fa_worker lack BYPASSRLS and SUPERUSER), force_rls (every tenant table has relforcerowsecurity), partition_grants (the app roles hold privileges on the current and future partitions of chunks and messages), pgvector_version >= 0.8, kafka_reachable (metadata request with a 2 s timeout), models_available (reuse the retired-model check), verifier_initialised (firebase-admin app created).
- Response 200 {status: 'ok' or 'degraded', checks: {name: 'ok'|'fail'|'degraded'}}; Kafka failure gives status 'degraded' and HTTP 200; any other failure gives 503. No error text, hostnames or credentials in the body.
- Record readiness_failing (gauge 0/1) via metrics.record for alerting (add it to the registry and to the 9.2 test list as an addition recorded in questions if not accepted).
Out of scope: /healthz, Kong's status listener, the demo-prewarm call.
readiness_failing (gauge 0/1) is part of the 9.2 registry (R74); it is set from the same checks as /readyz on each probe and by a 15 s background task. model_retirement_days is set by the E0-T4 check at each probe.
acceptance_criteria: Given a test DB where fa_app has BYPASSRLS, When GET /readyz, Then status 503 and checks.role_flags='fail' (pytest test_readyz.py).
Given a table with FORCE RLS disabled, Then 503 with force_rls='fail'; given pgvector 0.7, Then 503 with pgvector_version='fail'.
Given the Kafka broker unreachable and everything else healthy, When GET /readyz, Then HTTP 200 with status='degraded' and kafka_reachable='degraded'.
Given any failure, When the response body is serialised, Then it contains none of the DB host, user or exception text (assert on string).
Given a failing check, When /readyz is probed, Then readiness_failing=1; after recovery it is 0 (pytest).

tickets.title: Leak test for logs, spans and metrics
tickets.summary: A test fails if any log line, span, metric label or trace contains a request body, SQL parameter or unredacted PII after a full turn.
tickets.description:
Implements the Done-when item: "no log line, span or trace contains request bodies, SQL parameters or unredacted PII (test)". E4-T25 already tests that PII does not reach Voyage, Anthropic, logs or Langfuse; this ticket covers the E9 additions (spans, metric labels, consumer spans) and keeps one canary approach: do not repeat E4-T25's cases, reuse its canary fixtures.
Add backend/tests/observability/test_no_leaks.py (integration, local compose with Postgres and Kafka): run a chat turn with canary message text 'CANARY-BODY-7731 jane.doe@example.com 123-45-6789', an ACL change and an eval-sampled event; capture stdout log lines, all spans from an in-memory exporter (including attributes, events and links), and all metric data points and labels; assert none contains the canary strings or the SQL parameter values bound in that run.
Out of scope: Langfuse payloads (E0-T8, E4-T25).
acceptance_criteria: Given the canary turn, When all logs, spans and metric labels are searched, Then zero matches for 'CANARY-BODY-7731', 'jane.doe@example.com' and '123-45-6789' (pytest test_no_leaks.py fails otherwise).
Given OTEL_DB_CAPTURE_PARAMS=true is set by the test, When the same run happens, Then the test fails, proving it can detect parameter capture.
Given a deliberately injected logger.info(body=canary) via a test-only hook, When the redactor is bypassed, Then the test fails (negative control).
Given the full suite in CI, When it runs, Then this test is included in the required checks.

tickets.title: End-to-end trace test across Kong, API, DB and LLM
tickets.summary: A compose test proves one trace spans Kong, chat-api, a DB query and an LLM call, and a Kafka consumer links to its producer.
tickets.description:
Implements the Done-when item: "A single trace spans Kong, chat-api, a DB query and an LLM call, and a Kafka event's consumer span links to its producer span."
Add an integration test run against docker compose with Kong (opentelemetry plugin from E2-T15), chat-api, Postgres, Kafka, a worker, an OpenTelemetry Collector with a file or debug exporter writing spans as JSON, and a stubbed Anthropic/Voyage endpoint. The test sends POST /v1/chat, then reads collector output and asserts the span tree. Add the collector service and config to the compose file and set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT for services. Document how to run it in docs/runbooks/observability.md.
Out of scope: Cloud Trace itself (verified manually in the E9-T17 drill note).
acceptance_criteria: Given the compose stack up, When POST /v1/chat is sent through Kong, Then collector output holds one trace_id containing a Kong span, chat.turn, a DB span (asyncpg) and llm.stream with a child HTTP client span (pytest -m e2e test_e2e_trace.py).
Given a turn that writes an outbox row, When the relay publishes and the worker consumes, Then a consumer.<role> span exists whose link's trace_id equals the turn's trace_id.
Given the Kong plugin disabled, When the test runs, Then it fails on the missing Kong span (negative check documented in the test).
Given the e2e run, When the span dump is scanned, Then no span attribute contains the request message text.

tickets.title: Terraform: log-based metrics and notification channel
tickets.summary: Terraform defines the log-based metrics and the alert notification channel used by all dashboards and alert policies.
tickets.description:
Implements overview.md 9.2 "log-based and OTel, in Cloud Monitoring" for metrics emitted as log lines (event='metric', E9-T5), and creates the notification channel the alerts in 9.5 use. Existing terraform/ has main.tf, cloud_run.tf, variables.tf; add terraform/monitoring.tf.
- google_logging_metric (distribution or counter, label extractors on metric and labels) for every 9.2 metric that is emitted by log line; metrics emitted over OTLP need no resource here.
- google_monitoring_notification_channel (email) with the address from a variable alert_email (required).
- Variables env_profile (matches ENV_PROFILE) used by later tickets.
Out of scope: dashboards (E9-T12), SLOs (E9-T13), alert policies (E9-T14, E9-T15).
Notification channel: email to alert_email (R75).
acceptance_criteria: Given terraform validate and terraform plan -var-file=ci.tfvars, When run in CI, Then both succeed with no errors.

Given the plan output, When listed, Then one google_logging_metric exists for each name in the E9-T5 registry that is log-emitted and the notification channel exists (a script scripts/check_monitoring_tf.py compares names to the registry and fails on a gap).
Given a log line event='metric', metric='rerank_ms', value=412, When tested against the metric's filter with gcloud logging read in the drill (E9-T17), Then it matches and the extractor yields 412.
Given alert_email unset, When terraform plan, Then it errors (required variable).

tickets.title: Terraform: four Cloud Monitoring dashboards
tickets.summary: Dashboards chat, retrieval, events and cost exist as code and together show every 9.2 metric.
tickets.description:
Implements overview.md 9.5: "Dashboards in Cloud Monitoring (one per concern: chat, retrieval, events, cost)". Add terraform/dashboards/*.json and google_monitoring_dashboard resources in terraform/dashboards.tf.
- chat: chat_ttft_ms and chat_total_ms p50/p95 with the SLO lines (3.5 s, 2.0 s, 8 s), gate_refusals_total, guard_blocks_total by guard, llm_fallback_total, llm_breaker_state, answer_cache_hit_ratio, error rate.
- retrieval: retrieval_first_stage_ms and rerank_ms p95 with lines 300 and 700 ms, rerank_fallback_total by reason, rerank_429_total, retrieval_degraded_ratio.
- events: outbox_oldest_age_s, consumer_lag by group, acl_apply_lag_s, dlq_messages_total, default_partition_rows.
- cost: db_connections_in_use against 300, tenant_budget_rejections_total by tenant, Kong prometheus series, billing spend widget.
Each dashboard's metric names come from the registry; Kong prometheus series appear only where exported.
acceptance_criteria: Given the E9-T5 registry, When scripts/check_monitoring_tf.py runs, Then every one of its 19 names appears in at least one dashboard JSON; the check fails if one is missing.
Given terraform validate, When run in CI, Then it passes; given terraform apply to a scratch project in the drill, Then four dashboards are listed by gcloud monitoring dashboards list.
Given the chat dashboard JSON, When parsed, Then threshold lines of 3500, 2000 and 8000 ms exist on the right charts (jq assertions in the check script).
Given the retrieval dashboard JSON, Then threshold lines at 300 and 700 ms exist.

tickets.title: Terraform: availability and latency SLOs with burn-rate alerts
tickets.summary: SLOs for availability (prod only), latency and retrieval exist with multi-window burn-rate alerts whose thresholds are fixed in the ticket.
tickets.description:
Implements overview.md 9.5 SLO table: availability 99.5% monthly of chat requests not failing, prod profile only; TTFT p95 < 3.5 s (p50 < 2.0 s) and full answer p95 < 8 s on demo and prod; retrieval first stage p95 < 300 ms, rerank p95 < 700 ms on both. "Windows and thresholds set in E9."
Add google_monitoring_slo resources in terraform/slo.tf over a custom service for chat-api. Availability SLO created only when env_profile == "prod" (count). Burn-rate alert policies: fast (1 h window with 5 min lookback, burn rate 14.4) and slow (6 h window with 30 min lookback, burn rate 6), the standard multi-window values for a 99.5% target; record the choice and the budget (0.5% of a 30-day window = about 3.6 h) in docs/runbooks/slo.md. A chat request fails when the response is HTTP 5xx or the SSE stream ends with an error event other than the intended refusals/4xx codes; define the good/total filter in the doc.
Out of scope: other alerts.
Burn-rate numbers fixed by R72: 14.4x over 1 h and 6x over 6 h.
acceptance_criteria: Given env_profile=prod, When terraform plan, Then one availability SLO with goal 0.995 and rolling 30-day period and two burn-rate alert policies are planned; given env_profile=demo, Then the availability SLO and its alerts are absent and the latency SLOs remain (CI plan assertions through terraform show -json).
Given the plan JSON, When checked, Then the latency SLO thresholds are 3500 ms (p95), 2000 ms (p50), 8000 ms and retrieval 300 and 700 ms.
Given docs/runbooks/slo.md, When reviewed, Then it states the two windows, burn rates 14.4 and 6, and the failing-request definition (checked by a presence test in scripts/check_monitoring_tf.py).
Given the drill in E9-T17 injects a 20% error rate for 10 min in a scratch prod-profile project, Then the fast burn alert opens.

tickets.title: Terraform: chat and retrieval alert policies
tickets.summary: Alert policies exist for degraded turns, rerank 429, LLM fallback, readiness failing and model retirement.
tickets.description:
Implements these alerts from overview.md 9.5: "degraded turns > 5% in 15 min, rerank 429 > 0, LLM fallback in use, readiness failing, model retirement soon".
Add terraform/alerts_chat.tf with google_monitoring_alert_policy resources using the E9-T11 notification channel:
- degraded_turns: retrieval_degraded_ratio > 0.05 over a 15 min window.
- rerank_429: rate of rerank_429_total > 0 over 5 min.
- llm_fallback_in_use: llm_fallback_total increase > 0 over 5 min.
- readiness_failing: readiness_failing = 1 for 3 min (metric from E9-T8).
- model_retirement_soon: model_retirement_days (gauge, R74) < 30 for 5 min; the alert is on the gauge, not a log line.
Thresholds are tfvars with these defaults.
acceptance_criteria: Given terraform plan, When listed, Then five policies exist with the names above (terraform show -json assertion in scripts/check_monitoring_tf.py).
Given the degraded_turns policy JSON, Then threshold 0.05 and duration 900 s.
Given the E9-T17 drill emits rerank_429_total=1, When 5 minutes pass, Then the rerank_429 incident opens (drill record in docs/runbooks/alert-drills.md).
Given the drill stops /readyz (DB role flag changed), Then readiness_failing opens within 5 minutes.
Given the policy JSON for model_retirement_soon, Then its condition metric is model_retirement_days with threshold 30 and comparison LT (script assertion); no log-based metric is used for it.

tickets.title: Terraform: event pipeline and partition alert policies
tickets.summary: Alert policies exist for outbox age, ACL applier lag, consumer lag, DLQ non-empty and non-empty DEFAULT partitions.
tickets.description:
Implements from overview.md 9.5: "outbox oldest age, ACL applier lag, consumer lag, DLQ non-empty, DEFAULT partition non-empty". Add terraform/alerts_events.tf using the E9-T11 channel. Thresholds fixed by resolution R72, overridable in tfvars:
- outbox_age: outbox_oldest_age_s > 300 for 5 min.
- acl_lag: acl_apply_lag_s > 120 (the principal cache TTL is 60 s, 6.1) for 5 min.
- consumer_lag: consumer_lag{group} > 1000 for 10 min.
- dlq_non_empty: increase of dlq_messages_total > 0 over 5 min.
- default_partition_non_empty: default_partition_rows > 0 over a 30 min window (the maintenance job runs every 15 min in demo, R76) (E1-T12 only makes the maintenance job exit non-zero; this is the alert).
acceptance_criteria: Given terraform plan, Then five policies exist with the names above (scripts/check_monitoring_tf.py assertion).
Given the policy for default_partition_non_empty, When parsed, Then the condition metric is default_partition_rows with threshold 0 and comparison GT. Duration/alignment window is 1800 s.

Given the E9-T17 drill inserts one row into a DEFAULT messages partition and runs the maintenance job in a scratch project, Then the incident opens within 45 minutes (30 min window plus one 15 min job run).
Given the drill stops the acl-applier worker and POSTs an ACL change, Then acl_lag opens within 10 minutes.

tickets.title: Terraform: monthly budget alerts on GCP billing and LLM cost
tickets.summary: A billing budget plus an alert on llm_cost_usd_total cover monthly cloud and LLM spend against the $100-200 budget.
tickets.description: Implements overview.md 9.5: "budget alerts on the monthly cloud and LLM spend (thresholds set in E9 against the $100-200 budget)". Add terraform/budget.tf with google_billing_budget for the project: amount var monthly_budget_usd (default 150), notifications at 50%, 90% and 100% of actual spend and 100% forecasted, to the E9-T11 email channel. LLM spend (R73): add a google_monitoring_alert_policy on the cumulative monthly increase of llm_cost_usd_total (sum over provider and model, 30-day rolling window) with thresholds at 90% and 100% of var llm_monthly_budget_usd (default 75; the sum of monthly_budget_usd for cloud and LLM stays inside the $100-200 range, documented in docs/runbooks/slo.md). No manual check.
acceptance_criteria: Given terraform plan, Then one google_billing_budget exists with amount 150 USD and threshold rules 0.5, 0.9, 1.0 (actual) and 1.0 (forecasted) (plan JSON assertion).
Given monthly_budget_usd=250 outside the 100-200 range, When terraform plan, Then a validation block fails with a message naming the range 100-200.
Given billing_account variable unset, Then plan errors.
Given the drill (E9-T17) lowers the budget to $1 in a scratch project, Then a notification arrives on the channel (drill record).

Given the plan JSON, Then an alert policy on llm_cost_usd_total exists with thresholds equal to 0.9 and 1.0 times llm_monthly_budget_usd; in the drill, recording llm_cost_usd_total above that threshold opens the incident.

tickets.title: Alert drill runbook and script
tickets.summary: A script and runbook fire each 9.5 alert in a scratch project and record the result, covering the Done-when drill.
tickets.description:
Implements the Done-when item: "Each alert in overview.md#9.5 fires in a drill (degraded turns > 5% in 15 min, rerank 429, outbox age, ACL applier lag, DEFAULT partition non-empty, readiness failure, budget)". Add scripts/alert_drill.py and docs/runbooks/alert-drills.md. The script takes an alert name, injects the condition (writes the matching log-metric line or metric value for the alert; real fault injection where cheap: stop acl-applier, insert a DEFAULT partition row, flip a role flag for readiness, lower budget), polls the Cloud Monitoring API until an incident opens or a timeout (default 15 min), then clears the condition and reports PASS or FAIL as JSON. Include the burn-rate, LLM fallback, consumer lag, DLQ and model-retirement alerts too. The runbook records the date, result and incident link per alert, and a manual check that the E9-T10 trace appears in Cloud Trace.
Runs only against the scratch project named by a required --project argument and refuses ENV_PROFILE=prod project ids listed in a deny var.
The drill also covers the llm_cost_usd_total budget alert and the model_retirement_days alert; the DEFAULT-partition drill waits up to 45 min.
acceptance_criteria: Given a scratch project with E9-T11 to E9-T16 applied, When python scripts/alert_drill.py --all runs, Then each alert in overview.md 9.5 returns PASS in the JSON and the process exits 0; exit non-zero if any fails.
Given a project where one policy is removed, When the script runs, Then that alert reports FAIL (negative control).
Given --project equals a name in the deny list, Then the script exits 2 without calling any API (unit test).
Given docs/runbooks/alert-drills.md, Then it has a row per alert in 9.5 (presence test in scripts/check_monitoring_tf.py).

tickets.title: Spike: measure Cloud SQL start time and stopped billing
tickets.summary: Measure stopped-to-RUNNABLE time and confirm a stopped instance bills storage only, recorded as an ADR.
tickets.description:
Overview section 10 item 6: the stopped-to-RUNNABLE time of Cloud SQL is undocumented; measure it. Also confirm stopped-instance billing is storage only (ADR-020: 'The idle estimate assumes a stopped instance bills storage only; unverified').

Build: scripts/spikes/cloudsql_start_time.sh that, against a throwaway Cloud SQL PostgreSQL 16 Enterprise 2 vCPU / 8 GiB instance created with gcloud (not Terraform, same size as ADR-020, with ~10 GB of data and private IP via PSC if the E2 VPC exists, otherwise public IP for the throwaway only), runs N=5 cycles of: patch --activation-policy=NEVER, wait STOPPED, patch --activation-policy=ALWAYS, record seconds until state RUNNABLE and until a psql SELECT 1 succeeds. Then leave the instance stopped for >= 24 h and read the Cloud Billing export / SKU lines for that instance to confirm only storage (and reserved IP, if any) is billed. Delete the throwaway instance.

Output: docs/adr/cloud-sql-start-time.md with the measured table (per cycle: seconds to RUNNABLE, seconds to first query), min/median/max, the billing finding, and a recommendation for the demo-up wait timeout (used by E10-T18). Context for the researcher: the file is copied into decisions.md later.
Out of scope: the demo-up script itself (E10-T17), Terraform for Cloud SQL (E10-T6).
acceptance_criteria: docs/adr/cloud-sql-start-time.md exists and contains a table with 5 measured cycles (seconds to RUNNABLE and to first SELECT 1), plus min, median and max; a file with fewer than 5 rows fails the check `grep -c '^| [0-9]' docs/adr/cloud-sql-start-time.md` >= 5

The ADR states, with a billing-export SKU list or screenshot reference, whether a stopped instance bills storage only; if any other SKU is billed the ADR gives its monthly amount and the idle estimate delta against the 40-55 USD range
The ADR gives a recommended demo-up wait timeout equal to the max measured start time plus a stated margin
After the spike `gcloud sql instances list` shows no throwaway instance (command output attached in the PR)

tickets.title: Spike: worker pool scale to 0 and Terraform support
tickets.summary: Verify a Cloud Run worker pool can be set to 0 instances and managed by Terraform with ignore_changes, as an ADR.
tickets.description:
ADR-019 and ADR-020 list 'worker pool scale to 0 and its Terraform support' as unverified. Verify with a minimal worker pool using the chosen Google provider version from stack.md.

Build: a throwaway Terraform config under scripts/spikes/worker_pool/ that creates a Cloud Run worker pool (google_cloud_run_v2_worker_pool) from a hello-world image with manual_instance_count = 1 and lifecycle.ignore_changes = [scaling[0].manual_instance_count] (check the real attribute path), then: (a) set count to 0 with `gcloud run worker-pools update --scaling` or the documented equivalent and confirm 0 instances run and no billing for idle; (b) run `terraform plan` and confirm no diff; (c) scale back to 2 and plan again; (d) record the exact gcloud command the demo scripts must use.

Output: docs/adr/worker-pool-scale-to-zero.md with commands, provider version, plan outputs, and the result. If scale to 0 or the Terraform resource is not supported, the ADR states the fallback (for example min instance count semantics or deleting/recreating the pool) and that the fallback must be raised as a question before E10-T9.
Out of scope: the real fa-worker pool (E10-T9).

Out of scope: demo-up (E10-T18); demo-ttl job (E10-T19).

`terraform plan -detailed-exitcode` returns 0 after demo-down

tickets.title: Implement demo-prewarm Cloud Run job
tickets.summary: Add the in-VPC demo-prewarm job code that calls /readyz and warms pools, since it cannot run from the laptop.
tickets.description:
4.8: `demo-prewarm`, DB role none: 'Runs inside the VPC after demo-up: calls /readyz and warms pools and caches (not run from the operator laptop)'. Job entrypoint `jobs` in the one image. Look at the existing jobs entrypoint dispatcher from E1 to add the subcommand `demo-prewarm`.

Build backend/src/.../jobs/demo_prewarm.py: reads the internal chat-api URL, gets an ID token from the metadata server (audience = chat-api URL), polls /readyz up to a configured timeout (default 120 s, interval 5 s), then issues a small number of warm requests to bring connection pools up (use the readiness endpoint repeatedly with the concurrency equal to a fraction of DB_POOL_SIZE; no LLM calls, no data writes). Exit 0 only when /readyz returns 200; exit non-zero with the last response body otherwise. No DB credentials.

Out of scope: demo-up (E10-T18).
acceptance_criteria: Unit test with a fake HTTP server: returns 503 twice then 200 -> job exits 0 after 3 polls; always 503 -> exits non-zero after the timeout (fake clock)
Unit test: the job never reads DB_* variables and never calls an endpoint other than /readyz (assert on recorded requests)
`gcloud run jobs execute demo-prewarm --wait` after demo-up exits 0 and its logs show the poll count; output attached

tickets.title: Implement demo-up script, Valkey lifecycle and make demo-up
tickets.summary: Start the demo in the exact reverse order, create Valkey, redeploy Kong with its endpoint and print the measured start time.
tickets.description:
Flow 5 and ADR-020 (up is exactly the reverse, D16.13): (1) Cloud SQL activation policy ALWAYS and wait RUNNABLE (record elapsed seconds; wait timeout from docs/adr/cloud-sql-start-time.md of E10-T1), (2) create the Memorystore Valkey instance (shared-core-nano, fixed name from `VALKEY_INSTANCE_NAME`, in the E2 VPC, outside Terraform state; 4.6), (3) deploy a new fa-gateway (Kong) revision with the Valkey endpoint in an environment variable and raise chat-api and fa-gateway min instances (fa-gateway max 2 per 7.2), (4) worker pool manual instance count up (command from E10-T2), (5) resume Scheduler triggers, (6) run `maintenance` then `demo-prewarm` jobs (inside the VPC) and wait for success, (7) print the URL and the measured Cloud SQL start time. Remaining outbox rows from a forced down are delivered by the relay automatically after step 4; log the count at start.

Build scripts/demo/demo_up.py reusing scripts/demo/common.py (E10-T16) and `make demo-up`. Which env var name Kong reads for the Valkey endpoint comes from the E2 Kong config (check kong/ and the E2 fa-gateway module; if not defined, add to questions). Idempotent and rerunnable; the Valkey step succeeds if the instance already exists and is READY.

Out of scope: demo-prewarm job code (E10-T17), demo-ttl (E10-T19).
acceptance_criteria: Unit test with fake clients: the call order is exactly sql=ALWAYS, valkey create, gateway revision with the Valkey endpoint env, min instances up, worker up, scheduler resume, run maintenance, run demo-prewarm; a reversed order fails the test
Unit test: the script exits non-zero and skips the later steps if Cloud SQL is not RUNNABLE within the timeout
On the real project after `make demo-down` then `make demo-up`: `/readyz` through the ALB returns 200 and the script's last output line contains `cloud_sql_start_seconds=<number>`; output attached

The Kong revision created by demo-up has the Valkey host in its env (`gcloud run services describe fa-gateway` shows it) and a request burst over RATE_LIMIT_CHAT_PER_MIN gets 429 (counter stored in Valkey)
`terraform plan -detailed-exitcode` returns 0 after demo-up

tickets.title: Implement demo-ttl job to bring a forgotten demo down
tickets.summary: Add the hourly demo-ttl job that runs demo-down when the demo has been up longer than DEMO_TTL_HOURS.
tickets.description:
4.8: `demo-ttl`, role `fa_maint`: 'Hourly safety net: reads the outbox count and runs demo-down if the demo has been up longer than DEMO_TTL_HOURS (Cloud Run admin SA rights)'. ADR-020: 'An hourly demo-ttl job auto-downs the demo as a safety net.' The job must run the same logic as scripts/demo/demo_down.py (E10-T16), so package the demo scripts into the image under the jobs entrypoint rather than duplicating them.

Build jobs subcommand `demo-ttl`: determine 'up since' from the Cloud SQL activation transition (the time of the last operation START/patch ALWAYS from the Cloud SQL operations API) and from a label `demo_up_at` that demo-up sets on the Cloud SQL instance (add the label write to demo_up.py as part of this ticket's PR); if Cloud SQL is stopped do nothing (exit 0, log 'already down'); if now - up_since > DEMO_TTL_HOURS, read the outbox count (query as fa_maint, count of rows with published_at is null) and call the demo-down routine with the 10-minute drain; log the outbox count read. Value of DEMO_TTL_HOURS is set by this ticket via the Terraform variable default (4; see questions).

Out of scope: changing the drain order.
acceptance_criteria: Unit test with fake clients: up for 5 h and DEMO_TTL_HOURS=4 -> demo-down routine called once; up for 1 h -> not called; stopped instance -> not called and exit 0
Integration test against a Postgres container: the outbox count query runs as fa_maint and returns the number of unpublished rows seeded (3)

On the real project, after demo-up and temporarily setting DEMO_TTL_HOURS=0, `gcloud scheduler jobs run demo-ttl` results in Cloud SQL activation policy NEVER within 15 minutes (drain included); output attached
The job fails the check if its SA has roles/owner or roles/editor (E10-T10 IAM test still passes)

tickets.title: Add security and connection budget invariant checks
tickets.summary: Add a scripted check for no allUsers, invoker exception only on fa-gateway, no public Cloud SQL IP, no secret in state and pool sizes <= 300.
tickets.description:
Epic done-when: 'No allUsers binding on any service; the invoker check is disabled only on fa-gateway; Cloud SQL has no public IP; no secret value in Terraform state; the sum of pool sizes over max instances is <= 300.' Sources: 6.6 DB_POOL_SIZE ('pool per instance x max instances over all services must stay <= 300 of Cloud SQL max_connections 400'), 7.2 connection budget (`max_connections` 400, headroom for migrations, dbt and Dagster; fa-gateway max 2), 8.3, 8.4 (G-27), ADR-012.

Build scripts/check_invariants.py with two modes: `--plan plan.json` (static, from `terraform show -json`) and `--live` (gcloud). Checks: (1) no allUsers/allAuthenticatedUsers in any run service, job, worker pool or bucket policy; (2) invoker check disabled (`invokerIamDisabled`) on fa-gateway only, enabled on every other service; (3) Cloud SQL ipv4_enabled false and no PRIMARY/PUBLIC address; (4) state/plan values: no sensitive attribute from google_secret_manager_secret_version or any value matching a configured secret-name list; (5) budget: sum over services/pools of DB_POOL_SIZE x max_instance_count (chat-api, worker pool count, jobs max parallelism x pool) <= 300, printing the table and failing above. Run in CI (terraform-plan workflow) and by `make check-invariants`.

Out of scope: runtime load.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests with fixture plan JSON: one with allUsers on chat-api fails (exit 1); one with invokerIamDisabled on chat-api fails; one with ipv4_enabled true fails; clean fixture passes
Unit test: DB_POOL_SIZE=10, chat-api max 20, worker 2 x 10 = 220 passes; chat-api max 40 (total 420) fails with the table printed
Unit test: a fixture plan containing a google_secret_manager_secret_version with secret_data fails
`make check-invariants --live` on the real project exits 0 with the printed budget total <= 300; output attached
The terraform-plan workflow runs the check on PRs and fails when a fixture violation is introduced on a test branch

tickets.title: Verify no Terraform drift across a down and up cycle
tickets.summary: Run demo-down then demo-up and assert terraform plan is clean at every stage.
tickets.description:
Epic done-when: '`terraform plan` is clean (no drift) after a down / up cycle thanks to `ignore_changes`.' 4.14: Terraform uses lifecycle.ignore_changes on activation_policy, min_instance_count and manual_instance_count. Add scripts/demo/drift_check.sh and a make target `make demo-cycle-test`: apply, `terraform plan -detailed-exitcode`, demo-down, plan, demo-up, plan, each must return exit code 0; also confirm the end state of demo-down (SQL NEVER, worker 0, min 0, Valkey absent) and demo-up (`/readyz` 200).

If a plan shows drift on an attribute (for example the Scheduler paused state, a Cloud Run revision template field, or the Kong environment variable set by demo-up), fix it by adding a narrowly scoped ignore_changes in the owning Terraform file and list it in the PR; record each added attribute in questions if it is not one of the three the arch names. The Kong Valkey env var set by demo-up is the most likely candidate (E2 owns the module; make the minimal change there).
acceptance_criteria: `make demo-cycle-test` exits 0; the log shows three `terraform plan -detailed-exitcode` results all equal to 0 (after apply, after demo-down, after demo-up)

The test asserts the post-down state: Cloud SQL activation policy NEVER, worker pool count 0, chat-api and fa-gateway min 0, `gcloud redis`/memorystore instance absent; it fails if any is wrong (negative run with a stubbed non-zero worker count fails)
The test asserts the post-up state: `/readyz` through the ALB returns 200; and the job logs the measured start time

tickets.title: Load test with stub LLM at 10 QPS against synthetic corpus
tickets.summary: Run a 10 QPS peak load test with a stub LLM and report p95 against the overview 2.1 targets excluding LLM time.
tickets.description:
Epic done-when: 'A load test with a stub LLM runs at ~10 QPS peak and reports the p95 targets of overview 2.1 (excluding LLM time) against the 10k-chunk synthetic corpus numbers (fail if above).' Targets (2.1): retrieval first stage (embed + hybrid SQL) p95 < 300 ms, rerank p95 < 700 ms, TTFT p50 < 2.0 s / p95 < 3.5 s, full answer p95 < 8 s, all excluding LLM time (the stub returns a fixed streamed answer after a configured delay that is subtracted from the report). 7.2 and 4.6/rerank notes: Voyage Tier 1 allows ~5 QPS of rerank, so request the tier upgrade before the run (record in the PR) or run with the rerank step stubbed and state which was used.

Build load/ (k6 or Locust; pick the one already in stack.md, else k6) with a scenario that ramps to 10 QPS against the real ALB URL with a test tenant token, a stub LLM selected by a config setting on the deployed revision (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL pointing at a stub Cloud Run service or the Kong egress route replaced by the stub; the stub service is deployed only for the test, internal, not allUsers), reads per-stage timings from the metrics/traces defined in section 9, and writes docs/adr/load-test-results.md with p50/p95 for each metric, DB connection count peak (must stay below the budget of E10-T20), error rate, and pass/fail per target. Corpus: the 10k-chunk synthetic corpus from E3/E6 numbers. Use the `prod`-profile HA flag only if the report states it. Out of scope: tuning (record findings only).
acceptance_criteria: `make load-test` runs 10 QPS at peak for at least 5 minutes against the demo environment and exits non-zero if any p95 target of 2.1 (retrieval 300 ms, rerank 700 ms, TTFT p95 3.5 s, full answer p95 8 s, LLM time excluded) is exceeded
docs/adr/load-test-results.md contains the measured p50/p95 for each target, the peak Cloud SQL connection count and the error rate; peak connections < 300 asserted in the script
Rerank 429 counter (`rerank_429_total`) and `rerank_fallback_total` are reported; the run fails if degraded turns exceed 5% of turns
The stub LLM service has no allUsers binding and is removed after the test (`gcloud run services list` has no stub)
